choices.text: Every employee at Harbor Drug is required to complete thirty hours of continuing education annually.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every Harbor Drug employee whose nametag reads 'RPh' is required to complete thirty hours of continuing education annually.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most licensed pharmacists in the province work at Harbor Drug.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any employee who completes thirty hours of continuing education is a licensed pharmacist.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The province requires more continuing education of pharmacists than of other medical professionals.

explanations.correct: Every 'RPh' employee is a licensed pharmacist, and every licensed pharmacist must complete thirty hours of continuing education. By transitivity, every 'RPh' employee has the same requirement.
explanations.A: Too strong — the stimulus only places the 'RPh' employees in the pharmacist category, not all Harbor Drug staff.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Not supported — the stimulus says nothing about the share of the province's pharmacists that Harbor Drug employs.
explanations.D: Reversal — completing the education is necessary for licensure, not sufficient for it.
explanations.E: Out of scope — the stimulus says nothing about requirements for other medical professionals.

lr.difficultyReason: Single conditional plus a factual assertion about one individual; the credited inference is a straightforward modus ponens.
lr.stimulus: If a cargo container at the port weighs more than eight metric tons, it must be inspected by a customs officer before release. The blue container that arrived on Tuesday's shipment weighs nine metric tons.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true if the statements above are true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No container lighter than eight metric tons is inspected by a customs officer.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every container on Tuesday's shipment weighs more than eight metric tons.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The blue container must be inspected by a customs officer before it is released.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The blue container will not be released on Tuesday.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most containers at the port weigh more than eight metric tons.

explanations.correct: The conditional's antecedent is satisfied — the container weighs more than eight metric tons — so its consequent applies: it must be inspected before release.
explanations.A: Negation error — the rule says nothing about whether lighter containers are inspected.
explanations.B: Unsupported generalization — only the blue container's weight is given.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Unsupported — the timing of release is not addressed by the stimulus.
explanations.E: Out of scope — the stimulus gives no information about the weight distribution at the port.

lr.difficultyReason: Two facts about two overlapping groups support a single existential inference; the logical step is one application of the pigeonhole-style overlap.
lr.stimulus: Every student in Professor Halden's seminar has read Kant's Groundwork. At least one student in Professor Halden's seminar has never studied philosophy formally before.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most students who read Kant's Groundwork have studied philosophy formally before.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At least one person who has read Kant's Groundwork has never studied philosophy formally before.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Professor Halden requires every student to read Kant's Groundwork.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every student who has read Kant's Groundwork has never studied philosophy formally before.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Anyone who has studied philosophy formally has read Kant's Groundwork.

explanations.correct: The philosophy-novice student in the seminar has read the Groundwork, because every student in the seminar has. That student is a person who has read the Groundwork and has not studied philosophy formally before.
explanations.A: Unsupported — the stimulus provides no information about students outside this seminar.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Causal inference beyond the text — requiring isn't stated, only that each has read it.
explanations.D: Too strong — 'every' student reads it, but only 'at least one' is a newcomer.
explanations.E: Reversal and scope shift — the stimulus concerns seminar readers, not all formal philosophy students.

lr.difficultyReason: A conditional plus the denial of its consequent invites a single-step contrapositive inference.
lr.stimulus: If the township's general fund finishes the year with a surplus, the library's evening hours will be extended in January. The township's council has just confirmed that the library's evening hours will not be extended in January.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The township's general fund did not finish the year with a surplus.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The township's general fund finished the year with a deficit of a significant size.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The council opposes extending the library's evening hours under any circumstances.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The library will extend its evening hours later in the year instead of in January.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Any future surplus will be used to extend the library's hours.

explanations.correct: By contrapositive: if a surplus would guarantee extended hours and extended hours will not happen, then there was no surplus.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Too strong — absence of a surplus does not entail a deficit, let alone a significant one.
explanations.C: Unsupported — the council's general stance on library hours is not stated.
explanations.D: Unsupported — the stimulus says nothing about later in the year.
explanations.E: Unsupported — no claim is made about future surpluses.

lr.difficultyReason: A short conditional chain with two links collapses into a single transitive conclusion.
lr.stimulus: Whenever the coastal radar records a squall line moving east faster than forty kilometers per hour, the harbor office issues a small-craft warning. Whenever the harbor office issues a small-craft warning, the fishing fleet at Port Alden remains in dock.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The fishing fleet at Port Alden remains in dock only when a small-craft warning is in effect.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Whenever the coastal radar records a squall line moving east faster than forty kilometers per hour, the fishing fleet at Port Alden remains in dock.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The coastal radar records squall lines more often in winter than in summer.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whenever the fishing fleet at Port Alden is in dock, the coastal radar has recorded a fast-moving squall line.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Small-craft warnings cause squall lines to intensify.

explanations.correct: Chaining the two conditionals: fast east-moving squall line -> small-craft warning -> fleet in dock. So any fast east-moving squall line entails the fleet's being in dock.
explanations.A: Reversal — the stimulus gives a sufficient condition for the fleet's staying in dock, not a necessary one.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Out of scope — seasonal frequency is not addressed.
explanations.D: Reversal — the fleet could remain in dock for other reasons.
explanations.E: Causal overreach — the stimulus describes procedural responses, not atmospheric causation.

lr.difficultyReason: Two numerical statements about exhaustive and overlapping groups support a minimal-count inference via a pigeonhole-style argument.
lr.stimulus: Forty employees work at the Linden branch of Cresta Bank. Every employee at the Linden branch is either a teller or a loan officer, and some are both. Eighteen of the branch's employees are tellers, and twenty-nine are loan officers.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: More than half of the branch's employees are tellers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At least seven employees at the branch are both tellers and loan officers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Exactly three employees are only loan officers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No employee at the branch is only a teller.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The branch employs more loan officers than it would if it had fewer tellers.

explanations.correct: Eighteen plus twenty-nine equals forty-seven role-slots filled by only forty employees. Since everyone fills at least one role, the seven-slot surplus must come from employees who hold both roles. So at least seven employees are both.
explanations.A: Contradicts the stimulus — only eighteen of the forty employees are tellers, less than half.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Unsupported as exact — the count of loan-officer-only employees depends on the overlap, which need not equal three.
explanations.D: Unsupported — the stimulus permits, but does not require, the existence of teller-only employees.
explanations.E: Out of scope — the stimulus makes no counterfactual comparison.

lr.difficultyReason: A rule plus a specific labeling fact produce a one-step categorical inference.
lr.stimulus: Any package labeled 'Priority Express' by the Northern Postal Service is guaranteed delivery within two business days. The parcel that Arun mailed to Ines yesterday afternoon was labeled 'Priority Express' by the Northern Postal Service.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ines will receive Arun's parcel within two business days of yesterday afternoon.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Arun's parcel is guaranteed delivery within two business days.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No parcel not labeled 'Priority Express' is delivered within two business days.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Northern Postal Service only guarantees delivery for 'Priority Express' parcels.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Arun paid more to mail the parcel as 'Priority Express' than he would have for standard service.

explanations.correct: Arun's parcel belongs to the class of 'Priority Express' items, and every such item is guaranteed delivery within two business days. Therefore his parcel carries that guarantee.
explanations.A: Shift from guarantee to actual delivery — guarantees can fail in individual cases; the stimulus only asserts the guarantee.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Negation error — the stimulus does not rule out quick delivery of other parcels.
explanations.D: Scope shift — 'only' is not supported; other services may also carry guarantees.
explanations.E: Out of scope — pricing is not mentioned.

lr.difficultyReason: A disjunction combined with the denial of one disjunct yields a one-step disjunctive syllogism.
lr.stimulus: The winning entry in this year's Veldt Short Fiction Prize was submitted either by a novelist who has previously published with Veldt or by a first-time contributor. Investigation has revealed that the winning entry was not submitted by any novelist who has previously published with Veldt.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true if the statements above are true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The winning entry was submitted by an author whose work has never appeared in any journal.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The winning entry was submitted by a first-time contributor to Veldt.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most previous Veldt Prize winners were first-time contributors.

choices.label: D
choices.text: First-time contributors produce stronger short fiction than returning contributors do.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The judges preferred to award the prize to a newcomer this year.

explanations.correct: Given the either/or premise and the denial of the first disjunct, the remaining disjunct holds: the winner was a first-time contributor.
explanations.A: Too strong — 'first-time contributor to Veldt' does not entail never having published anywhere else.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Unsupported — past years are not addressed.
explanations.D: Unsupported evaluative claim — the stimulus does not compare quality.
explanations.E: Unsupported — the judges' preferences are not stated.

lr.difficultyReason: Two conditionals chain through a shared middle term to produce a one-step transitive inference about a named individual.
lr.stimulus: Every treaty ratified by the Federal Assembly takes legal effect on the first day of the following month. Every law taking legal effect in the country must be published in the Official Gazette within fourteen days of taking effect. The Saldano Trade Treaty was ratified by the Federal Assembly last week.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Saldano Trade Treaty will be published in the Official Gazette within fourteen days of the first day of next month.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No law takes legal effect without being ratified by the Federal Assembly.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Saldano Trade Treaty was the only treaty ratified by the Federal Assembly last week.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Official Gazette publishes all treaties before they take legal effect.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Any treaty published in the Official Gazette has been ratified by the Federal Assembly.

explanations.correct: The treaty, as a ratified treaty, takes effect on the first of next month; every law taking effect must then appear in the Gazette within fourteen days of that effective date. So publication must occur within fourteen days of the first of next month.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Reversal — the stimulus doesn't exclude other paths to legal effect.
explanations.C: Unsupported — uniqueness is not stated.
explanations.D: Contradicts the stimulus — publication follows, not precedes, legal effect.
explanations.E: Reversal — the stimulus requires Gazette publication for laws, not the converse.

lr.difficultyReason: A rule-plus-exception pattern supports a single-step contrapositive-style inference about a named case.
lr.stimulus: In the Panzar language, every verb that ends in the suffix '-eko' takes its past tense by adding '-ta'. The only exceptions are verbs whose stem ends in a vowel; those instead take '-nta'. The Panzar verb 'sareko' has a stem ending in the consonant 'r'.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The past tense of 'sareko' is formed by adding '-ta'.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most Panzar verbs end in the suffix '-eko'.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No Panzar verb ending in '-eko' has a stem ending in a vowel.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any Panzar verb taking '-nta' in the past tense ends in '-eko'.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The past tense of 'sareko' is 'sareko-nta'.

explanations.correct: 'sareko' ends in '-eko' and its stem ends in a consonant, so it does not fall under the vowel-stem exception. Therefore it follows the default rule: add '-ta'.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Unsupported — the stimulus gives no information about the relative frequency of '-eko' verbs.
explanations.C: Contradicts the stimulus — the exception clause asserts that some '-eko' verbs do have vowel-final stems.
explanations.D: Reversal — '-nta' applies to vowel-stem '-eko' verbs, not uniquely so as far as the stimulus tells us.
explanations.E: Contradicts the inference — 'sareko' has a consonant stem, so it takes '-ta', not '-nta'.

lr.difficultyReason: Two simple categorical facts with one direct deduction. No conditional complexity or multi-step inference required.
lr.stimulus: All mammals are vertebrates. Dogs are mammals.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All vertebrates are mammals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dogs are vertebrates.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some vertebrates are not mammals.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All dogs are carnivores.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Dogs might be vertebrates.

explanations.correct: If all mammals are vertebrates and dogs are mammals, then by transitivity, dogs must be vertebrates.
explanations.A: Reversal trap — the stimulus says all mammals are vertebrates, not all vertebrates are mammals.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: While true in the world, the stimulus does not entail this; it only establishes that all mammals are vertebrates.
explanations.D: The stimulus says nothing about diet or carnivory.
explanations.E: Must-be-true, not could-be-true; 'might' indicates uncertainty where the inference is certain.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple conditional with one clear application. The antecedent is satisfied, so the consequent must follow.
lr.stimulus: If a book is published by a university press, then it has undergone peer review. The novel 'Meridian' was published by Oxford University Press.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All books undergo peer review.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Novels published by university presses are always academic in nature.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 'Meridian' has undergone peer review.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any book that undergoes peer review is published by a university press.

choices.label: E
choices.text: 'Meridian' might have undergone peer review.

explanations.correct: Oxford University Press is a university press. The stimulus says all books published by university presses undergo peer review. Therefore, 'Meridian' must have undergone peer review.
explanations.A: Too broad — the stimulus limits the rule to university press publications only.
explanations.B: The stimulus does not claim all university-press novels are academic.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Reversal of the conditional — the stimulus says university press implies peer review, not the converse.
explanations.E: Must-be-true, not could-be-true; 'might' weakens a certain inference.

lr.difficultyReason: Two factual statements about a specific event. Correct answer directly restates a claim from the stimulus.
lr.stimulus: Last year, the hospital admitted fewer emergency patients than the previous year. Emergency admissions are the hospital's primary revenue source.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The hospital's revenue decreased last year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Emergency admissions account for some portion of the hospital's revenue.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The hospital's emergency department is less efficient than in previous years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fewer people required emergency care last year than the year before.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The hospital will admit fewer emergency patients this year than last year.

explanations.correct: If emergency admissions are the primary revenue source, they must account for some portion (likely a substantial one) of the hospital's revenue. This is directly entailed by the stimulus.
explanations.A: Too strong — fewer patients does not necessarily mean less revenue (prices could have risen).
explanations.C: Efficiency is not mentioned in the stimulus.
explanations.D: This conflates the hospital's admission patterns with the population's need; the stimulus does not establish causation.
explanations.E: Predicts the future based on one year of data; the stimulus does not justify this extrapolation.
explanations.B: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Straightforward numerical fact with one necessary consequence. No inference beyond counting and comparison.
lr.stimulus: The research team consists of five chemists, three biologists, and two physicists. Every member of the team holds a doctoral degree.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every chemist on the research team holds a doctoral degree.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The team has more biologists than physicists.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The research team has ten members in total.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All doctoral degree holders are members of this research team.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Physicists are less qualified than chemists or biologists.

explanations.correct: The stimulus says every member of the team holds a doctoral degree. Chemists are members of the team, so every chemist must hold a doctoral degree.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: True numerically (3 > 2) but this is stated in the stimulus, not inferred; the question asks for what 'must also be true,' implying a deduction beyond restatement. However, it is technically entailed. Still, A is more clearly a logical inference.
explanations.C: True numerically but again, a restatement rather than an inference.
explanations.D: Reversal trap — the stimulus says team members have doctorates, not that all doctorate holders are on this team.
explanations.E: Qualification level is not addressed in the stimulus.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple contrapositive application. The stimulus forbids one property; the correct answer applies the logical contrapositive.
lr.stimulus: No reptiles are warm-blooded. Snakes are reptiles.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All cold-blooded animals are reptiles.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Snakes are not warm-blooded.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some reptiles are cold-blooded.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Warm-blooded animals are not snakes.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If an animal is warm-blooded, it might not be a reptile.

explanations.correct: No reptiles are warm-blooded means reptiles are not warm-blooded. Snakes are reptiles, so snakes are not warm-blooded.
explanations.A: Reversal trap — the stimulus does not say all cold-blooded animals are reptiles.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: While likely true, the stimulus does not affirm that some reptiles are cold-blooded; it only denies they are warm-blooded.
explanations.D: While logically equivalent to B, it is less direct and reverses the subject-predicate structure unnecessarily.
explanations.E: Weakening with 'might' — the inference is certain, not probabilistic.

lr.difficultyReason: Three simple facts about a domain with one direct entailment. No hidden conditional or ambiguity.
lr.stimulus: All sculptures displayed in the museum's main gallery were created by living artists. The marble piece 'Form and Void' is on display in the main gallery. Therefore, 'Form and Void' was created by a living artist.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The museum's main gallery contains only sculptures created by living artists.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All sculptures created by living artists are displayed in the museum's main gallery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The sculptor of 'Form and Void' is still alive.

choices.label: D
choices.text: 'Form and Void' is made of marble.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Living artists create marble sculptures.

explanations.correct: The stimulus already contains a conclusion: 'Form and Void' was created by a living artist. Thus the sculptor is (or was at the time of creation) a living artist, meaning the sculptor is still alive (or was when the work was made—most naturally read as still alive).
explanations.A: Scope issue — the stimulus says all displayed works were created by living artists, not that the gallery contains only sculptures.
explanations.B: Reversal trap — the stimulus does not say all works by living artists are in the main gallery.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Restatement of the stimulus, not a new inference; the question implies deriving something beyond what is stated.
explanations.E: Too broad — the stimulus does not establish that all living artists create marble sculptures.

lr.difficultyReason: Two statements about complementary properties. One clear negation entailment.
lr.stimulus: All citizens are either registered voters or non-citizens. Chen is a citizen.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Chen is a registered voter.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chen is not a non-citizen.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some registered voters are citizens.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If Chen is not a registered voter, then Chen is a non-citizen.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Non-citizens are never citizens.

explanations.correct: Chen is a citizen. The stimulus does not say all citizens are registered voters; it says citizens are either voters or non-citizens. But since Chen is a citizen, Chen cannot be a non-citizen, so Chen is not a non-citizen.
explanations.A: Overreach — the stimulus allows citizens to be either registered voters OR non-citizens, not necessarily voters.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Likely true, but not entailed by the stimulus (we know only that Chen is a citizen, not whether Chen is a registered voter).
explanations.D: This logically follows but rephrases the original statement in a way that does not add new information. B is the cleaner inference.
explanations.E: Definition, not inference from the stimulus.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple factual statement about a policy. Correct answer restates a direct entailment from the stimulus.
lr.stimulus: All employees at the firm must complete annual ethics training. Rajesh is an employee at the firm.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rajesh has already completed ethics training this year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ethics training is the most important professional development at the firm.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rajesh must complete annual ethics training.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Employees who do not complete ethics training are not employed at the firm.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Annual ethics training improves employee conduct.

explanations.correct: The stimulus establishes a universal rule: all employees must complete annual ethics training. Rajesh is an employee. Therefore, Rajesh must complete the training.
explanations.A: Conflates the requirement with its fulfillment; we know Rajesh must complete it, not that Rajesh has done so.
explanations.B: Value judgment not supported by the stimulus.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Contrapositive phrasing of the rule, logically equivalent to C but less direct.
explanations.E: Causal claim not supported by the stimulus.

lr.difficultyReason: Two facts about overlapping sets. Correct answer uses set intersection logic.
lr.stimulus: All organisms that photosynthesize contain chlorophyll. All plants contain chlorophyll. Some plants photosynthesize.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All plants photosynthesize.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some organisms that photosynthesize are plants.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Chlorophyll is only found in plants.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Organisms that do not photosynthesize do not contain chlorophyll.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All organisms that contain chlorophyll photosynthesize.

explanations.correct: The stimulus says some plants photosynthesize. Plants are organisms. Therefore, some organisms that photosynthesize are plants.
explanations.A: The stimulus says 'some plants photosynthesize,' not 'all plants photosynthesize.'
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Overreach — the stimulus does not say chlorophyll is only in plants.
explanations.D: Contrapositive of the first statement leads to: if no chlorophyll, then does not photosynthesize. The stimulus does not entail this direction.
explanations.E: Reversal trap — the stimulus says photosynthesizers have chlorophyll, not that all organisms with chlorophyll photosynthesize.

lr.difficultyReason: Single conditional fact with a negation. One straightforward contrapositive inference.
lr.stimulus: Whenever a contract requires signature by a notary public, the contract is binding. The purchase agreement does not require a notary's signature.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The purchase agreement is not binding.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The purchase agreement might not be binding.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All binding contracts require a notary's signature.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Contracts that do not require a notary's signature are not binding.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It is possible that the purchase agreement is binding for reasons other than notary signature.

explanations.correct: The stimulus says notary-signature is a sufficient condition for binding, not a necessary one. The purchase agreement lacks a notary signature, but this does not prevent it from being binding via other means.
explanations.A: Denying the antecedent fallacy — the stimulus does not say the only way a contract is binding is via notary signature.
explanations.B: Correct conclusion but uses 'might' (uncertainty) where 'must' or 'can' (possibility) is more appropriate.
explanations.C: Reversal trap — the stimulus says notary signature implies binding, not that binding implies notary signature.
explanations.D: Denying the antecedent — again, lack of notary signature does not entail lack of binding.
explanations.E: Correct — the stimulus permits (does not rule out) the purchase agreement being binding through other means.

lr.difficultyReason: Two straightforward facts with one direct logical consequence. The stimulus states all tulips are perennials, and this particular flower is a tulip. The correct answer simply applies the categorical rule to the specific case.
lr.stimulus: All tulips are perennials. The flower that bloomed in the garden last spring is a tulip.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Some perennials bloom in the spring.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The flower that bloomed in the garden last spring is a perennial.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All flowers that bloom in the spring are tulips.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The flower that bloomed in the garden last spring will bloom again next year.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tulips are the most common perennial found in gardens.

explanations.correct: If all tulips are perennials, and the flower in the garden is a tulip, then it must be a perennial. This is a direct application of a universal categorical statement to a specific member.
explanations.A: While this could be true, it is not entailed by the stimulus. We know one tulip bloomed in spring, but this does not entail that some perennials do.
explanations.C: This reverses the logic. The stimulus says all tulips are perennials, not all spring bloomers are tulips.
explanations.D: Perennials return annually, but the stimulus gives no information about whether this particular flower will bloom again.
explanations.E: The stimulus contains no information about the frequency or commonality of tulips.
explanations.B: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple two-fact stimulus with conditional logic. If all members of the board are appointed by the mayor, and Chen is a board member, then Chen must be appointed by the mayor. One-step modus ponens.
lr.stimulus: Everyone who serves on the city planning board is appointed by the mayor. Chen serves on the city planning board.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The mayor appoints everyone who works for the city.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Chen was appointed by the mayor.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All of the mayor's appointees serve on the city planning board.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The mayor's appointment decisions are always made fairly.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No one except the mayor can appoint board members.

explanations.correct: The first statement is a universal conditional: all board members are mayoral appointees. Chen is a board member. Therefore, Chen must be a mayoral appointee.
explanations.A: The stimulus says only that board members are appointed by the mayor, not that the mayor appoints all city workers.
explanations.C: This inverts the conditional. The stimulus does not say that all appointees serve on the board.
explanations.D: The stimulus makes no claim about the fairness or quality of the mayor's decisions.
explanations.E: The stimulus does not exclude other entities from appointing board members; it only states that board members are appointed by the mayor.
explanations.B: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Three simple facts combined to yield one necessary conclusion. Combining sets: all aspirin is analgesic, all analgesics are pain relievers, therefore all aspirin are pain relievers. Transitive chain with one link, straightforward.
lr.stimulus: All aspirin is analgesic medication. All analgesic medication relieves pain. Aspirin was developed in the late nineteenth century.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pain relief was unknown before aspirin was developed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All medication that relieves pain is analgesic.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Aspirin relieves pain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Aspirin is the most widely used pain reliever.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All analgesic medication was developed in the nineteenth century.

explanations.correct: Since all aspirin is analgesic, and all analgesics relieve pain, aspirin must relieve pain. This is a simple transitive chain: aspirin → analgesic → pain relief.
explanations.A: The stimulus says aspirin was developed in the late nineteenth century, not that pain relief did not exist before.
explanations.B: The stimulus tells us analgesics relieve pain, not that all pain relievers are analgesics.
explanations.D: The stimulus contains no comparative claims about the prevalence of aspirin.
explanations.E: The stimulus only establishes that aspirin was developed in the nineteenth century, not all analgesics.
explanations.C: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Straightforward negation and contrapositive. If violating the code results in disciplinary action, and Ms. Wong was not disciplined, then she did not violate the code. Contrapositive of a simple conditional.
lr.stimulus: All employees who violate the employee conduct code are subject to disciplinary action. Ms. Wong was not subject to disciplinary action.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ms. Wong is an exemplary employee.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some employees who do not violate the conduct code are not disciplined.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ms. Wong did not violate the employee conduct code.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Everyone who is not disciplined did not violate the conduct code.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The employee conduct code is strictly enforced.

explanations.correct: By contrapositive: if all violators are disciplined, then anyone not disciplined did not violate. Ms. Wong was not disciplined, so she did not violate the code.
explanations.A: The stimulus provides no information about the overall quality of Ms. Wong's performance.
explanations.B: This may be true, but it is not entailed by the stimulus. We only know about one undisciplined employee.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: This overgeneralizes. While Ms. Wong is not disciplined and did not violate, we cannot infer that all non-disciplined people did not violate (there may be gaps in enforcement).
explanations.E: The stimulus provides no information about enforcement rigor.

lr.difficultyReason: Two facts with a simple logical intersection. If only English majors can take the advanced seminar, and Marcus is enrolled in it, then Marcus must be an English major. Direct application of a rule to a specific case.
lr.stimulus: Only English majors are permitted to enroll in the advanced literature seminar. Marcus is enrolled in the advanced literature seminar.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Marcus will graduate with an English degree.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All English majors are enrolled in the advanced literature seminar.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Marcus is an English major.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The advanced literature seminar is taught by the English department.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No student with a double major can enroll in the advanced literature seminar.

explanations.correct: Only English majors can take the seminar. Marcus is in the seminar. Therefore, Marcus must be an English major.
explanations.A: Enrollment in one advanced seminar does not guarantee graduation with that major.
explanations.B: The stimulus says only English majors can enroll, not that all English majors do enroll.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: The stimulus provides no information about which department teaches the course.
explanations.E: The stimulus places no restriction on double majors.

lr.difficultyReason: Two separate negative facts with no logical bridge between them. While each fact is true, neither entails anything about the other. One-step recognition that the stimulus does not support the conclusion.
lr.stimulus: No mammals are reptiles. No birds are reptiles.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All birds are mammals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No mammals are birds.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some animals that are not reptiles are either mammals or birds.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mammals and birds belong to the same biological family.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reptiles exist in nature.

explanations.correct: We know that mammals are not reptiles and birds are not reptiles. This means there exist animals (both mammals and birds) that are not reptiles. Choice C simply states this necessary conclusion in hedged language.
explanations.A: The stimulus does not connect birds and mammals; knowing they are both non-reptiles does not make all birds mammals.
explanations.B: Mammals and birds are not reptiles, but that does not preclude their overlap.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: The stimulus provides no information about biological classification beyond reptile status.
explanations.E: The stimulus only makes claims about which animals are not reptiles; it does not entail that reptiles exist.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple categorical fact: all members of a defined group share a property. If all board members have voting rights, and Rodriguez is a board member, then Rodriguez has voting rights. One-step modus ponens.
lr.stimulus: All members of the corporate board have voting rights in shareholder meetings. Rodriguez is a member of the corporate board.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rodriguez is a shareholder.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rodriguez has voting rights in shareholder meetings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Shareholders are members of the corporate board.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All shareholders have voting rights.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rodriguez's voting rights are greater than those of other board members.

explanations.correct: All board members have voting rights. Rodriguez is a board member. Therefore, Rodriguez must have voting rights.
explanations.A: The stimulus says board members have voting rights; it does not equate board members with shareholders.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: This reverses the relationship. Board members have voting rights in shareholder meetings, but the stimulus does not make them shareholders.
explanations.D: The stimulus only addresses board members, not all shareholders.
explanations.E: The stimulus provides no comparative information about voting power among board members.

lr.difficultyReason: Three facts: a universal rule, a specific instance, and a temporal fact. Combining the rule with the instance yields the necessary inference. The temporal fact is incidental noise.
lr.stimulus: All marine vessels registered in this port must comply with the new safety standards. The ferry that operates between the two islands is registered in this port. The safety standards were enacted last year.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The ferry began operating after the safety standards were enacted.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The ferry must comply with the new safety standards.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All ferries must comply with the new safety standards.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The safety standards have improved ferry transportation between the islands.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No vessel that was not registered in this port needs to comply with the standards.

explanations.correct: All vessels registered in the port must comply. The ferry is registered in the port. Therefore, the ferry must comply with the new safety standards.
explanations.A: The stimulus only says when the standards were enacted, not when the ferry began operating.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Only vessels registered in this particular port must comply; the stimulus does not address all ferries generally.
explanations.D: The stimulus provides no information about the efficacy or impact of the standards.
explanations.E: The stimulus addresses only vessels in this port; it does not restrict vessels outside the port.

lr.difficultyReason: Two straightforward facts: all members of a defined linguistic group use a certain feature, and a specific person is a member. Therefore, that person must use the feature. One-step categorical inference.
lr.stimulus: All speakers of the Mandarin dialect in this region use a distinctive tone pattern. Professor Liu is a speaker of the Mandarin dialect in this region.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Anyone who uses a distinctive tone pattern speaks the Mandarin dialect.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Professor Liu uses a distinctive tone pattern.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Mandarin dialect is the most common dialect in the region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All tone patterns are distinctive.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Professor Liu has lived in the region her entire life.

explanations.correct: All speakers of the regional Mandarin dialect use this tone pattern. Professor Liu speaks it. Therefore, Professor Liu must use the tone pattern.
explanations.A: The stimulus says all Mandarin speakers use the pattern, not that only Mandarin speakers use it.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: The stimulus provides no information about the prevalence or commonality of the dialect.
explanations.D: The stimulus discusses only the tone pattern used by Mandarin speakers in the region.
explanations.E: The stimulus provides no biographical information about Professor Liu.

lr.difficultyReason: Three facts: a universal principle, a specific case, and a time reference. Applying the principle to the case yields one necessary inference. The time reference provides context but does not prevent the inference.
lr.stimulus: Every artwork displayed in the museum's permanent collection has been authenticated by the chief curator. The portrait in the East Wing is displayed in the museum's permanent collection. The portrait was donated to the museum five years ago.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The portrait was authenticated by the chief curator.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The chief curator examined the portrait five years ago.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All donated artworks are displayed in the permanent collection.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The portrait is more valuable than other artworks in the East Wing.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The chief curator authenticates every artwork the museum acquires.

explanations.correct: Every artwork in the permanent collection has been authenticated by the chief curator. The portrait is in the permanent collection. Therefore, the portrait must have been authenticated by the chief curator.
explanations.B: The portrait was donated five years ago, but we do not know when it was authenticated—it could have been before or after.
explanations.C: The stimulus tells us the portrait is displayed and was donated, but this does not entail that all donations are displayed.
explanations.D: The stimulus provides no comparative value information.
explanations.E: The stimulus addresses artworks in the permanent collection, not all acquisitions.
explanations.A: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple two-premise fact stack with a straightforward categorical inference. No nested conditionals or contrapositives required.
lr.stimulus: All members of the orchestra play at least one wind instrument. Sarah is a member of the orchestra.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sarah plays only wind instruments.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sarah plays at least one wind instrument.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All wind instrument players are members of the orchestra.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Sarah is the best wind instrument player in the orchestra.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most members of the orchestra play wind instruments.

explanations.correct: If all orchestra members play at least one wind instrument, and Sarah is an orchestra member, then Sarah must play at least one wind instrument. This follows directly from the premises.
explanations.A: Overreach — the stimulus says 'at least one,' not 'only' wind instruments. Sarah may play other instruments too.
explanations.B: Correct — logically entailed by the two premises.
explanations.C: Reversal — the stimulus says all orchestra members play wind instruments, not that all wind players are orchestra members.
explanations.D: No information in the stimulus supports any claim about quality or rank.
explanations.E: The stimulus says 'all' orchestra members play wind instruments, not just 'most'.

lr.difficultyReason: Three straightforward declarative facts about a specific event. The correct answer is a simple conjunction of two facts stated in the stimulus.
lr.stimulus: The Rosetta Stone was discovered in Egypt in 1799. The stone contains inscriptions in three languages. Scholars used these inscriptions to decode ancient Egyptian hieroglyphics.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Rosetta Stone is the only artifact ever found that contains multiple languages.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inscriptions in three languages were found on an artifact discovered in Egypt in 1799.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphics could not have been decoded before the Rosetta Stone was discovered.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All artifacts discovered in Egypt contain inscriptions in multiple languages.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The three languages on the Rosetta Stone were all spoken in ancient Egypt.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states (1) the Rosetta Stone was discovered in Egypt in 1799, and (2) the stone contains inscriptions in three languages. Combining these two facts yields that inscriptions in three languages were found on an artifact discovered in Egypt in 1799.
explanations.A: Too strong — the stimulus does not say the stone is 'the only' such artifact.
explanations.B: Correct — direct conjunction of facts 1 and 2.
explanations.C: Contradicted by scope — the stimulus says scholars used the stone to decode hieroglyphics, not that it was the only possible means.
explanations.D: Overreach — the stimulus mentions one artifact; no generalization to 'all' artifacts is supported.
explanations.E: Beyond scope — the stimulus does not specify which languages they were or where they were spoken.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires chaining a universal conditional with an existential claim and applying the contrapositive. Trap (A) inverts the conditional; trap (D) converts 'some' into 'most.'
lr.stimulus: Every drug that has received expedited regulatory review in the past decade has been developed by a company with in-house clinical trial capacity. Some drugs developed by companies with in-house clinical trial capacity have later been withdrawn from the market because of safety concerns. No drug that was developed exclusively by an outside contract research organization has received expedited review.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any drug developed by a company with in-house clinical trial capacity has received expedited regulatory review.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most drugs that have received expedited regulatory review have been withdrawn from the market because of safety concerns.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At least some drugs developed by companies with in-house clinical trial capacity have been withdrawn from the market because of safety concerns.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most drugs developed exclusively by outside contract research organizations have been withdrawn from the market.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No drug that has been withdrawn for safety concerns has received expedited regulatory review.

explanations.correct: The second sentence states directly that some drugs developed by companies with in-house trial capacity have been withdrawn for safety concerns. (C) simply restates that existential claim using the hedged 'at least some,' which follows trivially.
explanations.A: Inverts the conditional. 'Every expedited drug has in-house capacity' does not entail that every in-house drug received expedited review.
explanations.B: Collapses 'some' into 'most.' The stimulus supports only that some withdrawals came from in-house developers, not that most expedited drugs were withdrawn.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Out of scope and overreaching — the stimulus says nothing about the fate of drugs developed exclusively by contract research organizations.
explanations.E: Could be true but not must. Some in-house-developed expedited drugs may have been withdrawn for safety reasons; the passage does not preclude that.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires chaining two conditionals and applying the contrapositive of the second. Trap (B) is the converse error; trap (E) overreaches to a universal.
lr.stimulus: All of the paintings in the Harwell Gallery's permanent collection were acquired before 1950. Any painting acquired before 1950 that has been exhibited in the last ten years has undergone conservation treatment. The gallery's painting 'Marsh at Dusk' has not undergone conservation treatment. 'Marsh at Dusk' is part of the gallery's permanent collection.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: 'Marsh at Dusk' has not been exhibited in the last ten years.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Any painting in the gallery's permanent collection that has undergone conservation treatment has been exhibited in the last ten years.

choices.label: C
choices.text: 'Marsh at Dusk' was acquired after 1950.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most paintings in the permanent collection have been exhibited in the last ten years.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Every painting acquired before 1950 has undergone conservation treatment.

explanations.correct: Because 'Marsh at Dusk' is in the permanent collection, it was acquired before 1950. The conditional then says any such painting that has been exhibited in the last ten years has been conserved. By contrapositive, a pre-1950 painting that has not been conserved has not been exhibited in the last ten years. That applies to 'Marsh at Dusk.'
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Inverts the conditional. The rule goes from 'exhibited' to 'conserved,' not the other way.
explanations.C: Contradicted by the stimulus — permanent-collection paintings were all acquired before 1950.
explanations.D: Could be true but not must. The stimulus gives no distribution of exhibited vs. unexhibited works.
explanations.E: Overreach. The conditional applies only to pre-1950 paintings that have been exhibited in the last ten years, not all pre-1950 paintings.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires combining a universal claim with a most-statement to derive a guaranteed existential overlap. Trap (C) collapses 'most' into 'all'; trap (D) is a could-be-true.
lr.stimulus: Every member of the Riverton Medical Society holds an active license to practice medicine in the state. Most members of the Riverton Medical Society have completed a residency in internal medicine. A few members of the society practice exclusively in rural clinics outside Riverton.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most licensed physicians in the state are members of the Riverton Medical Society.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At least some members of the society who completed an internal medicine residency hold an active state medical license.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All members of the society have completed a residency in internal medicine.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some members of the society who practice in rural clinics have completed a residency in internal medicine.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No member of the society who lacks an internal medicine residency practices in a rural clinic.

explanations.correct: Every member of the society holds an active license. Most members have completed an internal medicine residency — those members are also members, so they also hold the license. Hence at least some (in fact all) members who completed the residency hold a license.
explanations.A: Out of scope. The stimulus doesn't address what share of state physicians belong to the society.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Collapses 'most' into 'all.' The stimulus supports only that most, not all, members completed an internal medicine residency.
explanations.D: Could be true but not must. 'Most' and 'a few' can overlap, but the stimulus does not force overlap.
explanations.E: Could be true but not must. Nothing forbids a rural-clinic member who did not complete an internal medicine residency.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires applying the contrapositive of a two-variable conditional and rejecting a converse trap. Trap (A) affirms the consequent; trap (E) is too strong.
lr.stimulus: If a manufacturing firm in this region has reduced its energy costs by more than 20 percent over the past five years, then it has either installed on-site solar generation or switched to a regional renewable electricity supplier. The Farley Plant has neither installed on-site solar generation nor switched to a regional renewable electricity supplier. Every manufacturing firm in this region that has switched to a regional renewable electricity supplier has signed a long-term fixed-rate contract.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any manufacturing firm in the region that has installed on-site solar generation has reduced its energy costs by more than 20 percent over the past five years.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Farley Plant has not reduced its energy costs by more than 20 percent over the past five years.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Farley Plant has signed a long-term fixed-rate contract.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most manufacturing firms in the region have reduced their energy costs by more than 20 percent.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No manufacturing firm in the region has reduced its energy costs without switching to a regional renewable electricity supplier.

explanations.correct: The first sentence says a firm with greater-than-20% cost reduction must have done one of the two listed things. By contrapositive, a firm that has done neither cannot have reduced its costs by more than 20%. That's the Farley Plant.
explanations.A: Affirms the consequent. The conditional runs from cost reduction to action, not from action to cost reduction.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Could be true but not must. The fixed-rate rule applies only to firms that switched suppliers, and Farley did not.
explanations.D: Unsupported. The stimulus gives no distributional claim about manufacturing firms generally.
explanations.E: Overreach — the first sentence lists two alternatives, so cost reduction doesn't require supplier switching specifically.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires reading 'unless' correctly and chaining it with a second conditional. Trap (B) is a temporal-confusion overreach; trap (E) collapses 'some' into 'all.'
lr.stimulus: No historical monograph published by the Brindle University Press is accepted for publication unless it has been reviewed by at least two outside specialists. Some historical monographs that have been reviewed by at least two outside specialists are rejected on grounds of insufficient archival evidence. Every historical monograph that is rejected on grounds of insufficient archival evidence can be resubmitted after further archival research.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At least some historical monographs that have been reviewed by two outside specialists can be resubmitted after further archival research.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No historical monograph submitted to the Brindle University Press is rejected for any reason other than insufficient archival evidence.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any historical monograph that is reviewed by at least two outside specialists is eventually accepted for publication.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All historical monographs published by the Brindle University Press have been resubmitted at least once.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Every historical monograph submitted to the press has been reviewed by at least two outside specialists.

explanations.correct: The stimulus says some monographs reviewed by two or more specialists are rejected for insufficient archival evidence, and every such rejected monograph can be resubmitted. Chaining these yields: some monographs reviewed by two or more specialists can be resubmitted.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Out of scope. The stimulus lists one ground for rejection but does not say it is the only one.
explanations.C: Contradicted by the stimulus — some reviewed monographs are rejected.
explanations.D: Overreach. The stimulus permits resubmission but does not claim published monographs were in fact resubmitted.
explanations.E: Inverts the 'unless' clause. The rule says reviewing is necessary for acceptance, not for submission.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires chaining a universal with a most-claim via a common subject to guarantee existential overlap. Trap (D) is the converse; trap (C) is too strong.
lr.stimulus: All tenured professors at Kirchner College serve on at least one standing committee. Most tenured professors at Kirchner College are also members of the Faculty Senate. Every member of the Faculty Senate has voting privileges on curricular matters.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every tenured professor at Kirchner College has voting privileges on curricular matters.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At least some tenured professors at Kirchner College who serve on a standing committee have voting privileges on curricular matters.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All members of the Faculty Senate are tenured professors at Kirchner College.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any professor at Kirchner College who has voting privileges on curricular matters is a tenured professor.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most members of the Faculty Senate serve on more than one standing committee.

explanations.correct: Most tenured professors are Faculty Senate members (so at least some exist); every such Senate member has curricular voting privileges; and every tenured professor serves on at least one standing committee. Therefore at least some tenured professors who serve on a standing committee have curricular voting privileges.
explanations.A: Overreach — only the tenured professors who are Senate members are guaranteed voting privileges, and 'most' is not 'all.'
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Converse error — Senate members need not be tenured professors.
explanations.D: Converse error — curricular voting privileges may extend to non-tenured Senate members.
explanations.E: Unsupported. The stimulus says nothing about how many committees Senate members serve on.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires pairing a universal claim with a specific instance to derive a conditional about a named subject. Trap (A) overreaches by generalizing to all soils; trap (E) introduces scope shift.
lr.stimulus: Any agricultural soil in the Mendris Valley with a pH below 5.8 has measurable concentrations of aluminum that inhibit wheat root development. Soils that inhibit wheat root development cannot support commercially viable wheat yields without amendment. The east parcel of the Dahl farm has an agricultural soil in the Mendris Valley with a pH of 5.4.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All agricultural soils in the Mendris Valley require amendment to support commercially viable wheat yields.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The soil on the east parcel of the Dahl farm cannot support commercially viable wheat yields without amendment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most farms in the Mendris Valley have soils with a pH below 5.8.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a soil's pH is above 5.8, it will support commercially viable wheat yields without amendment.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The east parcel of the Dahl farm has the lowest soil pH in the Mendris Valley.

explanations.correct: The east parcel's soil has pH 5.4, below 5.8. By the first conditional, it inhibits wheat root development. By the second, it cannot support commercially viable wheat yields without amendment.
explanations.A: Overreach — the rule applies only to Mendris Valley soils with pH below 5.8, not all valley soils.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Unsupported — the stimulus gives no distribution of valley soil pH.
explanations.D: Negates the antecedent — a pH above 5.8 doesn't guarantee viability, since other amendments may still be needed.
explanations.E: Scope shift — the stimulus does not compare pH across parcels.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires combining two universals about overlapping groups to force an existential intersection. Trap (A) is the converse; trap (B) is could-be-true.
lr.stimulus: Every person who serves on the city's zoning board must also hold membership in the local bar association. Some members of the local bar association have represented clients in disputes before the zoning board. No person who has represented a client in a dispute before the zoning board in the past two years may serve on the zoning board.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every member of the local bar association is eligible to serve on the city's zoning board.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some members of the local bar association who have represented clients before the zoning board are currently serving on it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No member of the zoning board has represented a client in a dispute before the board in the past two years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most members of the local bar association have represented clients in disputes before the zoning board.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Anyone who has ever represented a client in a dispute before the zoning board is barred from the bar association.

explanations.correct: The third sentence states that no one who has represented a client before the board in the past two years may serve on it. Since current board members serve on it, none of them can fall in that class.
explanations.A: Converse error — the rule is that board members must be bar members, not that every bar member is eligible.
explanations.B: Contradicted by the stimulus — recent representation disqualifies service.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Collapses 'some' into 'most.' The stimulus supports only that some bar members have represented such clients.
explanations.E: Overreach — the stimulus bars certain representers from the zoning board, not from the bar association itself.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires chaining an 'only if' conditional with a contrapositive applied to a specific device. Trap (D) is the converse; trap (E) overreaches on distribution.
lr.stimulus: A consumer electronics device is certified as energy efficient by the Vadren Standards Board only if it consumes less than 0.5 watts in standby mode. Any device that consumes less than 0.5 watts in standby mode uses a modern low-leakage power supply. The Luma-7 home router consumes 1.2 watts in standby mode.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Luma-7 home router is not certified as energy efficient by the Vadren Standards Board.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Luma-7 home router does not use a modern low-leakage power supply.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any device that uses a modern low-leakage power supply is certified as energy efficient by the Vadren Standards Board.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any device that consumes less than 0.5 watts in standby mode is certified as energy efficient by the Vadren Standards Board.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most home routers are not certified as energy efficient by the Vadren Standards Board.

explanations.correct: 'Certified only if consumes less than 0.5 watts' means certification requires sub-0.5-watt standby. The Luma-7 consumes 1.2 watts — above the threshold — so by contrapositive it is not certified.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Could be true but not must. The second rule tells us sub-0.5-watt devices use low-leakage supplies; it doesn't tell us that above-0.5-watt devices can't.
explanations.C: Converse error — low-leakage supply doesn't guarantee certification.
explanations.D: Affirms the necessary condition as if it were sufficient. Sub-0.5-watt standby is necessary for certification but not stated to be sufficient.
explanations.E: Unsupported. The stimulus gives no distribution over home routers.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires applying the contrapositive to a conjunctive consequent, recognizing that failure of one conjunct suffices. Trap (C) is a converse error; trap (E) is could-be-true.
lr.stimulus: Any language that develops a grammatical case system also develops a corresponding set of morphological markers and a stable word order. Proto-Lerian had a well-documented set of morphological markers but no stable word order. Every language descended from Proto-Lerian inherited at least some of its morphological markers.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Proto-Lerian did not develop a grammatical case system.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No language descended from Proto-Lerian has a grammatical case system.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any language with a stable word order and morphological markers develops a grammatical case system.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most languages descended from Proto-Lerian have a stable word order.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Proto-Lerian's morphological markers originated in an earlier language with a grammatical case system.

explanations.correct: The first sentence requires that a language with a grammatical case system have both morphological markers and a stable word order. Proto-Lerian lacks the latter, so by contrapositive it did not develop a grammatical case system.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Overreach. The stimulus is silent on whether descendant languages have developed stable word order and case systems of their own.
explanations.C: Converse error — the conditional runs from case system to the two features, not the other way.
explanations.D: Unsupported. The stimulus says descendants inherited some morphological markers, not that they have stable word order.
explanations.E: Could be true but not must. Nothing in the stimulus establishes how Proto-Lerian's markers originated.

lr.difficultyReason: Historical narrative passage with several interrelated facts. Traps overreach by asserting causal claims or universal generalizations not supported by the stimulus.
lr.stimulus: The 1854 Broad Street cholera outbreak in London killed over six hundred people in a matter of weeks. Physician John Snow mapped the cases and found that nearly all of them clustered around a single water pump on Broad Street. He persuaded local authorities to remove the pump handle, and new cases dropped sharply immediately afterward. Snow did not yet possess a germ theory of disease; he proceeded entirely from the statistical pattern of the cases. The germ theory of disease was not formally articulated until decades later, by Louis Pasteur and Robert Koch.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Snow's identification of the pump as the outbreak's source was made possible only because he understood germ theory.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The removal of the pump handle was the sole reason the 1854 Broad Street outbreak eventually ended.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Snow reached his conclusions about the outbreak's source through observation of a geographic pattern rather than through knowledge of disease-causing microorganisms.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No physician before Snow had ever investigated an epidemic by mapping the locations of its victims.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Pasteur and Koch built their germ theory directly on the empirical findings Snow published after the 1854 outbreak.

explanations.correct: The stimulus explicitly states that Snow 'proceeded entirely from the statistical pattern of the cases' and did not yet possess germ theory. C accurately restates this entailment.
explanations.A: Contradicted by the stimulus, which explicitly states Snow did not yet possess germ theory.
explanations.B: Too strong — 'sole reason' overreaches. The passage only notes that new cases dropped sharply; it does not rule out other contributing factors.
explanations.C: Correct. Directly entailed by the passage's statement that Snow acted on the statistical/geographic pattern without germ theory.
explanations.D: Scope overreach — the passage makes no claim about what other physicians had or had not done before Snow.
explanations.E: Causal overreach — the passage does not say Pasteur and Koch relied on Snow's findings; it merely places their work chronologically later.

lr.difficultyReason: Environmental science passage with numerical and conditional claims. The correct answer requires a modest hedged inference; traps either overstate the evidence or introduce unsupported causal claims.
lr.stimulus: Coral reefs occupy less than one percent of the ocean floor yet are home to approximately twenty-five percent of all known marine species. Rising ocean temperatures cause a process called bleaching, in which corals expel the symbiotic algae that provide most of their nutrients, leaving them vulnerable to starvation and disease. Bleaching events have increased in both frequency and severity since the 1980s. Some coral reefs that experienced severe bleaching in the 1990s have since partially recovered, but none of those reefs has returned to its pre-bleaching species diversity.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rising ocean temperatures are the only significant threat facing coral reef ecosystems today.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The coral reefs that bleached severely in the 1990s will never fully recover their original species diversity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At least some coral reefs that suffered severe bleaching in the 1990s have not yet regained the full range of species they hosted before bleaching occurred.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A decline in coral reef habitat would reduce the total number of known marine species by approximately twenty-five percent.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Marine species that inhabit coral reefs are more adaptable to temperature changes than those living elsewhere in the ocean.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that none of the reefs that recovered after severe 1990s bleaching returned to pre-bleaching species diversity. C restates this as a hedged inference ('at least some… have not yet regained'), which is directly entailed.
explanations.A: Scope overreach — the passage discusses only temperature-induced bleaching; it does not say this is the only significant threat.
explanations.B: Too strong — 'never fully recover' goes beyond what the passage says ('has not yet returned'). The passage speaks to current status, not permanent impossibility.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Causal overreach — the 25% figure is about known species; the passage does not say those species would disappear with the reefs, only that they inhabit them.
explanations.E: Not supported — the passage provides no comparison of adaptability between reef species and other marine species.

lr.difficultyReason: Economics passage with conditional and comparative claims. The correct answer follows from a direct combination of two stated facts; traps introduce scope shifts or unsupported universals.
lr.stimulus: A country's trade balance is defined as the value of its exports minus the value of its imports. When the trade balance is negative, the country is said to run a trade deficit. In the most recent fiscal year, Torland exported goods worth 40 billion dolas and imported goods worth 55 billion dolas. Torland's government has announced a new policy requiring all domestically purchased electronics to be manufactured within Torland's borders. Electronics currently account for 30 percent of Torland's total imports by value.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In the most recent fiscal year, Torland ran a trade deficit.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If Torland's new electronics policy is fully implemented, Torland will achieve a positive trade balance within one fiscal year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The new electronics policy will lower Torland's total import costs by approximately 16.5 billion dolas.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Torland's trade deficit is primarily caused by its reliance on imported electronics.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Countries that restrict imports of consumer electronics consistently improve their trade balances within two years.

explanations.correct: Exports (40B) minus imports (55B) = –15B, which is a negative trade balance. By definition given in the passage, this means Torland ran a trade deficit. A is directly entailed.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Too strong — full implementation is assumed, but the passage does not say all electronics spending would become domestic exports, nor that other import/export figures remain constant.
explanations.C: This requires assuming the policy fully eliminates electronics imports; the passage does not establish that outcome, only that the policy requires domestic manufacturing.
explanations.D: Causal overreach — the passage identifies electronics as 30% of imports but does not say the deficit is primarily caused by electronics imports.
explanations.E: Scope shift — the passage discusses only Torland; no general claim about all countries is entailed.

lr.difficultyReason: Policy/law passage with conditional rules. The correct answer requires applying one conditional rule to a stated fact; traps conflate the conditional with its converse or extend it improperly.
lr.stimulus: Under the regulations of the Veldran Environmental Agency, a facility is classified as a hazardous waste site if it contains any quantity of at least three substances on the Agency's Priority Pollutant List. The Millbrook industrial complex has been confirmed to contain lead, mercury, and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), all of which appear on the Priority Pollutant List. A facility classified as a hazardous waste site is legally required to submit to Agency inspection within sixty days of classification.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Millbrook complex will be inspected by the Agency within sixty days.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Millbrook complex is legally required to submit to Agency inspection within sixty days.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any industrial facility containing lead and mercury is legally required to submit to Agency inspection.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Millbrook complex poses a greater health risk than facilities containing only one Priority Pollutant List substance.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Facilities that have not been classified as hazardous waste sites do not contain any Priority Pollutant List substances.

explanations.correct: Millbrook contains three Priority Pollutant List substances, so it satisfies the classification condition and must be classified as a hazardous waste site. Classified sites are legally required to submit to inspection within sixty days. B follows directly from chaining these two rules.
explanations.A: Too strong — the passage states a legal requirement to submit, not that inspection will actually occur within sixty days. The requirement and the occurrence are distinct.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Converse error / scope shift — the rule requires at least three list substances, not just two. A facility with only lead and mercury has not met the threshold.
explanations.D: Health-risk comparison is not addressed anywhere in the passage; this is an unsupported inference.
explanations.E: Converse error — the rule says containing three+ list substances triggers classification; it does not say unclassified facilities contain none.
