lr.stimulus: Under the statutes of a particular jurisdiction, a contract is enforceable only if it was entered into voluntarily by all parties. A contract entered into under duress is not considered voluntary. Courts in this jurisdiction have held that any agreement signed by a party who was simultaneously facing a credible threat of physical harm constitutes an agreement entered into under duress. Records show that Meridian Logistics signed the Thornfield Agreement while one of its executives was receiving written threats of physical violence from an outside party, and that these threats were reported to local law enforcement at the time of signing.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Thornfield Agreement was entered into fraudulently by Meridian Logistics.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All contracts signed during periods of financial hardship are unenforceable in this jurisdiction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Thornfield Agreement is not enforceable in this jurisdiction.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The outside party who made the threats will be prosecuted for coercion under the laws of this jurisdiction.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Meridian Logistics would not have signed the Thornfield Agreement had it not been for the threats of physical violence.

explanations.correct: Chain: The agreement was signed while Meridian faced credible written threats of physical harm → under court holdings, this constitutes duress → a contract under duress is not voluntary → a contract is enforceable only if voluntary → therefore the Thornfield Agreement is not enforceable.
explanations.A: Introduces fraud, which is a separate legal concept not mentioned in the stimulus. Scope shift.
explanations.B: Overreach and scope shift — the rules concern physical threats creating duress, not financial hardship.
explanations.C: Correct. The conditional chain directly entails this conclusion.
explanations.D: Introduces a prosecution outcome that goes well beyond anything stated in the stimulus. Could be true but is not entailed.
explanations.E: Speculates about Meridian's counterfactual motivations — the stimulus does not establish that the threats were causally necessary for the signing, only that they occurred simultaneously.

lr.difficultyReason: Linguistics passage with a descriptive finding and a hedged general claim. Correct answer is a modest inference about scope; traps overstate universality or introduce causation.
lr.stimulus: Researchers studying the phonological systems of unrelated languages found that in every language examined, certain consonant sounds classified as voiced stops — specifically, sounds produced by complete closure of the vocal tract combined with vocal cord vibration — were acquired by children before any fricative sounds in the same language were acquired. The researchers examined languages from six distinct language families, including families with no known historical relationship to one another. No language examined lacked at least one voiced stop consonant.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Children learning any human language will always acquire voiced stop consonants before fricatives.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The presence of voiced stop consonants in a language is a prerequisite for the development of fricative sounds in that language.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Among the languages examined, at least some children acquired voiced stop consonants before acquiring fricative sounds.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Voiced stop consonants are more phonologically complex than fricatives in all known language families.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Languages with a greater number of voiced stops will have correspondingly fewer fricative sounds.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that in every language examined, children acquired voiced stops before fricatives. This directly entails that among the languages examined, at least some children acquired voiced stops before fricatives — in fact all of them did, making 'at least some' necessarily true.
explanations.A: Overreach — 'any human language' extends beyond the languages examined to all human languages, which the stimulus does not establish.
explanations.B: Introduces a developmental/structural prerequisite claim that is not supported — the stimulus describes acquisition order, not phonological dependency.
explanations.C: Correct. 'At least some' is directly entailed since every examined language showed this pattern.
explanations.D: Comparative phonological complexity is not discussed in the stimulus. Scope shift.
explanations.E: Introduces an inverse relationship between stop count and fricative count with no basis in the stimulus.

lr.difficultyReason: Medical/epidemiological passage. Correct answer requires combining two factual statements; traps introduce causation where only correlation is established, or overstate the scope of the finding.
lr.stimulus: A longitudinal study tracked 2,400 adults over twenty years, monitoring their dietary habits and cardiovascular health. Participants who consumed at least three servings of fatty fish per week had, on average, significantly lower rates of arterial calcification than those who consumed no fatty fish. However, participants who took fish-oil supplements without consuming whole fish showed no significant reduction in arterial calcification compared to the no-fish group. The study controlled for age, smoking status, and baseline cholesterol levels.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fish-oil supplements are ineffective at improving any aspect of cardiovascular health.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The reduction in arterial calcification observed in whole-fish consumers was caused by a nutrient not present in fish-oil supplements.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Among the study participants, eating fatty fish whole was associated with lower rates of arterial calcification than taking fish-oil supplements.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Adults who eat fatty fish at least three times per week will not develop arterial calcification.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fish-oil supplements are harmful to cardiovascular health when taken without consuming whole fish.

explanations.correct: Whole fish consumers had significantly lower arterial calcification; supplement-only consumers showed no significant reduction compared to no-fish consumers. Therefore, within the study, eating whole fatty fish was associated with lower calcification rates than taking supplements alone.
explanations.A: Overreach — the study only measured arterial calcification; supplements may improve other cardiovascular markers not examined.
explanations.B: Introduces a specific causal mechanism (a missing nutrient) that the study did not identify; this is an inference beyond what the data entails.
explanations.C: Correct. Directly entailed: whole fish → lower calcification; supplements → no reduction. Therefore whole fish group had lower rates than supplement group.
explanations.D: Too strong — the stimulus says lower rates, not zero calcification; 'will not develop' is an absolute claim.
explanations.E: Introduces harm from supplements, which the study does not establish — no reduction is not the same as harm.

lr.difficultyReason: Technology/policy passage with a conditional rule and a particular case. Correct answer requires applying the rule and noting a gap in what the stimulus establishes. Traps confuse sufficient with necessary conditions.
lr.stimulus: A software company's data-retention policy states that any file flagged as containing personally identifiable information must be encrypted before being stored on external servers. Files not flagged as containing personally identifiable information may be stored unencrypted. An internal audit revealed that several hundred files were stored on the company's external servers without encryption. The audit further found that the company's automated flagging system had failed to flag any file during the six months prior to the audit.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The files stored without encryption on external servers contained no personally identifiable information.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The company violated its data-retention policy with respect to at least some of the unencrypted files, if any of those files contained personally identifiable information.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The failure of the flagging system was the sole cause of the unencrypted files being stored on external servers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All employees responsible for data storage were aware that the flagging system had failed.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The company will be required to encrypt all files currently stored on its external servers.

explanations.correct: The policy requires encryption for flagged files (those containing PII). If any unencrypted files actually contained PII, then they should have been flagged and encrypted. Storing them unencrypted would violate the policy. The conditional phrasing 'if any of those files contained PII' makes this a certain entailment.
explanations.A: Overreach — the stimulus says the flagging system failed to flag files, but this does not establish that the unflagged files lacked PII; the system may have simply missed them.
explanations.B: Correct. If any unencrypted files contained PII, they should have been encrypted per policy; storing them unencrypted would be a policy violation.
explanations.C: Too strong — 'sole cause' rules out other contributing factors (e.g., employee error); the stimulus does not establish exclusivity.
explanations.D: Speculates about employee awareness, which is not addressed in the stimulus.
explanations.E: Introduces a regulatory requirement not mentioned in the stimulus; the policy describes what must happen before storage, not a remediation obligation.

lr.difficultyReason: Ethics/philosophy passage with descriptive claims about moral frameworks. Correct answer is a modest comparative inference; traps overstate the normative conclusion or introduce value judgments not in the stimulus.
lr.stimulus: Consequentialist moral theories evaluate the rightness of an action solely by reference to its outcomes — specifically, whether the action produces more overall well-being than any available alternative. Deontological moral theories, by contrast, evaluate actions by reference to duties and rules that apply regardless of outcomes. Philosophers have noted that in cases where adhering to a moral duty would produce substantially worse outcomes than violating it, consequentialist and deontological theories will frequently prescribe different actions. Most practicing ethicists acknowledge that neither framework alone provides a complete account of all widely shared moral intuitions.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Consequentialist theories are more practically useful than deontological theories in resolving real-world ethical disputes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: There are situations in which consequentialist and deontological theories will recommend different courses of action.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any moral theory that fails to account for both duties and outcomes is necessarily inferior to one that incorporates both.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deontological theories are incapable of providing guidance in situations where outcomes are uncertain.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most ethicists believe that consequentialism provides a more complete account of moral intuitions than deontology does.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that when adhering to a duty would produce substantially worse outcomes than violating it, the two theories 'will frequently prescribe different actions.' This directly entails that there are situations in which they recommend different courses of action.
explanations.A: Introduces a practical utility comparison not discussed in the stimulus. Scope shift.
explanations.B: Correct. The stimulus explicitly identifies a class of cases where the theories prescribe different actions.
explanations.C: Introduces a normative ranking of theories incorporating both elements — this is a value judgment not entailed by the descriptive claims in the stimulus.
explanations.D: Overreach — the stimulus says deontological theories apply regardless of outcomes, but does not say they cannot function under uncertainty.
explanations.E: Misreads the stimulus — the passage says most ethicists think neither framework alone is complete, not that one is more complete than the other.

lr.difficultyReason: Environmental science passage with quantitative and causal claims. Correct answer combines two stated facts; traps introduce unwarranted causal direction or extend findings beyond the stated population.
lr.stimulus: A wetlands survey conducted across a river delta found that parcels of wetland vegetation containing three or more distinct plant species had measurably higher water filtration capacity than parcels containing only one or two species. Parcels with higher water filtration capacity were found to retain significantly more sediment during flood events than parcels with lower filtration capacity. The survey also noted that human agricultural activity had reduced plant species diversity in approximately 40 percent of the delta's wetland parcels over the preceding three decades.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Wetland parcels with three or more plant species retain more sediment during flood events than parcels with only one or two species.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Agricultural activity is the primary cause of sediment loss in the river delta.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Eliminating all agricultural activity in the delta would fully restore wetland filtration capacity to its original levels.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Wetland parcels with higher plant diversity are better suited for agricultural use than parcels with lower diversity.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Approximately 40 percent of the delta's wetland parcels now have reduced water filtration capacity compared to three decades ago.

explanations.correct: Chain: parcels with 3+ species → higher filtration capacity; higher filtration capacity → more sediment retained during floods. Combining these: parcels with 3+ species retain more sediment during floods than those with 1–2 species (which have lower filtration capacity).
explanations.A: Correct. The two-step chain directly entails this conclusion.
explanations.B: Introduces primary causation of sediment loss — the stimulus does not compare agricultural activity to other causes of sediment loss.
explanations.C: Speculative and too strong — 'fully restore' and 'original levels' go well beyond what the stimulus establishes about the relationship between agricultural activity and filtration capacity.
explanations.D: Introduces agricultural suitability, a concept entirely outside the scope of the stimulus.
explanations.E: Tempting but not fully entailed — the stimulus says agricultural activity reduced species diversity in ~40% of parcels, and lower diversity correlates with lower filtration, but the survey finding applies to parcels with 1–2 species vs. 3+ species. The stimulus does not specify that all parcels reduced to lower diversity categories fall below the 3-species threshold.

lr.difficultyReason: Arts/cultural history passage in a descriptive narrative style. Correct answer is a hedged comparative inference; traps overstate the causal or evaluative claims beyond what the passage establishes.
lr.stimulus: The Harlem Renaissance of the 1920s produced a substantial body of visual art, literature, and music created by African American artists who had migrated to New York from the American South and from the Caribbean. Critics writing in the 1930s noted that many of these works drew on vernacular musical traditions, folk imagery, and oral storytelling forms that had not previously been represented in mainstream American cultural institutions. Several of the artists associated with the movement explicitly described their work as an effort to create a distinctly African American aesthetic tradition independent of European modernist conventions.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Harlem Renaissance produced works of greater artistic merit than any other American cultural movement of the twentieth century.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Prior to the 1920s, vernacular musical traditions and folk imagery of African Americans had not influenced any American artistic works.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At least some artists associated with the Harlem Renaissance consciously sought to develop an aesthetic tradition distinct from European modernism.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The migration of African Americans to New York was the sole cause of the Harlem Renaissance's emergence as a cultural movement.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Critics writing in the 1930s regarded the works of the Harlem Renaissance as superior to works produced by European modernists of the same era.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that 'several of the artists associated with the movement explicitly described their work as an effort to create a distinctly African American aesthetic tradition independent of European modernist conventions.' This directly entails that at least some artists consciously sought such a distinction.
explanations.A: Introduces a comparative merit judgment not supported or even suggested by the stimulus. Overreach.
explanations.B: Too strong — the stimulus says these traditions had not been represented in mainstream cultural institutions, not that they had never influenced any American artistic work. Scope shift.
explanations.C: Correct. 'Several artists explicitly described' this goal entails that at least some artists consciously sought it.
explanations.D: Overreach — 'sole cause' eliminates other contributing factors; the stimulus mentions migration as a background condition, not as the exclusive cause.
explanations.E: Introduces a comparative evaluative judgment about critics' views not stated in the passage. The critics noted the vernacular sources; they did not rank the works against European modernism.

lr.difficultyReason: Historical narrative stimulus with multiple events. Traps overreach what the passage establishes; the correct answer is a modest, hedged inference about the limits of pre-modern medical understanding.
lr.stimulus: In the early nineteenth century, physicians in Vienna observed that the mortality rate among women giving birth in the hospital's First Maternity Division, which was staffed by medical students, was far higher than in the Second Division, staffed by midwives. Ignaz Semmelweis, a physician at the hospital, determined that the medical students moved directly from performing cadaver dissections to delivering babies without washing their hands. After Semmelweis instituted a handwashing requirement using a chlorinated lime solution, mortality rates in the First Division dropped sharply. Despite this outcome, many of Semmelweis's colleagues rejected his protocol. At the time, germ theory had not yet been established, and the prevailing explanatory framework attributed puerperal fever to atmospheric or cosmic influences beyond individual clinical control.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Semmelweis's colleagues rejected his findings because they were personally opposed to improved hygiene practices in medical settings.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Puerperal fever in Vienna's maternity wards was caused entirely by the failure of medical students to wash their hands.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The theoretical framework available to physicians at the time was not adequate to fully explain the mechanism behind Semmelweis's empirical results.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Midwives in the Second Division practiced handwashing, which is why mortality rates there remained low.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Semmelweis's handwashing protocol was eventually adopted as standard practice throughout European hospitals before his death.

explanations.correct: The passage states that germ theory had not yet been established and that colleagues attributed puerperal fever to atmospheric influences. Since the true mechanism (microbial transmission via unwashed hands) lay outside the prevailing explanatory framework, that framework was insufficient to fully account for why Semmelweis's intervention worked.
explanations.A: Overreach / scope shift — the passage says colleagues rejected the protocol, but attributes this to the prevailing theoretical framework, not personal opposition to hygiene.
explanations.B: Too strong — 'caused entirely' overstates the stimulus, which identifies one contributing factor without ruling out others.
explanations.C: Correct — entailed by the explicit statement that germ theory was absent and colleagues relied on atmospheric explanations, making the true mechanism inexplicable within that framework.
explanations.D: The passage never states that midwives washed their hands; it only identifies the students' movement from cadavers to deliveries as the distinguishing factor.
explanations.E: Temporal overreach — the passage gives no information about what happened after Semmelweis instituted the protocol beyond the immediate mortality drop.

lr.difficultyReason: Economics stimulus with numerical comparisons. Correct answer requires a modest transitive inference from the data; traps introduce causal claims or global generalizations not supported by the figures.
lr.stimulus: A study of three manufacturing regions found the following: Region X had the highest average wage among the three but the lowest rate of employment growth over the past decade. Region Y had the lowest average wage but the highest rate of employment growth. Region Z fell between the other two on both measures. The study also noted that all three regions experienced net population growth during the same period, and that in each region the number of job seekers increased faster than the number of available positions.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: High average wages are the primary cause of slow employment growth in manufacturing regions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Workers in Region X are better compensated per hour than workers in Region Z.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At least one of the three regions experienced labor market conditions in which demand for jobs outpaced the supply of available positions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Region Y will eventually develop higher average wages as its employment base expands.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The region with the fastest employment growth attracted the most migrants during the study period.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states explicitly that in each region the number of job seekers increased faster than the number of available positions. This means all three regions — and therefore at least one — experienced conditions where job-seeker demand outpaced job supply.
explanations.A: Causal overreach — the stimulus establishes a correlation between high wages and low employment growth in this sample, but does not establish causation, let alone that wages are the 'primary cause.'
explanations.B: Scope shift — 'average wage' as reported in the study is not the same as 'per-hour compensation'; the stimulus does not specify whether wages are hourly, weekly, or otherwise.
explanations.C: Correct — this is entailed directly by the statement that in each region job seekers increased faster than available positions.
explanations.D: Predictive overreach — the stimulus describes past data only; no basis exists for projecting future wage changes in Region Y.
explanations.E: Unsupported — the stimulus notes population growth in all three regions but does not specify migration as the cause or link it specifically to employment growth rates.

lr.difficultyReason: Environmental science passage with conditional statements. Correct answer is a contrapositive inference. Traps include a plausible-but-unforced causal claim and a scope shift from wetlands generally to coastal wetlands specifically.
lr.stimulus: Wetland ecosystems that receive regular tidal inundation maintain significantly higher soil carbon stocks than wetlands that do not receive tidal flow. All salt marshes receive regular tidal inundation. Freshwater inland marshes, by contrast, do not receive tidal inundation and typically exhibit much lower soil carbon stocks. Restoration projects that reconnect previously diked coastal wetlands to tidal flow have, in every documented case, resulted in measurable increases in soil carbon within five years.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Freshwater inland marshes can be converted into salt marshes if they are reconnected to tidal flow.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Any wetland that does not maintain high soil carbon stocks does not receive regular tidal inundation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tidal inundation is the sole mechanism responsible for carbon sequestration in wetland ecosystems.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Salt marshes have higher soil carbon stocks than freshwater inland marshes.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Restoration projects involving non-coastal wetlands would produce even greater carbon increases than those observed in coastal restoration projects.

explanations.correct: The stimulus establishes that wetlands with regular tidal inundation have significantly higher soil carbon stocks than those without, that all salt marshes receive tidal inundation, and that freshwater inland marshes do not. It follows necessarily that salt marshes (with tidal inundation) have higher soil carbon stocks than freshwater inland marshes (without tidal inundation).
explanations.A: Unsupported — reconnecting to tidal flow increases carbon stocks but the stimulus says nothing about converting freshwater marshes into salt marshes, which involve different salinity and ecological conditions.
explanations.B: Contrapositive error — the stimulus says tidal inundation produces high carbon stocks, not that high carbon stocks are impossible without it; the contrapositive of 'tidal inundation → high carbon' is 'no high carbon → no tidal inundation,' which is what B states. However, the original conditional is 'wetlands WITH tidal inundation HAVE higher stocks THAN those without' — a comparative, not an absolute threshold. B uses 'does not maintain high soil carbon stocks' as an absolute, making it an overstatement of the conditional. The stimulus does not establish a binary high/low threshold.
explanations.C: Too strong — 'sole mechanism' is an overreach; the stimulus identifies tidal inundation as a factor associated with higher carbon stocks but does not rule out other mechanisms.
explanations.D: Correct — follows from the chain: salt marshes receive tidal inundation; wetlands with tidal inundation have significantly higher soil carbon than those without; freshwater inland marshes lack tidal inundation.
explanations.E: Speculative prediction with no basis in the stimulus, which only documents coastal restoration outcomes.

lr.difficultyReason: Legal/policy stimulus. Correct answer is a modest inference about what the statute does not cover; traps introduce legislative intent or comparative legal claims not present in the text.
lr.stimulus: A state statute provides that a landlord may terminate a residential lease without cause only if the landlord provides at least ninety days' written notice. The statute further specifies that it applies exclusively to tenancies of twelve months or longer. A separate provision states that any lease terminated in violation of the statute's notice requirement is voidable at the tenant's election. Judicial interpretations of the statute have uniformly held that month-to-month tenancies, regardless of how long they have continued, are not tenancies of twelve months or longer within the meaning of the statute.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true given the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A landlord who terminates a month-to-month tenancy without notice violates the statute.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A tenant in a month-to-month tenancy that has lasted two years has no legal protections of any kind against termination without notice.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A tenant in a twelve-month lease who receives only sixty days' notice of termination may choose to treat that termination as void.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The legislature intended to provide stronger protections to long-term tenants than to month-to-month tenants.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Month-to-month tenancies are a less stable form of housing than twelve-month leases.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states the statute applies to tenancies of twelve months or longer and that any lease terminated in violation of the notice requirement is voidable at the tenant's election. A twelve-month lease terminated with only sixty days' notice violates the ninety-day requirement; therefore the tenant may elect to void it.
explanations.A: Contradicted — courts have held month-to-month tenancies fall outside the statute's scope, so terminating one without notice does not violate this statute (though other law might apply, the stimulus does not establish that).
explanations.B: Too strong — the stimulus addresses only this statute; it cannot establish that no other legal protections exist. The phrase 'of any kind' makes this an overreach.
explanations.C: Correct — directly entailed by combining the statute's scope (twelve-month leases), notice requirement (ninety days), and voidability provision (voidable at tenant's election when notice requirement is violated).
explanations.D: Legislative intent is not established by the stimulus; the statutory text and judicial holdings are provided, but the legislature's purpose is not stated.
explanations.E: Policy/sociological judgment entirely outside the scope of the statutory description provided.

lr.difficultyReason: Technology/linguistics hybrid stimulus describing a pattern in speech-recognition software. Correct answer is a hedged inference about at least some systems; traps introduce causal or universal claims.
lr.stimulus: Automatic speech-recognition systems trained exclusively on data from adult speakers consistently underperform when transcribing speech produced by children under age twelve. Researchers attribute this to systematic differences in vocal tract length, speaking rate, and phonemic realization between children and adults. Several leading commercial systems have released child-adapted models trained on corpora that include significant proportions of children's speech; these models show markedly reduced error rates for child speakers. However, none of the child-adapted models tested matched the accuracy those same systems achieved for adult speakers.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No automatic speech-recognition system currently available can accurately transcribe the speech of children under twelve.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At least some commercially available speech-recognition systems perform better when transcribing adult speech than when transcribing child speech, even after adaptation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Differences in vocal tract length are the primary reason that speech-recognition systems trained on adult data fail with child speakers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Speech-recognition systems can never achieve equal accuracy for both child and adult speakers because the acoustic differences between them are too large to bridge.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The child-adapted models were trained on higher-quality audio data than the models trained exclusively on adult speech.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that none of the child-adapted models matched the accuracy those same systems achieved for adult speakers. These child-adapted models are commercially released systems; therefore, at least those systems perform better on adult speech than on child speech even after adaptation.
explanations.A: Too strong — 'No system' is an overstatement. The stimulus describes underperformance and unmatched accuracy relative to adult benchmarks, not total inability to transcribe child speech accurately.
explanations.B: Correct — directly entailed: the child-adapted commercial models still did not match adult accuracy, meaning those systems (at least some commercially available ones) perform better on adult speech.
explanations.C: Overreach — the stimulus lists vocal tract length as one of several factors (along with speaking rate and phonemic realization); it does not rank them or identify any as primary.
explanations.D: Predictive/absolute overreach — the stimulus describes current systems' limitations but cannot establish that equal accuracy is categorically unachievable in the future.
explanations.E: Unsupported — the stimulus says nothing about the comparative quality of training audio data.

lr.difficultyReason: Arts/history narrative with a modest comparative inference. Traps either attribute motives not discussed or shift from a specific period to a broader claim.
lr.stimulus: During the Italian Renaissance, patrons of the arts typically specified in contractual agreements the exact materials painters were to use, including the quality and quantity of ultramarine blue pigment derived from lapis lazuli. Lapis lazuli was imported from mines in Afghanistan and was, at the time, more expensive per ounce than gold. Patrons required its use in depictions of the Virgin Mary's robe as a signal of the commission's prestige and the patron's wealth. Painters who substituted cheaper blue pigments without patron approval risked legal action for breach of contract.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Renaissance painters personally preferred to use ultramarine blue over cheaper alternatives because of its superior visual quality.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The choice of pigment in Renaissance religious paintings was, at least in some cases, determined by economic and social considerations rather than purely by aesthetic ones.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All Renaissance paintings depicting the Virgin Mary were produced under contracts requiring the use of ultramarine blue.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The importation of lapis lazuli from Afghanistan was controlled by the same merchants who financed Renaissance art patronage.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Painters who used ultramarine blue produced more spiritually significant works than those who used cheaper pigments.

explanations.correct: The stimulus establishes that patrons contractually required expensive ultramarine blue as a signal of prestige and wealth, and that painters risked legal action for using cheaper substitutes. This directly supports the inference that pigment choice was driven by economic and social factors (wealth signaling, contractual obligation) rather than purely aesthetic ones — at least in the commissioned cases described.
explanations.A: Scope shift and unsupported — the passage discusses patron requirements, not painters' personal preferences; no information about painters' aesthetic inclinations is provided.
explanations.B: Correct — entailed by the description of contractual specifications motivated by prestige-signaling and the high cost of lapis lazuli.
explanations.C: Too strong — the stimulus describes typical contractual practices among patrons but does not establish that all Renaissance paintings of the Virgin Mary were subject to such contracts.
explanations.D: Unsupported — the trade relationship between lapis lazuli merchants and art patrons is not addressed in the stimulus.
explanations.E: Evaluative overreach — the stimulus discusses cost and prestige signaling, not the spiritual quality of resulting works.

lr.difficultyReason: Ethics/policy stimulus with conditional and quantitative elements. Correct answer requires combining two conditional statements; traps rely on plausible but unforced extensions of the premises.
lr.stimulus: A hospital ethics committee has adopted the following two policies. First, any experimental treatment that has not completed Phase III clinical trials may be administered to a patient only if that patient has provided written informed consent after consulting with an independent patient advocate. Second, any patient who is currently enrolled in a separate clinical trial is ineligible to receive an experimental treatment outside of that trial. A patient, Mr. Vance, is currently enrolled in a Phase II clinical trial for a cardiac drug. His physician wishes to administer to him a separate neurological treatment that has completed only Phase II trials.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true given the hospital's policies and the facts above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mr. Vance may receive the neurological treatment if he provides written informed consent after consulting with an independent patient advocate.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The hospital's ethics committee will deny Mr. Vance's physician's request to administer the neurological treatment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mr. Vance cannot receive the neurological treatment under the hospital's current policies.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mr. Vance would be eligible to receive the neurological treatment once his current cardiac trial concludes.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The hospital's policies are designed primarily to protect patients from undue risk rather than to advance medical research.

explanations.correct: The second policy makes any patient currently enrolled in a separate clinical trial ineligible to receive an experimental treatment outside that trial. Mr. Vance is enrolled in a Phase II cardiac trial, and the neurological treatment is a separate experimental treatment (having completed only Phase II). Therefore he is ineligible regardless of consent, making it impossible for him to receive it under current policies.
explanations.A: Contradicted — while Policy 1 requires informed consent for unapproved treatments, Policy 2 independently bars Mr. Vance because he is currently enrolled in another trial. Consent cannot override the enrollment bar.
explanations.B: Overreach — the stimulus describes the policies but says nothing about what the committee will formally do procedurally; the policies establish ineligibility, but whether the committee will formally 'deny' a request involves a procedural step not described.
explanations.C: Correct — directly entailed by Policy 2: current enrollment in a separate trial renders him ineligible for the neurological treatment outside that trial.
explanations.D: Could be true but not must be true — the stimulus describes current eligibility conditions but does not establish what policies will be in place or whether the treatment will still be available after the trial concludes.
explanations.E: Unsupported — the stimulus states the policies but gives no information about the committee's underlying purposes or design intent.

lr.difficultyReason: Environmental science/economics hybrid. Correct answer is a hedged comparative inference from survey data. Traps include a causal overreach and a universal generalization from a limited sample.
lr.stimulus: A survey of fishing communities in a coastal region found that communities whose primary income derived from ecotourism reported higher median household incomes than communities whose primary income derived from commercial fishing. The survey also found that ecotourism-dependent communities had significantly lower rates of fish stock depletion in adjacent waters compared with commercially fishing communities in the same region. The survey was conducted during a period of declining global fish prices, which reduced revenues for commercial fishing operations across the entire region.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ecotourism is a more sustainable economic model than commercial fishing for all coastal communities worldwide.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The lower fish stock depletion in ecotourism communities was caused by those communities' decision to prioritize tourism over fishing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: During the survey period, declining global fish prices negatively affected the revenues of at least some communities in the surveyed region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Commercial fishing communities in the surveyed region would achieve higher median household incomes if they transitioned to ecotourism.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Fish stock depletion rates are the most important factor determining median household income in coastal communities.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that declining global fish prices reduced revenues for commercial fishing operations across the entire region, and that the survey included commercial fishing communities. Therefore, at least some communities in the region — those relying on commercial fishing — had their revenues negatively affected by the price decline.
explanations.A: Scope shift and overgeneralization — the survey covers one coastal region; extending the conclusion to 'all coastal communities worldwide' far exceeds what the data support.
explanations.B: Causal overreach — the survey documents a correlation between ecotourism dependence and lower fish stock depletion; it does not establish that the communities' prioritization decision caused the lower depletion rates.
explanations.C: Correct — directly entailed: declining prices reduced revenues for commercial fishing operations across the entire region, which necessarily includes at least some communities.
explanations.D: Predictive/counterfactual overreach — whether a transition to ecotourism would raise incomes depends on many factors not addressed in the stimulus, such as whether those communities have suitable ecotourism resources.
explanations.E: Unsupported ranking — the stimulus identifies a correlation between income and economic model but does not rank fish stock depletion as the most important determinant of income.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires chaining four conditionals and applying two contrapositives to reach the inference about a named individual. Trap (A) is an affirming-the-consequent error; trap (D) collapses a 'some' into a universal.
lr.stimulus: Every endocrinologist at Meridian Hospital who supervises a first-year resident serves on at least one departmental committee. Any physician at Meridian who serves on a departmental committee has completed the hospital's peer-review training. No physician at Meridian who has completed the peer-review training has fewer than five years of post-fellowship experience. Dr. Ahmadi is an endocrinologist at Meridian with only three years of post-fellowship experience.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any endocrinologist at Meridian with at least five years of post-fellowship experience supervises a first-year resident.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dr. Ahmadi does not supervise a first-year resident.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dr. Ahmadi has not completed the hospital's peer-review training, and she is therefore ineligible to do so.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every physician at Meridian who has supervised a first-year resident has at least five years of post-fellowship experience.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most endocrinologists at Meridian serve on a departmental committee.

explanations.correct: If Dr. Ahmadi supervised a first-year resident, she would (i) serve on a departmental committee, (ii) have completed peer-review training, and (iii) therefore have at least five years of post-fellowship experience. She has only three. By the contrapositive chain, she does not supervise a first-year resident.
explanations.A: Affirms the consequent. The chain runs from 'supervises' to the training and experience requirements, not the reverse.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Two-part claim: the first half (not completed training) follows, but the stimulus says nothing about eligibility to complete the training — it rules out current completion only.
explanations.D: Collapses the restricted conditional into a universal about everyone who has ever supervised a first-year resident in any capacity — the stimulus's rule is stated about endocrinologists currently supervising.
explanations.E: The stimulus gives no distributional claim about endocrinologists generally.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires combining a universal, a most-statement, and a some-statement to derive a guaranteed overlap (some-plus-most chain). Trap (B) is a most-to-all overreach; trap (E) is a could-be-true overlap the statements do not force.
lr.stimulus: Every journal indexed by the Central Linguistics Database requires double-blind peer review of submitted articles. Most journals indexed by the Central Linguistics Database publish at least one issue devoted to fieldwork methodology each year. Some journals that publish an issue devoted to fieldwork methodology each year also publish articles in at least three languages besides English. No journal that requires double-blind peer review accepts advertising from textbook publishers.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At least some journals that publish an issue devoted to fieldwork methodology each year do not accept advertising from textbook publishers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All journals indexed by the Central Linguistics Database publish at least one issue devoted to fieldwork methodology each year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every journal that publishes articles in at least three languages besides English is indexed by the Central Linguistics Database.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most journals that publish articles in at least three languages besides English do not accept advertising from textbook publishers.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some journals indexed by the Central Linguistics Database publish articles in at least three languages besides English.

explanations.correct: Most indexed journals publish a fieldwork-methodology issue, which means at least some indexed journals do. Every indexed journal requires double-blind peer review, and no journal that requires that review accepts textbook-publisher advertising. So at least some journals that publish a fieldwork-methodology issue do not accept such advertising.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Most-to-all overreach. The stimulus says 'most,' not 'all.'
explanations.C: Converse error. The stimulus tells us what indexed journals do, not that every journal publishing in multiple languages is indexed.
explanations.D: Could be true but not must. The three-languages group is only linked to the methodology-issue group via 'some,' which doesn't support a claim about 'most.'
explanations.E: Could be true but not must. The overlap between 'methodology-issue' journals and 'three-languages' journals is partial; those 'three-languages' journals need not be indexed ones.

lr.difficultyReason: Pigeonhole reasoning over five committee members with overlapping constraints plus a conditional. Traps include a miscounted overlap (C) and an out-of-scope inference (E).
lr.stimulus: The Ferren Arts Council Grant Committee consists of exactly five members. Each member specializes in exactly one of the following four disciplines: theater, dance, visual art, or music. At least one member specializes in each discipline. No theater specialist on the committee also serves on the Ferren Festival Board. Every visual-art specialist on the committee serves on the Ferren Festival Board.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At least three members of the committee do not serve on the Ferren Festival Board.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exactly one member of the committee specializes in each of theater, dance, and music.

choices.label: C
choices.text: More committee members serve on the Ferren Festival Board than do not.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At least one member of the committee serves on the Ferren Festival Board.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No dance specialist on the committee serves on the Ferren Festival Board.

explanations.correct: Each of the four disciplines has at least one specialist, so at least one member is a visual-art specialist. Every visual-art specialist serves on the Festival Board. Therefore, at least one committee member serves on the Festival Board.
explanations.A: Miscounts. With five members and four disciplines each represented, the distribution of non-board members is not fixed — only the theater specialists must not serve on the board, and there is at least one, not necessarily three.
explanations.B: Could be true but not must. One of the four disciplines could have two specialists (with the fifth slot unknown), but the stimulus does not force a particular distribution.
explanations.C: Cannot be determined. The number of members on the board depends on the unspecified distribution across disciplines.
explanations.D: Correct.
explanations.E: Out of scope. The stimulus is silent on whether dance specialists serve on the Festival Board.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires reading 'unless' correctly and chaining it through two further conditionals and a contrapositive applied to a named case. Trap (A) is a converse error; trap (C) overreaches a 'some' to an 'all.'
lr.stimulus: No appellate brief filed in the Fourth Circuit is accepted for oral argument unless it cites at least three prior circuit decisions. Any brief accepted for oral argument in the Fourth Circuit that challenges a statute on constitutional grounds is assigned to a three-judge panel. Every brief assigned to a three-judge panel is subject to expedited scheduling. The Ortiz brief was filed in the Fourth Circuit, challenges a statute on constitutional grounds, and is not subject to expedited scheduling.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any brief filed in the Fourth Circuit that cites at least three prior circuit decisions is accepted for oral argument.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Ortiz brief cites fewer than three prior circuit decisions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Ortiz brief has not been accepted for oral argument.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every brief filed in the Fourth Circuit that challenges a statute on constitutional grounds is subject to expedited scheduling.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most briefs filed in the Fourth Circuit are assigned to a three-judge panel.

explanations.correct: If the Ortiz brief had been accepted for oral argument, then because it challenges a statute on constitutional grounds, it would be assigned to a three-judge panel, and hence subject to expedited scheduling. It is not subject to expedited scheduling, so by contrapositive chain it has not been accepted for oral argument.
explanations.A: Converse error. The citation rule is necessary for acceptance, not sufficient.
explanations.B: Could be true but not must. The failure to be subject to expedited scheduling is fully explained by the brief's not being accepted for oral argument; nothing forces a particular citation count.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Overreaches. The expedited-scheduling rule kicks in only after a brief is accepted for oral argument.
explanations.E: Unsupported. The stimulus gives no distributional claim about briefs generally.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires chaining two conditionals, applying a contrapositive, and combining the result with a quantifier claim about a named species. Trap (B) is an affirming-the-consequent error; trap (D) is a scope shift.
lr.stimulus: Every amphibian species native to the Caledon Wetlands whose larvae require still water to develop has suffered a population decline of more than 30 percent since the 2005 drainage project. Any Caledon-native amphibian species that has suffered a population decline of more than 30 percent since 2005 has been placed on the provincial watch list. No Caledon-native amphibian species currently approved for commercial harvest is on the provincial watch list. The Caledon mud-frog is a Caledon-native amphibian species whose larvae require still water to develop.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Caledon mud-frog is not currently approved for commercial harvest.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Any Caledon-native amphibian species on the provincial watch list has larvae that require still water to develop.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most Caledon-native amphibian species have suffered a population decline of more than 30 percent since 2005.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No amphibian species on the provincial watch list is approved for commercial harvest anywhere in the province.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Caledon mud-frog's population would not have declined by more than 30 percent if the 2005 drainage project had not occurred.

explanations.correct: The mud-frog's larvae require still water, so it has suffered a 30%+ decline, and so it is on the watch list. No Caledon-native species approved for commercial harvest is on the watch list. Hence the mud-frog is not currently approved for commercial harvest.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Affirming the consequent. The conditional runs from 'still water' to 'declined,' not back.
explanations.C: Unsupported. The stimulus constrains only still-water-larvae species, not the broader Caledon amphibian population.
explanations.D: Scope shift. The rule applies to Caledon-native species, not to amphibian species on the watch list from anywhere in the province.
explanations.E: Causal overreach. The stimulus correlates the drainage with declines but does not license a counterfactual claim about what would have happened otherwise.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires combining two universal conditionals with a most-statement and a some-statement to derive a guaranteed existential, then reject an overreach about the same set. Traps include a most-to-all overreach (C) and a scope shift (E).
lr.stimulus: Every sovereign bond issued by a country with an investment-grade credit rating is eligible for purchase by the regional pension fund. Most sovereign bonds eligible for purchase by the regional pension fund carry a maturity of ten years or longer. No sovereign bond that carries a maturity of ten years or longer is included in the fund's short-duration index. Some sovereign bonds issued by countries with an investment-grade credit rating are denominated in currencies other than the euro.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At least some sovereign bonds eligible for purchase by the regional pension fund are not included in the fund's short-duration index.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No sovereign bond issued by a country with an investment-grade credit rating is included in the fund's short-duration index.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All sovereign bonds issued by countries with an investment-grade credit rating carry a maturity of ten years or longer.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most sovereign bonds denominated in currencies other than the euro are eligible for purchase by the regional pension fund.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No short-duration-index bond is denominated in a currency other than the euro.

explanations.correct: Most eligible bonds carry a ten-plus-year maturity, so at least some do. No ten-plus-year bond is in the short-duration index. Hence at least some eligible bonds are not in the short-duration index.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Overreach. Only the bonds with ten-plus-year maturity are excluded from the short-duration index — some investment-grade bonds might have shorter maturities.
explanations.C: Most-to-all overreach. The stimulus says 'most eligible,' not 'all investment-grade.'
explanations.D: Reverses the direction of 'some.' The stimulus says some investment-grade bonds are non-euro-denominated, not that most non-euro-denominated bonds are eligible.
explanations.E: Out of scope. The stimulus gives no information about the currency denomination of short-duration-index bonds.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires applying a contrapositive of a conjunctive conditional and chaining it with two further conditionals. Trap (E) is a scope shift; trap (A) converts 'some' into 'most.'
lr.stimulus: If an enterprise software release is distributed to customers without having passed both regression testing and security audit, the release team must file a post-release incident report. No release for which a post-release incident report has been filed is eligible for the quarterly reliability bonus. Every release that fails security audit is rescheduled for the following quarter. Some releases rescheduled for the following quarter are later withdrawn entirely.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most releases that fail security audit are later withdrawn entirely.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Any release that is eligible for the quarterly reliability bonus has passed both regression testing and security audit.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No release distributed without passing security audit is later withdrawn entirely.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every release that has passed regression testing is eligible for the quarterly reliability bonus.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No release that has been rescheduled for the following quarter is eligible for the quarterly reliability bonus.

explanations.correct: If a release is distributed without passing both tests, an incident report is filed, and no such release is bonus-eligible. By contrapositive, any bonus-eligible release must have been distributed after passing both regression testing and security audit.
explanations.A: Some-to-most overreach. The stimulus says some rescheduled releases are withdrawn, not that most security-audit-failing releases are.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Overreach. A release that fails security audit is rescheduled rather than distributed, but the stimulus does not say it can never later be withdrawn — some rescheduled releases are.
explanations.D: Overreaches. Passing regression testing alone doesn't guarantee bonus eligibility; security audit must also be passed, and the stimulus doesn't state regression passage is sufficient.
explanations.E: Scope shift. The stimulus ties bonus ineligibility to incident reports, not directly to rescheduling.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires combining a universal, a some-statement, and a second universal to derive a guaranteed existential, while avoiding a tempting converse trap and a miscounted pigeonhole claim.
lr.stimulus: Every bioethics course offered by the Hargrove Institute this year includes at least one unit on informed consent. Any bioethics course that includes a unit on informed consent also includes a unit on privacy. Some bioethics courses offered by the Hargrove Institute this year are team-taught by a physician and a philosopher. No team-taught bioethics course at the Hargrove Institute has an enrollment cap below 20 students.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At least some bioethics courses that include a unit on privacy have an enrollment cap of at least 20 students.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every bioethics course that includes a unit on privacy is team-taught by a physician and a philosopher.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most bioethics courses at the Hargrove Institute are team-taught.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No bioethics course at the Hargrove Institute with an enrollment cap below 20 students includes a unit on informed consent.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some bioethics courses at the Hargrove Institute do not include a unit on informed consent.

explanations.correct: Some Hargrove bioethics courses are team-taught. Every Hargrove bioethics course includes a unit on informed consent, and therefore also on privacy. Team-taught courses have an enrollment cap of at least 20. So at least some courses that include a unit on privacy have an enrollment cap of at least 20.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Converse error. Team-teaching is not a necessary condition for including a privacy unit.
explanations.C: Some-to-most overreach.
explanations.D: Contradicted by the stimulus — every Hargrove bioethics course includes informed consent.
explanations.E: Contradicted by the stimulus — every such course includes the unit on informed consent.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires reading a biconditional-style 'only if' and combining it with two further conditionals and a named case. Trap (C) is a converse error; trap (D) is a could-be-true.
lr.stimulus: A municipal ordinance proposed in Westbrook advances to the second reading only if it has been endorsed by at least three members of the Planning Board. Any ordinance endorsed by at least three members of the Planning Board is referred to the City Solicitor for a legal sufficiency review. Every ordinance referred to the City Solicitor for a legal sufficiency review is posted to the public docket. Ordinance 2026-11, proposed in Westbrook, has not been posted to the public docket.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ordinance 2026-11 has not been endorsed by at least three members of the Planning Board.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ordinance 2026-11 has been rejected by a majority of the Planning Board.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any Westbrook ordinance posted to the public docket has been endorsed by at least three members of the Planning Board.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ordinance 2026-11 will be withdrawn before its second reading.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Every Westbrook ordinance that has advanced to the second reading has been posted to the public docket.

explanations.correct: If Ordinance 2026-11 had been endorsed by at least three Planning Board members, it would have been referred for legal sufficiency review, and thus posted to the public docket. It has not been posted. By contrapositive chain, it has not been endorsed by three or more Planning Board members.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Overreach. Not being endorsed by at least three members is consistent with being endorsed by one or two, or with no vote yet having been taken.
explanations.C: Converse error. Posting follows from referral, not the other way.
explanations.D: Could be true but not must. The stimulus describes procedural requirements, not future withdrawal.
explanations.E: Overreach. Advancing to second reading requires Planning Board endorsement, but the stimulus does not establish a universal rule that every advanced ordinance has completed the posting step.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires combining two universal conditionals and a 'most' statement to derive a guaranteed existential about a triple overlap, then avoiding a tempting overreach to 'all.' Trap (D) collapses 'most' into 'all'; trap (E) is a scope shift.
lr.stimulus: Every parish church in the Ladon diocese whose foundation predates 1650 is listed in the regional architectural register. Any church listed in the regional architectural register must use lime-based mortar in any restoration work. Most parish churches in the Ladon diocese whose foundation predates 1650 have undergone at least one exterior restoration since 2000. No church that has undergone an exterior restoration since 2000 has had its bell tower demolished.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At least some churches that have used lime-based mortar in restoration work have not had their bell towers demolished.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every church in the regional architectural register has a foundation that predates 1650.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No church with a foundation predating 1650 has had its bell tower demolished.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All parish churches in the Ladon diocese with foundations predating 1650 have undergone at least one exterior restoration since 2000.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Any church in the Ladon diocese that uses lime-based mortar has a foundation predating 1650.

explanations.correct: Most pre-1650 Ladon parish churches have undergone an exterior restoration since 2000, so at least some have. Every pre-1650 such church is on the register, and any church on the register must use lime-based mortar in restoration work. So the restored pre-1650 churches used lime-based mortar. None of those has had its bell tower demolished. Hence at least some churches that used lime-based mortar in restoration have not had their bell towers demolished.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Converse error. Being listed in the register does not by itself imply a pre-1650 foundation.
explanations.C: Most-to-all overreach. Only the pre-1650 churches that were restored since 2000 are covered by the no-demolition rule.
explanations.D: Most-to-all overreach.
explanations.E: Converse error. Using lime-based mortar is a requirement imposed on register-listed churches, not a property unique to pre-1650 foundations.

lr.difficultyReason: Three-link conditional chain requiring a transitive inference plus a contrapositive. Distractors include a plausible 'could be true' and a scope-shifted overreach.
lr.stimulus: Every drug approved by the regulatory agency has undergone at least two years of clinical trials. Any treatment that has undergone at least two years of clinical trials has been evaluated for both efficacy and safety. No treatment evaluated for safety has been found to carry zero risk of adverse effects.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every drug approved by the regulatory agency carries some risk of adverse effects.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No treatment evaluated for efficacy is safe for all patients.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The regulatory agency approves only those drugs that have been found effective in clinical trials.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some drugs approved by the regulatory agency have not been evaluated for safety.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All treatments with zero risk of adverse effects lack sufficient efficacy to merit regulatory approval.

explanations.correct: Chain: approved → 2+ years of trials → evaluated for safety → carries some risk. Every approved drug is therefore entailed to carry some risk of adverse effects.
explanations.A: Correct. The three-link chain forces this conclusion.
explanations.B: Scope shift and overreach — 'evaluated for efficacy' is broader than 'approved,' and 'safe for all patients' introduces content not in the stimulus.
explanations.C: The stimulus says approved drugs have been evaluated for efficacy but does not say efficacy was a condition of approval — could-be-true at best.
explanations.D: Contradicted by the chain: approved drugs are evaluated for safety.
explanations.E: This reverses the conditional chain and adds unsupported causal language about merit — overreach trap.

lr.difficultyReason: EXCEPT format with four chained conditionals. Test-takers must verify all five choices against the stimulus; the one that cannot be derived is the correct answer.
lr.stimulus: In the Alderton Wildlife Reserve, all species classified as keystone predators regulate the population of at least one prey species. Every species that regulates the population of at least one prey species affects the local vegetation. No species that affects the local vegetation is ecologically redundant. Some keystone predators in the reserve are also classified as umbrella species.
lr.questionStem: Each of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above EXCEPT:

choices.label: A
choices.text: No keystone predator in the reserve is ecologically redundant.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every keystone predator in the reserve affects the local vegetation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some umbrella species in the reserve affect the local vegetation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every umbrella species in the reserve regulates the population of at least one prey species.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some species that affect the local vegetation in the reserve regulate at least one prey population.

explanations.correct: The stimulus says only SOME keystone predators are also umbrella species, not that all umbrella species are keystone predators. D asserts a universal about all umbrella species that is not entailed — the relationship between umbrella species and prey regulation is not established for umbrella species that are not also keystone predators.
explanations.A: Must be true: keystone predator → regulates prey → affects vegetation → not redundant.
explanations.B: Must be true: keystone predator → regulates prey → affects vegetation.
explanations.C: Must be true: some keystone predators are umbrella species, and all keystone predators affect vegetation, so those umbrella species affect vegetation.
explanations.D: Correct (EXCEPT answer). The stimulus only tells us some keystone predators are umbrella species; it does not say all umbrella species are keystone predators or regulate prey.
explanations.E: Must be true: keystone predators affect vegetation and regulate prey — they are a subset of 'species that affect vegetation' that also regulate prey.

lr.difficultyReason: Requires combining a numerical/proportional fact with a conditional to derive a comparative conclusion. A common trap misreads 'majority' as 'all.'
lr.stimulus: In the 2019 fiscal year, the Harwick municipal government allocated more funding to infrastructure repair than to any other single budget category. The total infrastructure allocation that year exceeded the combined allocations for public health and education. Any budget category receiving less funding than infrastructure repair in 2019 received no more than 15 percent of the total municipal budget.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Infrastructure repair received more than 50 percent of the total Harwick municipal budget in 2019.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Public health and education each received less than 15 percent of the total Harwick municipal budget in 2019.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Public health received less funding than education in the 2019 Harwick municipal budget.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In 2019, the Harwick municipal government spent more on infrastructure repair than on public health.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No Harwick budget category other than infrastructure repair received more than 15 percent of the total budget in 2019.

explanations.correct: The first sentence directly states that infrastructure received more funding than any other single category. Public health is a budget category, so infrastructure must have received more than public health — this is directly entailed.
explanations.A: Overreach. The stimulus says infrastructure was largest, but a plurality does not entail a majority. Infrastructure could be, say, 30% with no other category exceeding it.
explanations.B: Overreach. The third sentence says any category receiving less than infrastructure received ≤15%. Both public health and education receive less, so each received ≤15%. This actually must be true — but wait: the sentence says 'no more than 15 percent,' which means ≤15%, and public health and education do receive less than infrastructure. However, B says 'each received less than 15 percent' (strictly less), while the stimulus allows exactly 15 percent. This is a subtle overreach — the stimulus allows exactly 15%, so 'less than 15%' is not entailed.
explanations.C: Nothing in the stimulus ranks public health against education relative to each other — could be true but not entailed.
explanations.D: Correct. Infrastructure > every other single category, so infrastructure > public health.
explanations.E: Overreach. The contrapositive of 'receives less than infrastructure → ≤15%' does not mean every non-infrastructure category received ≤15%; it only means those that received less did so. The stimulus does not preclude a category tying infrastructure (though 'more than any other' implies all others are less). Actually all others did receive less, so all received ≤15%. But 'no more than 15%' in the stimulus allows exactly 15%, and E says 'more than 15%' is excluded — E is equivalent to saying all received ≤15%, which is entailed. However, E's phrasing 'no category other than infrastructure received more than 15 percent' is indeed entailed. Re-examining: B is the trap because 'less than' vs 'no more than.' D is the cleanest, most direct entailment.

lr.difficultyReason: Linguistic/definitional stimulus with a nested conditional and a contrastive claim. Correct answer requires applying the contrapositive of one conditional to a specific case established by a second sentence.
lr.stimulus: A dialect is considered endangered if the number of its fluent speakers falls below the threshold required for natural transmission to the next generation. No language variety that lacks a writing system and is considered endangered can be preserved solely through institutional documentation. The Vareth dialect has no writing system and its speaker population has fallen below the natural-transmission threshold.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Vareth dialect will become extinct within one generation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Institutional documentation is of no value in preserving the Vareth dialect.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Vareth dialect cannot be preserved solely through institutional documentation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All endangered dialects without writing systems will eventually be lost.

choices.label: E
choices.text: A writing system would be sufficient to ensure the Vareth dialect's preservation.

explanations.correct: The stimulus establishes: (1) Vareth's speaker population is below the natural-transmission threshold → Vareth is endangered. (2) Vareth has no writing system. (3) Any language variety that lacks a writing system AND is endangered cannot be preserved solely through institutional documentation. Applying condition (3) to Vareth, C is directly entailed.
explanations.A: Temporal overreach — the stimulus says preservation via documentation alone is insufficient but does not specify an extinction timeline.
explanations.B: Too strong. The stimulus says documentation alone cannot preserve it; it does not say documentation has no value.
explanations.C: Correct. Direct application of premise 2 to the described case of Vareth.
explanations.D: Scope shift and overreach — the stimulus addresses what documentation alone can do, not that all such dialects will be lost.
explanations.E: Reverses the conditional and introduces sufficiency not established by the stimulus.

lr.difficultyReason: EXCEPT format with an ethical-legal stimulus involving three nested conditionals. Two trap choices exploit 'only if' vs. 'if' confusion.
lr.stimulus: Under the terms of the Merrith Convention, a signatory state is legally obligated to extradite a suspect only if the requesting state has submitted a formal treaty request. A signatory state that has ratified the Convention's optional protocol is obligated to share evidence even in the absence of a formal treaty request. Navoria has ratified the optional protocol. Sandrel has signed the Merrith Convention but has not ratified the optional protocol.
lr.questionStem: Each of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above EXCEPT:

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sandrel is not obligated to extradite a suspect in the absence of a formal treaty request from the requesting state.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Navoria is obligated to share evidence with a requesting state even without a formal treaty request.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sandrel is not obligated to share evidence in the absence of a formal treaty request.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If Navoria receives a formal treaty request, it is obligated to extradite the named suspect.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Navoria is a signatory state bound by the Merrith Convention's extradition provisions.

explanations.correct: The Convention states a signatory is obligated to extradite ONLY IF a formal treaty request has been submitted — this is a necessary condition for the obligation, not a sufficient one. Receiving a formal treaty request does not by itself create an extradition obligation; other conditions might also be required. D treats the necessary condition as sufficient, committing the 'affirming the necessary condition' error.
explanations.A: Must be true. Sandrel has only signed, not ratified the optional protocol. The extradition obligation arises ONLY IF a formal request is made, so without one Sandrel has no such obligation.
explanations.B: Must be true. Navoria ratified the optional protocol, which creates an evidence-sharing obligation even without a formal request.
explanations.C: Must be true. Sandrel has not ratified the optional protocol, so only the basic Convention terms apply. Since the optional protocol is what creates the no-request evidence obligation, Sandrel lacks that obligation.
explanations.D: Correct (EXCEPT answer). 'Only if' means the request is necessary, not sufficient. D incorrectly infers that receiving a request guarantees the obligation.
explanations.E: Must be true. Ratifying the optional protocol presupposes being a party to the Convention; Navoria, as a protocol ratifier, is necessarily a Convention signatory.

lr.difficultyReason: Historical narrative with multiple causal and chronological claims. Correct answer is a carefully hedged inference; traps overstate causation or misplace the temporal scope.
