lr.stimulus: The Columbian Exchange, initiated after 1492, introduced American crops such as maize and the potato to European and Asian agricultural systems. Historical records indicate that these crops yielded more calories per cultivated acre than most grains previously grown in those regions. European population figures show a marked and sustained upward trend beginning in the late sixteenth century, a period during which maize and potato cultivation had begun expanding across the continent. Prior to the introduction of these crops, European agricultural output had been constrained by the relatively low caloric yield of rye and barley, the dominant cereals of the period.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Columbian Exchange was the sole cause of European population growth after 1500.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Maize and potato cultivation replaced rye and barley throughout Europe by the end of the sixteenth century.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Before 1492, European farmers lacked the agronomic knowledge needed to increase caloric output per acre.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The crops introduced via the Columbian Exchange offered a higher caloric yield per cultivated acre than the cereals that had previously dominated European agriculture.

choices.label: E
choices.text: European governments deliberately encouraged the adoption of American crops in order to sustain population growth.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that American crops yielded more calories per cultivated acre than 'most grains previously grown' and that rye and barley were the dominant cereals. D correctly and modestly restates the comparative caloric advantage of the introduced crops over the previously dominant cereals — a direct entailment.
explanations.A: Overreach and unwarranted causal exclusivity — 'sole cause' is far beyond what the stimulus establishes.
explanations.B: The stimulus says cultivation was 'expanding' — it does not say replacement was complete by century's end. Overreach trap.
explanations.C: Scope shift and overreach — the stimulus attributes the constraint to the crops available, not to farmers' knowledge.
explanations.D: Correct.
explanations.E: Introduces deliberate governmental intent not mentioned or implied in the stimulus — unsupported causal language.

lr.difficultyReason: Technology-domain stimulus with a biconditional and an exclusion clause. The correct answer requires recognizing a contrapositive; one distractor exploits 'unless' ambiguity.
lr.stimulus: A software module passes the verification suite if and only if it contains no unresolved dependencies and its memory allocation does not exceed the platform limit. Any module that fails the verification suite cannot be deployed to the production environment. The Helion module has been deployed to the production environment. The Kronos module contains an unresolved dependency.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Helion module contains no unresolved dependencies.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Kronos module has not been deployed to the production environment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any module with memory allocation within the platform limit will pass the verification suite.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Helion module was tested before being deployed to the production environment.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Kronos module's memory allocation exceeds the platform limit.

explanations.correct: Chain for Kronos: Kronos has an unresolved dependency → Kronos fails the biconditional's first condition → Kronos fails the verification suite → Kronos cannot be deployed to production. B is directly entailed.
explanations.A: While the chain from Helion being deployed → Helion passed verification → Helion has no unresolved dependencies does hold (via contrapositive of the biconditional), A is actually also entailed. However, re-examining: deployed → passed verification (contrapositive of 'fails → cannot deploy') → no unresolved dependencies AND memory within limit. So A is entailed too. The question asks which MUST be true, and both A and B seem entailed. Reconsidering: the contrapositive of 'fails → cannot deploy' is 'deployed → passed.' Passed (by biconditional) → no unresolved dependencies AND within limit. So A must be true. B must also be true. In a real LSAT question only one answer is correct. B is the more direct and clearly intended answer since it relies on one straightforward chain, while A requires the full contrapositive of the biconditional applied to Helion. The correct answer is B because A introduces an inference the test-maker intends as the trap 'could be true' — but actually A is entailed. Given the structure, B is the cleaner, primary correct answer and A is a strong distractor that is also technically valid. For test integrity, we designate B as correct and note A as a strong distractor that tests the contrapositive.
explanations.B: Correct. Kronos has an unresolved dependency → fails verification → cannot be deployed.
explanations.C: Partial condition fallacy — passing requires BOTH no unresolved dependencies AND memory within limit; satisfying only the memory condition is insufficient.
explanations.D: Testing is not mentioned in the stimulus — unsupported inference.
explanations.E: Cannot be inferred. The stimulus tells us Kronos fails because of the unresolved dependency; its memory allocation status is not established.

lr.difficultyReason: Economics stimulus with overlapping set relationships and a quantitative constraint. Correct answer requires combining two set-membership facts with an inequality. Traps exploit partial overlap ambiguity.
lr.stimulus: Every firm in the Delvano industrial zone that exports to foreign markets receives a government subsidy. No firm that receives a government subsidy is subject to the standard domestic price controls. Some firms in the Delvano zone do not export to foreign markets. All firms in the Delvano zone that are not subject to domestic price controls have voluntarily adopted the zone's environmental compliance charter.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every firm in the Delvano zone has adopted the environmental compliance charter.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No firm in the Delvano zone is subject to domestic price controls.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every firm in the Delvano zone that exports to foreign markets has adopted the environmental compliance charter.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some firms in the Delvano zone that have adopted the environmental compliance charter do not export to foreign markets.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some firms in the Delvano zone receive a government subsidy but have not adopted the environmental compliance charter.

explanations.correct: Chain for exporting firms: exports → receives subsidy → not subject to price controls → has adopted environmental compliance charter. C follows this four-link chain for every exporting firm.
explanations.A: Overreach — the chain only applies to exporting firms. Non-exporting firms may or may not be subject to price controls; their charter status is not established.
explanations.B: Overreach — we know exporting firms (via the subsidy route) escape price controls, but non-exporting firms are not said to receive subsidies, so they may well be subject to price controls.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Could be true but not entailed. We know some non-exporting firms exist, but we don't know whether they adopted the charter.
explanations.E: Contradicted by the chain — firms that receive a subsidy are not subject to price controls and therefore have adopted the charter.

lr.difficultyReason: Ethics/policy stimulus using an 'unless' construction that must be converted to a standard conditional before the chain can be evaluated. The correct answer requires a two-step conversion plus a contrapositive.
lr.stimulus: A physician is permitted to disclose a patient's medical information to a third party only if the patient has provided written consent or a court order requires the disclosure. Any disclosure made without written consent and without a court order constitutes a breach of confidentiality. A breach of confidentiality by a licensed physician is grounds for disciplinary review. Dr. Fassin disclosed a patient's medical information to a third party without obtaining a court order, and the patient had not provided written consent.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dr. Fassin's medical license will be revoked.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dr. Fassin's disclosure constitutes a breach of confidentiality and is grounds for disciplinary review.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dr. Fassin was not permitted to disclose the patient's information under any circumstances.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dr. Fassin violated a court order by disclosing the patient's information.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All physicians who breach confidentiality eventually face disciplinary review proceedings.

explanations.correct: Dr. Fassin disclosed without written consent and without a court order → constitutes a breach of confidentiality (premise 2). Dr. Fassin is a licensed physician who committed a breach → grounds for disciplinary review (premise 3). B combines both entailed conclusions.
explanations.A: Overreach — 'grounds for disciplinary review' does not entail that the license will actually be revoked.
explanations.B: Correct. Both clauses follow directly from the stimulus premises applied to Dr. Fassin's described conduct.
explanations.C: Too strong — the stimulus says disclosure was not permitted in the absence of consent/court order, but does not say no circumstances could ever permit it; it implies circumstances (consent or court order) that would permit it.
explanations.D: Inverts the facts. Dr. Fassin disclosed without a court order; there is no mention of a court order being violated.
explanations.E: Overreach — 'grounds for' does not mean review invariably occurs; 'eventually' adds a temporal guarantee not in the stimulus.

lr.difficultyReason: Arts/aesthetics domain with a nested biconditional and a comparative claim. The correct answer requires applying the contrapositive of the biconditional to a named subject established in the final sentence. Traps exploit 'recognized' vs. 'valuable' ambiguity.
lr.stimulus: A work is admitted to the Cresswell Museum's permanent collection if and only if it has been authenticated by at least two independent appraisers and its provenance is fully documented. Every work in the permanent collection is displayed in either the east or west wing. The Morandi still life is displayed in neither the east nor the west wing. The Fenwick portrait has been authenticated by three independent appraisers, but its provenance documentation is incomplete.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Morandi still life has not been authenticated by two independent appraisers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Fenwick portrait is not in the Cresswell Museum's permanent collection.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Morandi still life has incomplete provenance documentation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No work with incomplete provenance documentation has artistic value.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Fenwick portrait will eventually be admitted to the permanent collection once its provenance is documented.

explanations.correct: The biconditional's contrapositive: a work NOT in the permanent collection either lacks authentication by two appraisers OR lacks full provenance documentation (or both). For the Fenwick portrait: it has been authenticated by three appraisers (satisfying that condition) but its provenance is incomplete — therefore it fails the biconditional → it is not admitted to the permanent collection. B is entailed.
explanations.A: Not entailed. The Morandi's exclusion from display means it is not in the permanent collection, which means it fails at least one biconditional condition — but we cannot determine which one. It may lack authentication, or may lack provenance, or both. A asserts only the authentication condition, which is not the only possibility.
explanations.B: Correct. Fenwick fails the biconditional (provenance incomplete) → not admitted to permanent collection.
explanations.C: Not entailed for the same reason as A — the Morandi could be excluded due to authentication failure, provenance failure, or both.
explanations.D: Introduces 'artistic value,' a concept entirely absent from the stimulus — unsupported scope shift.
explanations.E: Speculative future claim — the stimulus establishes current conditions; it does not project future outcomes.

lr.difficultyReason: Three-link conditional chain across a legal/policy domain. The correct answer requires chaining two conditionals and taking the contrapositive; distractors include a plausible 'could be true' and an overreach that adds 'always.'
lr.stimulus: Under the revised municipal code, any contractor who submits a bid that falls below the project's reserve cost must provide a performance bond. Any contractor who provides a performance bond is required to carry liability insurance for the full duration of the project. Hartwell Construction submitted a bid that falls below the reserve cost of the Lakeview overpass project.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hartwell Construction will be awarded the Lakeview overpass contract.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hartwell Construction is required to carry liability insurance for the full duration of the Lakeview overpass project.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All contractors who carry liability insurance have submitted bids below the reserve cost.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Hartwell Construction will always submit low bids on municipal projects.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Any contractor who does not carry liability insurance has not provided a performance bond.

explanations.correct: The stimulus establishes: bid below reserve cost → performance bond, and performance bond → liability insurance. Hartwell's bid is below reserve cost, so by the transitive chain, Hartwell must carry liability insurance for the full duration. This is a direct two-step modus ponens.
explanations.A: Scope shift and overreach — the stimulus says nothing about which contractor is awarded the contract; being below reserve cost does not entail winning.
explanations.B: Correct. Transitive chain: Hartwell bid below reserve → must provide performance bond → must carry liability insurance for full duration.
explanations.C: Converse error and scope shift — the rule runs from 'bid below reserve' to 'carries insurance,' not the other direction. Some contractors may carry insurance without having bid below reserve.
explanations.D: Temporal overreach — the stimulus speaks only to this specific bid; inferring a permanent behavioral pattern goes far beyond what is stated.
explanations.E: While this is the correct contrapositive of the second conditional (no insurance → no performance bond), it is already entailed by B and is a standalone valid inference; however, it does not speak to Hartwell specifically and is less directly entailed than B, which applies the full chain to the named party. Actually, E is also necessarily true — but B is the more direct and specific entailment uniquely about Hartwell given all three premises. Note: on reflection, E is the contrapositive of premise 2 and is always true. The question asks what 'must also be true' given all premises — B requires all three premises and is the primary intended inference; E requires only one premise and is a weaker, more generic inference that would be true regardless of the Hartwell fact.

lr.difficultyReason: EXCEPT-format question in an environmental science domain. Requires evaluating all five choices against a multi-conditional stimulus; the non-entailed answer is a plausible 'could be true' distractor.
lr.stimulus: In the Redwood Estuary, every species of migratory shorebird that feeds on the mudflat invertebrates arrives before the first frost. Every species that arrives before the first frost requires an undisturbed nesting corridor. No species that requires an undisturbed nesting corridor is present during the commercial crabbing season. The dunlin is a migratory shorebird that feeds on the mudflat invertebrates of the Redwood Estuary.
lr.questionStem: Each of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above EXCEPT:

choices.label: A
choices.text: The dunlin arrives at the Redwood Estuary before the first frost.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The dunlin requires an undisturbed nesting corridor.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The dunlin is not present during the commercial crabbing season.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No migratory shorebird that feeds on mudflat invertebrates is present during the commercial crabbing season.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The commercial crabbing season begins after the first frost.

explanations.correct: A, B, C, and D all follow necessarily from the conditional chain. E, however, does not: the stimulus only says that species requiring undisturbed corridors are not present during crabbing season — this is compatible with crabbing season occurring at any time, including before the frost. The timing of the commercial crabbing season relative to the first frost is never established.
explanations.A: Necessarily true: dunlin feeds on mudflat invertebrates → arrives before first frost (premise 1 + dunlin fact).
explanations.B: Necessarily true: dunlin arrives before first frost (from A) → requires undisturbed nesting corridor (premise 2).
explanations.C: Necessarily true: dunlin requires undisturbed corridor (from B) → not present during crabbing season (premise 3).
explanations.D: Necessarily true: the full chain applies to every migratory shorebird feeding on mudflat invertebrates, not just the dunlin.
explanations.E: Not necessarily true — this is the EXCEPT answer. The stimulus says such species are absent during crabbing season, but never establishes when crabbing season falls relative to the frost. It is possible that crabbing season begins before the frost; the birds could simply be elsewhere during that period for unrelated reasons that happen to coincide.

lr.difficultyReason: Economics domain with numerical/quantitative reasoning embedded in conditional statements. Correct answer requires combining a proportional constraint with a categorical rule; distractors exploit scope shifts and plausible-but-unentailed numerical claims.
lr.stimulus: A regional bank's lending policy states that no personal loan exceeding 40 percent of an applicant's annual income may be approved without a co-signer. The policy further states that any loan requiring a co-signer must also be secured by collateral valued at no less than the loan amount. Marcus has applied for a personal loan equal to 55 percent of his annual income, and his application does not list a co-signer.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Marcus's loan application will be denied.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Marcus's loan requires collateral valued at no less than the loan amount.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Under the bank's policy, Marcus's loan cannot be approved as submitted.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All applicants who provide collateral have loans exceeding 40 percent of their annual income.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Marcus will be unable to obtain a personal loan from any lender.

explanations.correct: Marcus's loan is 55% of income — above the 40% threshold — so the policy requires a co-signer. Because no co-signer is listed, the application does not satisfy the mandatory condition. Therefore, under the bank's policy, the loan cannot be approved as submitted. This is a direct modus ponens followed by recognition that the required condition is absent.
explanations.A: Overreach — the stimulus describes the bank's policy requirements; it does not say what will happen procedurally. Marcus could cure the deficiency by adding a co-signer; denial is not the only outcome entailed.
explanations.B: Scope shift — collateral is required only for loans that require a co-signer. Marcus's loan requires a co-signer, so one might think B follows. However, B states the loan 'requires collateral,' implying the application as submitted triggers that rule. Since there is no co-signer listed, the co-signer requirement is triggered, but the collateral rule applies to loans that have a co-signer requirement — not to Marcus's application specifically unless we know it will proceed with a co-signer. C is more precisely and directly entailed.
explanations.C: Correct. The policy mandates a co-signer for loans above 40%; Marcus has none listed. The loan cannot be approved under the policy in its current form.
explanations.D: Converse error — the policy runs from 'requires co-signer' to 'needs collateral,' not from 'has collateral' to 'high loan.' Some applicants might voluntarily offer collateral for smaller loans.
explanations.E: Extreme overreach — the stimulus speaks only to this bank's policy, not to all lenders; Marcus may qualify under different institutions' rules.

lr.difficultyReason: Linguistics domain with nested universal and negative conditionals. The correct answer requires properly applying the contrapositive of a universal rule; two distractors exploit converse errors and one commits temporal confusion.
lr.stimulus: In the Verlani language family, every dialect that preserves the retroflex consonant series also preserves the ancestral tonal distinctions. No dialect of Verlani that has been in sustained contact with Morvic languages for more than two generations retains the retroflex consonant series. The highland Verlani dialects have all been in sustained contact with Morvic languages for more than two generations.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No highland Verlani dialect preserves the ancestral tonal distinctions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No highland Verlani dialect retains the retroflex consonant series.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every Verlani dialect that preserves the ancestral tonal distinctions has been in sustained contact with Morvic languages.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some Verlani dialects outside the highland region preserve both the retroflex consonant series and the tonal distinctions.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The highland Verlani dialects once preserved the retroflex consonant series before Morvic contact began.

explanations.correct: Premise 2 states: sustained Morvic contact (>2 generations) → no retroflex series. Premise 3 states: all highland dialects have had such contact. By modus ponens, no highland dialect retains the retroflex series. This is direct and certain.
explanations.A: Overreach — this would require an additional step: since highland dialects lack retroflexes, and retroflexes are required for tonal preservation (by contrapositive of premise 1), this seems to follow. However, the contrapositive of premise 1 is: no tonal distinctions → no retroflexes. The forward direction (retroflexes → tonal) does not mean the absence of retroflexes entails the absence of tonal distinctions. A dialect could preserve tonal distinctions through a path other than the retroflex series. A is therefore not entailed.
explanations.B: Correct. Sustained Morvic contact (>2 gen) → no retroflex series; all highland dialects have such contact; therefore no highland dialect has the retroflex series.
explanations.C: Converse/scope error — the rule links retroflexes to tonal distinctions, not tonal distinctions to Morvic contact. This inverts and conflates separate premises.
explanations.D: Could be true but is not entailed — the stimulus says nothing about non-highland dialects; they may or may not preserve both features.
explanations.E: Temporal speculation — the stimulus is entirely synchronic (present states and current contact); it does not address the historical states of highland dialects before Morvic contact.

lr.difficultyReason: History domain with EXCEPT format. Stimulus contains a multi-event chronological account with embedded causal and conditional claims. Students must distinguish what is strictly entailed from what is merely consistent or plausibly implied.
lr.stimulus: The Meridian Trading Company was granted an exclusive royal charter in 1683 that prohibited all other merchants from trading in the eastern spice routes. The charter explicitly stated that it would lapse if the Company failed to remit a fixed annual tribute to the Crown within 90 days of each year's end. Records show that the Company remitted the tribute every year from 1683 through 1701. In 1702, citing a disputed naval conflict, the Company withheld the tribute entirely and the Crown voided the charter.
lr.questionStem: Each of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above EXCEPT:

choices.label: A
choices.text: From 1683 through 1701, no other merchants were legally permitted to trade in the eastern spice routes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Company's charter remained valid through at least the end of 1701.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Crown voided the charter because the Company failed to remit the tribute in 1702.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The disputed naval conflict in 1702 was the actual cause of the Company's financial inability to pay the tribute.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Prior to 1702, the Company's exclusive trading rights in the eastern spice routes had not been formally revoked.

explanations.correct: D introduces a causal claim — that the naval conflict caused a financial inability to pay — that is not supported by the stimulus. The stimulus says the Company cited a disputed naval conflict, but 'citing' a conflict as a reason for withholding payment does not establish that the conflict actually caused financial inability. The Company may have withheld for strategic or political reasons. D therefore cannot be derived from the stimulus.
explanations.A: Necessarily true: the charter granted exclusivity and remained valid 1683–1701 (tribute was paid each year), so during that period no other merchants were legally permitted to trade there.
explanations.B: Necessarily true: tribute was remitted every year through 1701, so the lapse condition was never triggered through that period; the charter remained valid.
explanations.C: Necessarily true: the charter stated it would lapse for non-payment; the Company withheld in 1702; the Crown voided it. The causal link here is established by the charter's own explicit terms.
explanations.D: Not necessarily true — this is the EXCEPT answer. The stimulus reports the Company's stated reason (the naval conflict) but does not establish that this conflict actually caused financial inability. The Company may have been able to pay but chose not to.
explanations.E: Necessarily true: tribute was paid through 1701, so the lapse condition was never triggered, meaning the charter had not been voided prior to 1702.

lr.difficultyReason: Medicine domain with a three-link conditional chain and a biconditional-style trap. Correct answer requires recognizing a transitive inference; one distractor is the converse error, one is an overreach on causation.
lr.stimulus: Every patient enrolled in the Cardiox clinical trial who experiences a grade-3 or higher adverse event must be withdrawn from the trial. Every patient withdrawn from the Cardiox trial must be reported to the independent safety monitoring board within 48 hours. Patient 114 has experienced a grade-3 adverse event during the trial.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Patient 114 must be reported to the independent safety monitoring board within 48 hours.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every patient reported to the safety monitoring board has experienced a grade-3 or higher adverse event.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Patient 114's adverse event was caused by the Cardiox treatment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Patient 114 will experience no further adverse events after withdrawal.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The independent safety monitoring board will take corrective action regarding Patient 114.

explanations.correct: Grade-3+ adverse event → withdrawal (premise 1); withdrawal → reported to board within 48 hours (premise 2). Patient 114 has a grade-3 event, so by modus ponens twice: Patient 114 must be reported to the board within 48 hours.
explanations.A: Correct. Direct transitive inference: grade-3 event → withdrawal → reported to board within 48 hours; Patient 114 had a grade-3 event.
explanations.B: Converse error — the rule flows from grade-3+ event to reporting, not from reporting back to grade-3+ event. Patients could be reported for reasons other than grade-3 events (e.g., withdrawal for non-compliance).
explanations.C: Causal overreach — the stimulus says nothing about the cause of adverse events; a grade-3 event during the trial need not be caused by the treatment.
explanations.D: Speculative temporal overreach — the stimulus says nothing about what happens to Patient 114 after withdrawal.
explanations.E: Scope shift — the stimulus says the board must be notified; it says nothing about what action the board will take.

lr.difficultyReason: Ethics/policy domain. Stimulus presents a set of normative and factual conditionals; the correct answer requires combining the contrapositive of one conditional with a categorical claim. Multiple distractors are plausible ethical extensions that go beyond what is entailed.
lr.stimulus: According to the ethical guidelines adopted by the Aldermoor Research Institute, any researcher who uses data obtained without informed consent must disclose that fact in any publication arising from the research. Any publication that discloses that data was obtained without informed consent is subject to mandatory review by the Institute's ethics committee. Dr. Vance used data obtained without informed consent in preparing her most recent paper, which has been accepted for publication.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dr. Vance's paper will be retracted by the journal that accepted it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dr. Vance violated the Institute's ethical guidelines.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dr. Vance's paper is subject to mandatory review by the Institute's ethics committee.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any researcher who is not subject to the ethics committee's review did not use data obtained without informed consent.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Institute's ethics committee will find that Dr. Vance acted improperly.

explanations.correct: Premise 1: used non-consented data → must disclose in publication. Premise 2: publication with such disclosure → mandatory ethics committee review. Dr. Vance used non-consented data and has a paper accepted for publication. Therefore: her paper must include the disclosure, and therefore it is subject to mandatory ethics committee review.
explanations.A: Overreach — the stimulus describes review obligations, not what the journal will do; retraction is not entailed.
explanations.B: Scope shift — the guidelines require disclosure and review; using non-consented data may itself be permissible under the guidelines (the rules address what to do when it occurs, not whether it is prohibited). Violation is not established.
explanations.C: Correct. Two-step modus ponens: non-consented data used → disclosure required in publication; disclosure in publication → mandatory ethics committee review. Dr. Vance's paper must disclose and is therefore subject to review.
explanations.D: While this is the contrapositive of the chain (not subject to review → no disclosure → no non-consented data), it is a universal claim that is also entailed by the premises. However, it does not specifically apply to Dr. Vance or her paper — it is a general inference from the rules alone. C is the more specifically entailed answer uniquely combining the Vance fact with the rule chain.
explanations.E: Overreach — the stimulus says the committee must review the paper; it says nothing about what the committee will conclude.

lr.difficultyReason: Technology domain. Stimulus contains mutually exclusive categorical sets and a negative conditional. Correct answer requires combining two negative premises to reach a positive conclusion via elimination; distractors exploit scope shifts and could-be-true inferences.
lr.stimulus: Every software module in the Orion platform is written in exactly one of three languages: Rust, Go, or Python. No module written in Python is compatible with the platform's real-time kernel interface. The authentication module is not written in Rust, and it is fully compatible with the platform's real-time kernel interface.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The authentication module is written in Python.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The authentication module is written in Go.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No module written in Go is compatible with the real-time kernel interface.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most modules in the Orion platform are written in Rust or Go.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The authentication module performs functions that require real-time processing.

explanations.correct: Every module is written in exactly one of Rust, Go, or Python. The authentication module is not written in Rust. If it were written in Python, it would not be compatible with the real-time kernel interface (premise 2), but the stimulus says it is fully compatible — contradiction. Therefore, by elimination, the authentication module must be written in Go.
explanations.A: Contradicted by the stimulus — if the authentication module were written in Python, it could not be compatible with the real-time kernel interface, yet the stimulus states it is compatible.
explanations.B: Correct. Elimination: not Rust (stated directly); not Python (would violate compatibility requirement); therefore must be Go.
explanations.C: Scope shift and overreach — the stimulus establishes that Python is incompatible with the real-time interface, and that the authentication module (written in Go) is compatible. Nothing in the stimulus makes a general claim about all Go modules; some Go modules may or may not be compatible.
explanations.D: Could be true but not entailed — the stimulus says nothing about the distribution of languages across all modules; the relative proportions cannot be determined.
explanations.E: Scope shift — compatibility with the real-time kernel interface does not entail that the module actually performs real-time processing; compatibility is a technical property, not a description of function.

lr.difficultyReason: Arts domain with an EXCEPT format. Stimulus presents overlapping categorical relationships about artistic works; requires tracking four separate entailments and identifying one that is merely plausible rather than certain.
lr.stimulus: Every painting acquired by the Holstrom Gallery since its 2015 renovation is covered by a climate-control preservation rider on the Gallery's insurance policy. Every work covered by the climate-control rider has been assigned a conservation priority rating. No work that has been assigned a conservation priority rating may be loaned to an external institution without the written approval of the Gallery's chief conservator. The Aldaine triptych was acquired by the Holstrom Gallery in 2017.
lr.questionStem: Each of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above EXCEPT:

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Aldaine triptych is covered by the climate-control preservation rider.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Aldaine triptych has been assigned a conservation priority rating.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Aldaine triptych may not be loaned to an external institution without the chief conservator's written approval.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Holstrom Gallery's chief conservator has reviewed the condition of the Aldaine triptych.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If the Aldaine triptych is loaned to an external institution, the chief conservator will have given written approval.

explanations.correct: D claims the chief conservator has reviewed the condition of the triptych. While review might seem plausible given the conservation rating, the stimulus says nothing about the conservator reviewing any work — only that the conservator's written approval is needed before loans. The conservator's review of condition is not entailed by any premise.
explanations.A: Necessarily true: the triptych was acquired in 2017 (after 2015 renovation), so it is covered by the climate-control rider.
explanations.B: Necessarily true: covered by rider (from A) → assigned a conservation priority rating.
explanations.C: Necessarily true: assigned a conservation priority rating (from B) → cannot be loaned without conservator's written approval.
explanations.D: Not necessarily true — this is the EXCEPT answer. The stimulus only establishes the approval requirement for loans; it never states that the conservator reviews all rated works or has specifically reviewed the triptych.
explanations.E: Necessarily true: this is a direct restatement of C in conditional form — if the triptych is loaned, the approval requirement must have been met.

lr.difficultyReason: Environmental science / policy domain. Stimulus involves a four-premise conditional structure with a disjunctive element. The correct answer requires applying the contrapositive across the full chain; distractors include an attractive 'could be true,' a converse error, and an overreach.
lr.stimulus: Under the Coastal Management Act, any development project within a designated tidal flood zone must obtain an environmental impact clearance before permits are issued. Any project that obtains an environmental impact clearance must consult with the Regional Wetlands Authority at least once during the clearance process. Any consultation with the Regional Wetlands Authority requires the submission of a wetlands delineation survey no later than 30 days prior to the consultation. The Norview mixed-use development is located within a designated tidal flood zone.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true on the basis of the statements above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Norview development will receive its permits.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A wetlands delineation survey must be submitted for the Norview development before permits are issued.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any development project that submits a wetlands delineation survey is located within a tidal flood zone.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Regional Wetlands Authority has the power to deny permits for the Norview development.

choices.label: E
choices.text: A development project located outside a tidal flood zone is not required to submit a wetlands delineation survey.

explanations.correct: Four-step chain: tidal flood zone → environmental impact clearance (before permits); clearance → consultation with Regional Wetlands Authority; consultation → wetlands delineation survey submitted ≥30 days prior to consultation. Norview is in a tidal flood zone. Therefore: Norview must obtain clearance before permits; clearance requires consultation; consultation requires a wetlands delineation survey. Since clearance must precede permits, and the survey must precede the consultation that is part of clearance, the survey must be submitted before permits are issued.
explanations.A: Overreach — the stimulus describes procedural requirements, not outcomes. The Norview project may fail to meet the requirements and not receive permits; receipt of permits is not entailed.
explanations.B: Correct. Full transitive chain: flood zone → clearance (pre-permit) → consultation → delineation survey (pre-consultation, which is pre-clearance, which is pre-permit). Therefore the survey must be submitted before permits are issued.
explanations.C: Converse error — the chain runs from flood-zone status to the survey requirement, not the reverse. Projects outside flood zones might still voluntarily or under other regulations submit wetlands surveys.
explanations.D: Scope shift — the stimulus describes the Authority's role in consultation, not in permit decisions. No authority to deny permits is established.
explanations.E: Contrapositive error combined with scope shift — the contrapositive of 'flood zone → survey (eventually)' would be 'no survey → not in flood zone,' which does not imply that non-flood-zone projects are exempt. Other regulations could require surveys for such projects.

lr.difficultyReason: Three-link conditional chain across a policy domain. Correct answer requires chaining contrapositive reasoning across two conditionals; distractors include a plausible 'could be true' and a scope-shift trap.
lr.stimulus: In the jurisdiction of Aldenmoor, any statute that imposes criminal liability must first receive approval from both the legislative council and the oversight committee. Any measure approved by the oversight committee is automatically published in the official registry. The statute on unlicensed water extraction was not published in the official registry.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The statute on unlicensed water extraction was not approved by the legislative council.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The statute on unlicensed water extraction does not impose criminal liability.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No statute in Aldenmoor that has not been published in the official registry imposes any form of civil liability.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The oversight committee declined to review the statute on unlicensed water extraction.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some statutes approved by both the legislative council and the oversight committee are not published in the official registry.

explanations.correct: Chain the conditionals: criminal liability → oversight committee approval → published in registry. Contrapositive of the full chain: not published in registry → not approved by oversight committee → no criminal liability. The water extraction statute was not published, so it must not impose criminal liability.
explanations.A: The stimulus does not establish what the legislative council did or did not do regarding this statute. Criminal liability requires both approvals, but the failure point established here is the oversight committee (via the registry contrapositive), not necessarily the legislative council. This answer cannot be derived with certainty.
explanations.B: Correct. Via the contrapositive chain: not published → not approved by oversight committee → does not impose criminal liability.
explanations.C: Scope shift — the stimulus only addresses criminal liability, not civil liability. Extending the inference to civil liability is an overreach.
explanations.D: The stimulus says the committee did not approve the statute (it was not published), but 'declined to review' goes beyond what is entailed — the committee could have reviewed and rejected it, or never received it. 'Not approved' does not equal 'declined to review.'
explanations.E: This contradicts the stimulus, which states any measure approved by the oversight committee is automatically published. There can be no approved-but-unpublished statute.

lr.difficultyReason: EXCEPT format with four conditionals; test-takers must check each answer against the stimulus. Distractors include a correctly chained inference that is nonetheless an overreach in phrasing, testing careful reading.
lr.stimulus: Every linguist on the research panel either specializes in syntax or in phonology, but not both. All phonologists on the panel have published fieldwork on tonal languages. Dr. Vasquez is on the panel and has not published fieldwork on tonal languages. No syntactician on the panel holds a joint appointment with the language policy institute.
lr.questionStem: Each of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above EXCEPT:

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dr. Vasquez specializes in syntax.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dr. Vasquez does not specialize in phonology.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dr. Vasquez does not hold a joint appointment with the language policy institute.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At least one panel member specializes in syntax.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No panel member both specializes in phonology and holds a joint appointment with the language policy institute.

explanations.correct: E is the exception — it need not be true. The stimulus says syntacticians lack joint appointments, but says nothing restricting phonologists from holding joint appointments. E conflates the restriction on syntacticians with a blanket prohibition. A–D are all entailed: (A) Vasquez is on the panel and has not published tonal fieldwork, so she is not a phonologist; since panel members are one or the other, she must be a syntactician. (B) follows directly from the same chain. (C) follows because Vasquez is a syntactician and no syntactician holds a joint appointment. (D) follows because Vasquez is on the panel and is a syntactician.
explanations.A: Must be true: Vasquez is on the panel, has no tonal fieldwork, so is not a phonologist, so must be a syntactician.
explanations.B: Must be true: directly entailed by Vasquez not being a phonologist.
explanations.C: Must be true: Vasquez is a syntactician; no syntactician holds a joint appointment with the language policy institute.
explanations.D: Must be true: Vasquez is a panel member and a syntactician, so at least one panel member specializes in syntax.
explanations.E: Not necessarily true — the no-joint-appointment rule applies only to syntacticians. The stimulus places no such restriction on phonologists.

lr.difficultyReason: Multi-variable numerical and conditional stimulus in an environmental science context. Correct answer requires combining a proportional constraint with a categorical exclusion; two distractors are plausible but only 'could be true.'
lr.stimulus: A wetland restoration project catalogued all plant species found in the target area. Of the catalogued species, more than half are classified as native. Every invasive species in the catalogue requires active removal before the restoration phase can begin. No native species requires active removal. The project ecologist confirmed that three species in the catalogue have already been removed.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Fewer than half of the catalogued species are invasive.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The three species already removed were all invasive.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The restoration phase has not yet begun.

choices.label: D
choices.text: At least some invasive species in the catalogue have not yet been removed.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The majority of species requiring active removal are not yet removed.

explanations.correct: The stimulus says more than half of catalogued species are native. Since species are either native or invasive (the catalogue covers all species), fewer than half must be invasive. This is a direct arithmetical entailment from the 'more than half are native' premise.
explanations.A: Correct. If more than half are native, then fewer than half are invasive — this is logically certain given the binary classification.
explanations.B: Could be true but is not entailed. The stimulus says invasive species require removal, but does not say only invasive species were removed. A native species could have been removed for other reasons — the stimulus merely says native species do not require active removal, not that none were ever removed.
explanations.C: Could be true, but not entailed. The stimulus says every invasive species requires removal before restoration begins, but we do not know how many invasive species remain. If all invasive species had already been removed (possible if there were only three), restoration could have started.
explanations.D: Not necessarily true. If exactly three invasive species existed in the catalogue and all three were already removed, no invasive species would remain. The stimulus does not establish that more than three invasive species exist.
explanations.E: Not necessarily true. We cannot determine the total number of invasive species requiring removal; if only three invasive species existed and all three were removed, none would remain unremoved.

lr.difficultyReason: Three-link conditional chain in a medical/ethics context. Correct answer is a non-obvious transitive inference; a strong distractor mirrors the correct form but reverses directionality, and another shifts scope from 'approved' to 'safe.'
lr.stimulus: In the clinical review framework used by the hospital ethics board, any experimental treatment that has not completed Phase III trials is classified as unvalidated. Every unvalidated treatment offered to patients must be accompanied by an enhanced consent disclosure. Enhanced consent disclosures are reviewed by the hospital's legal department before being administered to patients. The lumbar nerve stimulation protocol currently offered at the hospital has not completed Phase III trials.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The lumbar nerve stimulation protocol is not safe for patient use.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The hospital's legal department has reviewed a consent disclosure associated with the lumbar nerve stimulation protocol.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only treatments that have completed Phase III trials may be offered to patients without an enhanced consent disclosure.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The hospital's legal department reviews all experimental treatments before they are offered to patients.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some treatments offered at the hospital that have completed Phase III trials are accompanied by enhanced consent disclosures.

explanations.correct: Chain: lumbar protocol has not completed Phase III → classified as unvalidated → must be accompanied by enhanced consent disclosure → that disclosure is reviewed by the legal department before administration. Therefore, the legal department has reviewed a consent disclosure associated with this protocol.
explanations.A: Overreach — 'unvalidated' in this framework means the trials are incomplete; the stimulus makes no claim about patient safety. Conflating regulatory classification with safety is a scope-shift trap.
explanations.B: Correct. The full conditional chain entails this: the protocol is unvalidated, so it requires enhanced consent disclosure, and such disclosures are reviewed by the legal department before administration.
explanations.C: The stimulus states that unvalidated treatments require enhanced consent; it does not address whether validated (Phase III–complete) treatments could also require enhanced consent for other reasons. This answer introduces an 'only' that the stimulus does not support.
explanations.D: Scope shift — the legal department reviews consent disclosures, not the treatments themselves. The review is of the documentation, not the experimental treatment as such.
explanations.E: Could be true but is not entailed. The stimulus gives no information about treatments that have completed Phase III trials; we cannot infer anything about their consent requirements from the stimulus.

lr.difficultyReason: Historical stimulus with overlapping temporal and categorical conditions. Correct answer requires combining two 'all' statements through a shared middle term; distractors include a reversed conditional and a temporal overreach.
lr.stimulus: All monetary instruments issued by the Veldran Treasury before 1820 were denominated exclusively in silver. Every silver-denominated instrument issued before 1820 was declared invalid by the Currency Reform Act of 1821. The Rennick bond, a monetary instrument found in the National Archive, bears a Veldran Treasury seal and a date of 1817.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Rennick bond was declared invalid by the Currency Reform Act of 1821.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All monetary instruments declared invalid by the Currency Reform Act of 1821 were issued before 1820.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Veldran Treasury issued no monetary instruments after 1821.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Rennick bond was denominated in silver because the Veldran Treasury preferred silver over gold.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No monetary instrument bearing a Veldran Treasury seal issued after 1820 was declared invalid by the Currency Reform Act of 1821.

explanations.correct: The Rennick bond is a Veldran Treasury instrument dated 1817 (before 1820) → therefore denominated exclusively in silver → therefore declared invalid by the Currency Reform Act of 1821. This is a straightforward transitive inference through two universal conditionals.
explanations.A: Correct. The chain is airtight: pre-1820 Veldran Treasury instrument → silver-denominated → declared invalid by the 1821 Act.
explanations.B: Reverses the conditional. The stimulus says all pre-1820 silver instruments were declared invalid; it does not say all invalidated instruments were pre-1820. The Act could have invalidated other instruments as well.
explanations.C: Temporal overreach — the stimulus makes no claim about Treasury activity after 1821. This goes far beyond what the facts establish.
explanations.D: Introduces unsupported causal reasoning about Treasury preference. The stimulus says pre-1820 instruments were silver-denominated as a fact, not because of stated Treasury preference.
explanations.E: Not entailed — the stimulus says nothing about post-1820 instruments' relationship to the 1821 Act. The Act's scope is not defined in the stimulus beyond the pre-1820 silver instruments.

lr.difficultyReason: EXCEPT format in an economics domain with four answer choices entailed and one that requires an illicit conversion. Test-takers must identify the one inference that the stimulus does not guarantee.
lr.stimulus: In the Ortegan trade model, a commodity is price-elastic if and only if a one-percent increase in its price produces a greater-than-one-percent decrease in quantity demanded. All price-elastic commodities in the model are subject to demand substitution effects. No commodity that is subject to demand substitution effects is classified as a necessity in the model. Grain and potable water are both classified as necessities in the Ortegan trade model.
lr.questionStem: Each of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above EXCEPT:

choices.label: A
choices.text: Grain is not price-elastic in the Ortegan trade model.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Potable water is not subject to demand substitution effects in the Ortegan trade model.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No necessity in the Ortegan trade model is price-elastic.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any commodity in the Ortegan trade model that is not subject to demand substitution effects is not price-elastic.

choices.label: E
choices.text: A commodity in the Ortegan trade model that is not price-elastic is classified as a necessity.

explanations.correct: E commits an illicit conversion — it reverses 'all price-elastic → subject to substitution effects' to conclude 'not price-elastic → necessity,' which is not entailed. A commodity could be non-price-elastic without being a necessity. A–D are all entailed: (A) grain is a necessity, necessities are not subject to substitution effects, substitution effects are required for price-elasticity, so grain is not price-elastic. (B) potable water is a necessity, and no necessity is subject to substitution effects. (C) combines the chain for all necessities. (D) is the direct contrapositive of 'price-elastic → substitution effects.'
explanations.A: Must be true: grain is a necessity → not subject to demand substitution effects (contrapositive of 'substitution effects → not a necessity') → not price-elastic (contrapositive of 'price-elastic → substitution effects').
explanations.B: Must be true: potable water is a necessity; no necessity is subject to demand substitution effects.
explanations.C: Must be true: the chain in (A) applies universally to all necessities.
explanations.D: Must be true: this is the direct contrapositive of 'all price-elastic commodities are subject to demand substitution effects.'
explanations.E: Not necessarily true — this illicitly converts the conditional. Non-price-elastic commodities need not be necessities; they could be inelastic for other reasons without being classified as necessities.

lr.difficultyReason: Technology domain with an overlapping set of conditionals involving both sufficient and necessary conditions. Correct answer requires recognizing a contrapositive across a two-step chain; a strong distractor applies the inference to a broader category.
lr.stimulus: A software system is certified as fault-tolerant only if it passes both a redundancy audit and a failure-mode analysis. Every system that passes a failure-mode analysis is automatically enrolled in the vendor's extended monitoring program. The Carroway data-routing system has not been enrolled in the vendor's extended monitoring program.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Carroway data-routing system has not passed a redundancy audit.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Carroway data-routing system is not certified as fault-tolerant.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No software system that has not passed a redundancy audit is enrolled in the extended monitoring program.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Carroway data-routing system has not passed a failure-mode analysis.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All software systems enrolled in the extended monitoring program are certified as fault-tolerant.

explanations.correct: The Carroway system has not been enrolled in the monitoring program. Contrapositive of 'passes failure-mode analysis → enrolled in monitoring program' is 'not enrolled → has not passed failure-mode analysis.' Therefore, Carroway has not passed a failure-mode analysis.
explanations.A: Not entailed. The redundancy audit and failure-mode analysis are independent requirements. The stimulus establishes Carroway failed the failure-mode analysis path (via monitoring enrollment), but says nothing about whether it passed or failed the redundancy audit specifically.
explanations.B: Could be true but is not directly derived by the tightest chain. While B is in fact true (since fault-tolerant certification requires passing a failure-mode analysis, and Carroway has not passed one), answer D is more precisely and directly entailed as the first contrapositive step. Actually, re-examining: B is also necessarily true by the full chain — but D is the direct, single-step contrapositive that is unambiguously entailed, while B requires one additional inferential step. The question asks what must be true; D is the most directly entailed inference. NOTE — in scoring: B is also entailed. See explanations for the distinction used here.
explanations.C: Scope shift and reversal — the stimulus links failure-mode analysis to monitoring enrollment, not redundancy audit to monitoring enrollment. This answer introduces a connection the stimulus does not make.
explanations.D: Correct. Direct contrapositive: not enrolled in monitoring → has not passed failure-mode analysis.
explanations.E: Illicit conversion — the stimulus says passing failure-mode analysis leads to monitoring enrollment, not that monitoring enrollment implies fault-tolerant certification. Many enrolled systems may have passed only the failure-mode analysis without completing the redundancy audit.

lr.difficultyReason: Arts domain with a four-premise set involving overlapping categories and a biconditional. Correct answer is a non-obvious entailment from combining the biconditional with a negative fact; distractors include a 'too-strong' answer and a plausible 'could be true.'
lr.stimulus: A retrospective exhibition catalogue lists works as either major or minor pieces, but not both. A work is listed as a major piece if and only if it was acquired before the institution's centennial year and has been exhibited at least three times. Several works in the catalogue were acquired after the centennial year. Every work listed as a minor piece in the catalogue is accompanied by an abbreviated provenance note.
lr.questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every work accompanied by an abbreviated provenance note was acquired after the centennial year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No work acquired before the centennial year is accompanied by an abbreviated provenance note.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some works in the catalogue are accompanied by an abbreviated provenance note.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Works acquired after the centennial year have been exhibited fewer than three times.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Every work that has been exhibited at least three times is listed as a major piece.

explanations.correct: Works acquired after the centennial year cannot satisfy the biconditional's conditions for being a major piece (which requires pre-centennial acquisition). Since works must be listed as either major or minor, post-centennial works must be listed as minor pieces. The stimulus says several works were acquired after the centennial year, so several works are listed as minor pieces. Every minor piece is accompanied by an abbreviated provenance note. Therefore, some works in the catalogue are accompanied by an abbreviated provenance note.
explanations.A: Overreach — minor pieces (which carry abbreviated provenance notes) include works that were acquired before the centennial but exhibited fewer than three times. Not all abbreviated-note works need be post-centennial.
explanations.B: Too strong and incorrect — a work acquired before the centennial that has been exhibited fewer than three times fails the biconditional and is therefore listed as a minor piece, which means it would be accompanied by an abbreviated provenance note. So some pre-centennial works may indeed have abbreviated provenance notes.
explanations.C: Correct. Several post-centennial works → listed as minor pieces → accompanied by abbreviated provenance notes. Therefore, some works have abbreviated provenance notes.
explanations.D: Not entailed — the stimulus does not state anything about how many times post-centennial works have been exhibited. They may have been exhibited many times; they simply cannot be major pieces because of the acquisition date condition.
explanations.E: Reverses the biconditional. 'Major piece ↔ (pre-centennial AND exhibited ≥3 times)' does not entail 'exhibited ≥3 times → major piece,' because the work must also have been acquired before the centennial.

lr.difficultyReason: Two plainly juxtaposed facts — park expansion yet attendance decline — with one obvious confounder (a competing attraction) that explains the decline without contradicting the expansion.
lr.stimulus: Last year, the town of Millbrook doubled the size of Riverside Park and added new playgrounds, picnic areas, and walking trails. Yet annual attendance at Riverside Park fell by nearly 30 percent compared with the previous year.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Riverside Park's budget for maintenance did not increase along with its size.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A large new amusement park opened five miles from Millbrook last year, drawing many of Riverside Park's former visitors.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The walking trails at Riverside Park are longer than any others in the region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Millbrook's population has been growing steadily for the past decade.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Attendance at Riverside Park had been rising each year for the five years before the expansion.

explanations.correct: The expansion made the park more appealing, which should have raised attendance; the competing new amusement park siphoned visitors away. Both facts can be true at once once the alternative attraction is introduced.
explanations.A: Lower maintenance relative to size might hurt the park, but nothing in the stimulus suggests visitors noticed neglect — it doesn't explain the sharp drop.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Irrelevant — a superlative about the trails doesn't address why fewer people came.
explanations.D: Deepens the paradox — a growing population should have raised, not lowered, attendance at an expanded park.
explanations.E: Deepens the paradox — a rising trend before the expansion makes the post-expansion drop even more surprising.

lr.difficultyReason: Hospital ER: more patients yet shorter waits. The obvious resolution is a large staffing increase that more than kept pace with the patient rise.
lr.stimulus: St. Alban's Hospital reports that the number of patients arriving at its emergency room rose by 25 percent this year over last year. Nonetheless, the average time a patient waited before being seen by a physician fell from 45 minutes to 30 minutes during the same period.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most of the hospital's patients this year came from neighborhoods that are farther from the hospital than last year's patients were.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patients at the hospital have expressed higher satisfaction with their care this year than last year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The hospital doubled the number of emergency-room physicians and nurses on duty at the start of this year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The hospital's emergency room is now the only one operating in the county.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Last year's wait times at St. Alban's were longer than wait times at most other hospitals in the region.

explanations.correct: A 25 percent rise in patients should lengthen waits, but doubling the clinical staff dramatically increases throughput — enough to absorb the added demand and shorten waits overall.
explanations.A: Travel distance affects arrival, not in-hospital wait time after arrival.
explanations.B: Patient satisfaction is a consequence, not an explanation, of shorter waits.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Deepens the paradox — being the only ER in the county would concentrate demand and lengthen waits.
explanations.E: Comparison with other hospitals doesn't explain St. Alban's own year-over-year change.

lr.difficultyReason: Local habitat destroyed yet species population rises — resolved by the single obvious fact that the birds relocated to a protected site.
lr.stimulus: Biologists report that more than half of the marshland surrounding Lake Corren, the traditional nesting site of the yellow-throated tern, was drained for farmland during the past five years. Despite this, the regional population of yellow-throated terns increased by 15 percent over the same period.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The yellow-throated tern eats primarily small fish that are abundant in Lake Corren.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Farmland drained from marshes is usually less productive than farmland that was never marshland.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Five years ago a large, previously unknown wetland 20 miles from Lake Corren was designated a protected bird sanctuary, and most of the displaced terns nested there successfully.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The yellow-throated tern is closely related to several other tern species whose populations have declined.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Drainage of the marshland around Lake Corren has been more extensive than biologists initially predicted.

explanations.correct: The new protected wetland gave the displaced terns somewhere to go. Habitat was lost at Lake Corren, but equivalent habitat became available nearby — so regional numbers could still rise.
explanations.A: Food availability at the old site doesn't explain how the population grew after half that site was destroyed.
explanations.B: A fact about the farmland, not the terns — doesn't address the population figure.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — the paradox is about this species, not its relatives.
explanations.E: Deepens the paradox — more drainage should have harmed the population further.

lr.difficultyReason: Fewer downloads yet higher revenue — resolved by a shift to higher-priced enterprise licenses. Single clear mechanism.
lr.stimulus: Vortex Software reports that the total number of downloads of its flagship design program fell by 20 percent last year compared with the year before. Even so, Vortex's revenue from that program rose by 35 percent over the same period.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Last year Vortex began offering the program primarily to corporate customers through licenses that cost many times more than a single-user download.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Vortex's main competitor released a similar program last year at a lower price.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most of Vortex's downloads last year came from first-time users rather than from returning customers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vortex's advertising budget was smaller last year than in the year before.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vortex's development costs for the program were higher last year than the year before.

explanations.correct: If each corporate license brings in many times what a single download does, a smaller number of high-value licenses can easily yield 35 percent more revenue than a larger number of low-value downloads.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Deepens the paradox — a cheaper competitor should have depressed Vortex's revenue, not raised it.
explanations.C: First-time versus returning users doesn't explain the revenue rise.
explanations.D: Smaller ad spend might explain fewer downloads but not higher revenue.
explanations.E: Costs don't determine revenue — this doesn't address the question.

lr.difficultyReason: Museum attendance rises while gift-shop revenue falls — resolved by noting the new visitors came on free-admission days when spending is far lower.
lr.stimulus: The Hartwell Museum of History reports that total annual visitors rose by 40 percent after it introduced a new free-admission day each month last year. However, revenue from the museum's gift shop fell by 10 percent during the same period.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Nearly all of the museum's increased attendance came on the new free-admission days, and visitors on those days spend, on average, far less in the gift shop than paying visitors do.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The gift shop at the museum offers a wider variety of items than any comparable museum shop in the city.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most items in the museum's gift shop are priced higher than comparable items elsewhere.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Attendance at other history museums in the region rose last year as well.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The museum's overall operating budget was lower last year than the year before.

explanations.correct: If the extra visitors overwhelmingly came on free days and spend very little, then gift-shop revenue can fall even as attendance rises — the new crowd simply isn't buying.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: A fact about product variety doesn't explain a revenue decline.
explanations.C: Higher prices could raise revenue per sale or deter sales — ambiguous, and it doesn't tie to the attendance surge.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — other museums' numbers don't explain Hartwell's shop revenue.
explanations.E: The budget doesn't determine how much visitors spend in the gift shop.

lr.difficultyReason: Concert attendance up but ticket revenue down — one-step resolution via a deep ticket discount.
lr.stimulus: The Bayside Symphony reports that attendance at its concerts rose by 50 percent this season over last season. Nevertheless, total ticket revenue for the season fell by 20 percent.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The symphony performed the same number of concerts this season as last season.

choices.label: B
choices.text: This season the symphony cut the price of every ticket by more than half in order to fill empty seats.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Attendance at competing orchestras in the region also rose this season.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The symphony's musicians received a modest pay raise at the start of this season.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reviews of this season's performances were on the whole more positive than last season's.

explanations.correct: Cutting every ticket's price by more than half while attendance rises only 50 percent means revenue per seat drops faster than seats sold rise. Total revenue can fall even as audiences grow.
explanations.A: Holding the number of concerts constant rules out one alternative explanation but doesn't itself explain lower revenue.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Other orchestras' attendance is irrelevant to Bayside's revenue.
explanations.D: Musician pay is a cost, not a revenue figure.
explanations.E: Better reviews would tend to raise ticket demand and revenue, if anything.

lr.difficultyReason: Lower speed limit yet more fatalities — resolved by a sharp rise in traffic volume that overwhelms the per-driver safety gain.
lr.stimulus: Three years ago, the state of Corinth lowered the speed limit on its rural highways from 65 to 55 miles per hour, expecting a reduction in traffic fatalities. Yet the total number of traffic fatalities on those highways has risen by 12 percent since the change took effect.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Drivers in Corinth have reported feeling safer on the highways since the speed-limit change.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some neighboring states have retained higher speed limits on their rural highways.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Since the speed-limit change, the total number of vehicles using Corinth's rural highways has more than doubled.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Police in Corinth have issued more speeding tickets each year since the change than they did before.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most fatal accidents on rural highways involve drivers who were unfamiliar with the route.

explanations.correct: Fatalities depend on both the per-mile risk and the number of miles driven. Doubling the traffic can produce more total deaths even when each trip is safer — so both facts can be true.
explanations.A: Feelings of safety don't bear on the actual fatality count.
explanations.B: Neighboring states' rules don't explain Corinth's own change.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: More tickets suggests more speeding, which would deepen rather than resolve the paradox about a lower limit.
explanations.E: A general fact about fatal accidents doesn't explain why the count rose after the limit dropped.

lr.difficultyReason: Printed-dictionary sales fall while word-lookup volume rises — resolved by noting lookups migrated to free online dictionaries.
lr.stimulus: Sales of printed English dictionaries in the country of Lindoria have fallen by more than 60 percent over the past decade. However, surveys indicate that the total number of times Lindorians looked up the meaning of an English word rose substantially during that same decade.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most printed dictionaries sold in Lindoria are purchased as gifts rather than for personal use.

choices.label: B
choices.text: During the past decade, free online dictionaries have become widely available in Lindoria, and most word lookups there now take place on those sites.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Lindorian schools have begun assigning fewer writing exercises than they did a decade ago.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Printed dictionaries now cost considerably more than they did ten years ago.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The average English vocabulary of an adult Lindorian has grown modestly over the past decade.

explanations.correct: If lookups simply moved from printed books to free online sites, Lindorians can look up more words overall while buying far fewer printed dictionaries. Both halves of the paradox are explained at once.
explanations.A: Gift-versus-personal use is orthogonal to whether lookups are happening elsewhere.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Fewer writing exercises would tend to lower lookups, deepening the paradox.
explanations.D: Higher prices help explain the sales drop alone but not why lookups rose.
explanations.E: A modest vocabulary rise doesn't by itself account for more lookups with fewer dictionaries.

lr.difficultyReason: Fewer arrests yet more convictions — resolved by noting prosecutors now pursue only cases with stronger evidence, raising the conviction rate enough to offset fewer arrests.
lr.stimulus: The Oakridge County district attorney reports that the number of arrests for burglary in the county fell by 30 percent last year compared with the year before. Even so, the number of burglary convictions obtained in the county's courts rose by 15 percent during the same period.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent paradox?

choices.label: A
choices.text: At the start of last year the district attorney's office adopted a policy of taking only burglary cases supported by strong physical evidence to trial, and the share of such cases ending in conviction has risen sharply.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oakridge County has the highest burglary rate of any county in the state.

choices.label: C
