lr.difficultyReason: Another textbook modus ponens in an environmental-science setting. Traps include a same-topic modus tollens (B) and an affirming-the-consequent lure (E).
lr.stimulus: If the wetland's water level drops below one meter, the resident herons will relocate to the river delta. The water level dropped below one meter last week. Therefore, the resident herons relocated to the river delta.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every licensed electrician carries liability insurance. Marcus is a licensed electrician. Therefore, Marcus carries liability insurance.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the wetland's pH rises above eight, the frog population declines. The frog population has not declined. Therefore, the pH has not risen above eight.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If the train is on schedule, the 7:15 departure leaves from platform two. The train is on schedule today. Therefore, the 7:15 departure leaves from platform two.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the greenhouse vent is open or the temperature will exceed 90 degrees. The temperature did not exceed 90 degrees. Therefore, the vent was open.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If a meadow is grazed, wildflowers become more abundant. The meadow's wildflowers are more abundant, so the meadow has been grazed.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A -> B; A; therefore B. (C) matches: on-schedule -> platform two; on schedule; therefore platform two.
explanations.A: Universal instantiation — categorical rather than propositional. While close in spirit, the stimulus is explicitly conditional; (C) is a cleaner match.
explanations.B: Same wetland topic but modus tollens, not modus ponens. Classic same-topic trap.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.E: Affirms the consequent — invalid.

lr.difficultyReason: Universal instantiation in an economics setting. Distractors include a 'most' generalization and a disjunctive syllogism.
lr.stimulus: All currencies pegged to the dollar fluctuate with U.S. monetary policy. The Beltran peso is pegged to the dollar. Therefore, the Beltran peso fluctuates with U.S. monetary policy.
lr.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most countries that run trade surpluses accumulate foreign reserves. Valoria accumulates foreign reserves, so it probably runs a trade surplus.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every bridge built after 1980 in this province uses prestressed concrete. The Ormond Bridge was built in 1994 in this province. Therefore, the Ormond Bridge uses prestressed concrete.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If a bond is rated below investment grade, institutional funds will not buy it. This bond is rated below investment grade, so institutional funds will not buy it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the exchange rate is fixed or it is floating. The Beltran peso is not floating, so it is fixed.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If consumer spending rises, GDP rises. GDP did not rise, so consumer spending did not rise.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B. (B) is the same universal-to-particular instantiation with bridges: all post-1980 provincial bridges use prestressed concrete; Ormond is one; therefore it does.
explanations.A: Uses 'most' and reverses direction — weaker modal force and different shape.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Modus ponens with an explicit conditional. Close but not universal instantiation.
explanations.D: Disjunctive syllogism; same topic (Beltran peso) is the lure.
explanations.E: Modus tollens.

lr.difficultyReason: Contrapositive (modus tollens) in a historical setting. Traps include a same-topic modus ponens and an affirming-the-consequent lure.
lr.stimulus: If General Hargrove had arrived before dawn, the garrison would have surrendered without a fight. The garrison did not surrender without a fight. Therefore, General Hargrove did not arrive before dawn.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If the treaty had been ratified by both assemblies, the border would have been redrawn. The border was redrawn, so the treaty was ratified by both assemblies.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a compound contains sulfur, it will tarnish silver. This compound does not tarnish silver. Therefore, this compound does not contain sulfur.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If General Hargrove marches at first light, the supply lines will hold. General Hargrove marched at first light. Therefore, the supply lines held.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every cavalry officer trained at the academy learned dead-reckoning navigation. Colonel Vance trained at the academy. Therefore, Colonel Vance learned dead-reckoning.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Either the siege was broken or the city fell. The siege was broken, so the city did not fall.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A -> B; not B; therefore not A — modus tollens. (B) matches: sulfur -> tarnishes silver; does not tarnish; therefore no sulfur.
explanations.A: Same historical topic but affirms the consequent — invalid and so not parallel to the valid stimulus.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Same topic but modus ponens. A same-topic trap.
explanations.D: Universal instantiation, not conditional contrapositive.
explanations.E: Disjunctive syllogism.

lr.difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism in a linguistics setting. Distractors include same-topic conditionals of other forms.
lr.stimulus: A verb in Old Karnish must take either the accusative suffix or the dative suffix. The verb 'velmir' does not take the accusative suffix. Therefore, 'velmir' takes the dative suffix.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a noun in Old Karnish ends in a consonant, it is masculine. The noun 'dran' ends in a consonant, so it is masculine.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every vowel in the Karnish script represents a single phoneme. The symbol 'a' is a vowel in the Karnish script. Therefore, 'a' represents a single phoneme.

choices.label: C
choices.text: On any given weekday, the Mendez family eats either fish or poultry for dinner. Last Tuesday, the Mendez family did not eat poultry. Therefore, they ate fish.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a verb is irregular, it does not follow the standard suffix rules. The verb 'velmir' is not irregular, so it follows the standard suffix rules.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most verbs in Old Karnish take the accusative suffix. 'Velmir' is an Old Karnish verb, so it probably takes the accusative suffix.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A or B; not A; therefore B. (C) is the same disjunctive syllogism in a domestic setting: fish or poultry; not poultry; therefore fish.
explanations.A: Modus ponens, not a disjunction.
explanations.B: Universal instantiation.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Modus tollens with a same-topic lure.
explanations.E: Statistical generalization with 'most' and a probabilistic conclusion.

lr.difficultyReason: Two-link conditional chain in a technology context. Only one answer choice exhibits a hypothetical syllogism; the rest are single-conditional variants or a disjunctive syllogism.
lr.stimulus: If a smartphone's battery degrades below 80 percent capacity, the operating system throttles processor speed. If the operating system throttles processor speed, app launch times become noticeably slower. Therefore, if a smartphone's battery degrades below 80 percent capacity, app launch times become noticeably slower.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a smartphone is dropped in water, its speakers will malfunction. This phone was dropped in water, so its speakers will malfunction.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a bicycle chain is not lubricated, it rusts. If a bicycle chain rusts, pedaling becomes harder. Therefore, if a bicycle chain is not lubricated, pedaling becomes harder.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every laptop in the teaching lab has 16 gigabytes of memory. This machine is in the teaching lab, so it has 16 gigabytes of memory.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the router is offline or the cable has been unplugged. The cable has not been unplugged, so the router is offline.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If a file is encrypted, it cannot be read without the key. This file can be read without the key, so it is not encrypted.

explanations.correct: Stimulus is a hypothetical syllogism: A -> B; B -> C; therefore A -> C. (B) has the identical chain: unlubricated -> rust; rust -> harder pedaling; therefore unlubricated -> harder pedaling.
explanations.A: Modus ponens with one conditional, not a chain. Same-domain lure.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Universal instantiation.
explanations.D: Disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.E: Modus tollens.

lr.difficultyReason: Transparent modus ponens structure. Stimulus presents a simple conditional (If A then B), affirms the antecedent, and draws the conclusion. The correct answer uses the identical logical form with entirely different subject matter.
lr.stimulus: If the shipment arrives on time, the warehouse will be fully stocked. The shipment has arrived on time. Therefore, the warehouse is fully stocked.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a musician practices daily, she will master her instrument. Sarah practices daily. Therefore, Sarah will master her instrument.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most professional athletes train extensively. James is a professional athlete. Therefore, James probably trains extensively.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If the contract is signed, the merger will proceed. The merger did not proceed. Therefore, the contract was not signed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the defendant is guilty or the evidence is unreliable. The evidence is reliable. Therefore, the defendant must be guilty.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All plants require sunlight to grow. This organism grows without sunlight. Therefore, this organism is not a plant.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and A follow modus ponens: If P then Q; P is true; therefore Q is true. The conditional structure and affirmation of the antecedent are identical, only subject matter differs.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Uses probabilistic reasoning ('probably') rather than the definitive conditional chain of the stimulus.
explanations.C: Uses modus tollens (conditional + denial of consequent) rather than modus ponens.
explanations.D: Uses disjunctive syllogism, not conditional reasoning.
explanations.E: Uses categorical logic and contrapositive, not the simple conditional affirmation of the stimulus.

lr.difficultyReason: Clear disjunctive syllogism: A or B; not A; therefore B. The stimulus presents an explicit disjunction, denies one disjunct, and concludes the other. Answer choices mix conditional chains, universals, and other forms to test whether students can isolate the disjunctive structure.
lr.stimulus: Either the report was completed yesterday or it will be completed tomorrow. The report was not completed yesterday. Therefore, the report will be completed tomorrow.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All birds have feathers. This creature has feathers. Therefore, this creature is a bird.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If inflation rises, the central bank will raise interest rates. Inflation has risen. Therefore, the central bank will raise interest rates.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either the suspect fled the country or is hiding locally. The suspect did not flee the country. Therefore, the suspect is hiding locally.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most employees arrive before nine o'clock. This employee arrives before nine o'clock. Therefore, most employees is a reasonable generalization.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If the patient has the virus, she will show symptoms. The patient does not show symptoms. Therefore, the patient does not have the virus.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and C follow disjunctive syllogism: A or B; not A; therefore B. The structure of disjunction + denial + remaining conclusion is identical.
explanations.A: Affirms the consequent (invalid form), not a valid disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.B: Uses modus ponens (conditional + affirmation), not disjunction.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Inductive generalization, not a deductive disjunctive form.
explanations.E: Uses modus tollens (conditional + denial of consequent), not disjunction.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple contrapositive (modus tollens) form: If A then B; not B; therefore not A. The structure is transparent — students must recognize that denying the consequent allows us to deny the antecedent. Distractors use modus ponens, affirm consequent, or categorical logic.
lr.stimulus: If a restaurant has poor sanitation, it will fail the health inspection. The restaurant did not fail the health inspection. Therefore, the restaurant does not have poor sanitation.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a student studies hard, they will pass the exam. This student studied hard. Therefore, this student will pass the exam.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a contract is breached, the other party can sue. The other party did not sue. Therefore, the contract was not breached.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All successful entrepreneurs take risks. These entrepreneurs are successful. Therefore, these entrepreneurs take risks.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the supplier is reliable or the delivery is late. The delivery is not late. Therefore, the supplier is reliable.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most companies invest in research. This company invests in research. Therefore, this company is probably successful.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and B follow modus tollens: If P then Q; not Q; therefore not P. The denial of the consequent leads to denial of the antecedent in both.
explanations.A: Uses modus ponens (affirms antecedent), not modus tollens.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Uses categorical logic (universal + particular), not a conditional chain.
explanations.D: Uses disjunctive syllogism, not a conditional denial.
explanations.E: Uses inductive generalization with probabilistic language.

lr.difficultyReason: Conditional chain (hypothetical syllogism): If A then B; if B then C; A is true; therefore C. Students must track the transitive property through two conditionals and an initial premise. Distractors offer single conditionals, invalid chains, or categorical universals.
lr.stimulus: If the regulatory approval is obtained, the project will be funded. If the project is funded, construction will begin. Regulatory approval has been obtained. Therefore, construction will begin.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If the economy is strong, consumers spend more. Consumers are spending more. Therefore, the economy is strong.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a drug is approved for use, doctors will prescribe it. If doctors prescribe it, patients will take it. The drug is approved. Therefore, patients will take it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All mammals breathe oxygen. This animal breathes oxygen. Therefore, this animal is a mammal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the bill passes or the provision is abandoned. The bill did not pass. Therefore, the provision is abandoned.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most people who exercise regularly are healthy. Marcus exercises regularly. Therefore, Marcus is probably healthy.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and B use hypothetical syllogism: If P then Q; If Q then R; P; therefore R. The chain of two conditionals plus affirmation of the starting premise matches exactly.
explanations.A: Uses modus ponens with affirmation of consequent (invalid).
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Uses categorical universal logic, not chained conditionals.
explanations.D: Uses disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.E: Uses inductive generalization with probability markers.

lr.difficultyReason: Universal-to-particular instantiation: All A are B; X is A; therefore X is B. This is among the simplest deductive forms. Distractors confuse this with converses, probabilistic inferences, disjunctions, or conditional chains.
lr.stimulus: All members of the committee must sign the agreement. Jordan is a member of the committee. Therefore, Jordan must sign the agreement.
lr.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If someone is a manager, they have supervisory responsibilities. Kim has supervisory responsibilities. Therefore, Kim is a manager.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every student enrolled in this course must attend at least one seminar. Elena is enrolled in this course. Therefore, Elena must attend at least one seminar.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either the meeting will be rescheduled or the attendees will be notified. The attendees will not be notified. Therefore, the meeting will be rescheduled.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some critics of the proposal are economists. This person is a critic of the proposal. Therefore, this person is probably an economist.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If the merger succeeds, the two companies will consolidate. The merger has succeeded. Therefore, the companies will consolidate.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and B follow universal instantiation: All/Every A must be B; X is A; therefore X must be B. The structure of universal claim + particular case + necessary conclusion is identical.
explanations.A: Affirms consequent (invalid), not a universal instantiation.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Uses disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.D: Uses inductive reasoning with a probabilistic ('probably') qualifier.
explanations.E: Uses modus ponens (conditional reasoning).

lr.difficultyReason: Simple analogy with parallel structure: X and Y share properties P and Q; Y has property R; therefore X has property R. The conclusion transfers a property across a likeness. Distractors use conditionals, universals, or failed analogies.
lr.stimulus: Orchestral music and chamber music both use multiple instrumental voices and follow classical forms. Chamber music creates an intimate listening experience. Therefore, orchestral music also creates an intimate listening experience.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a team has strong coaching, it will win championships. This team has strong coaching. Therefore, this team will win championships.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All professional athletes dedicate themselves to their sport. This person is a professional athlete. Therefore, this person dedicates themselves to their sport.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Novels and short stories both employ narrative structure and character development. Novels are commercially published. Therefore, short stories are commercially published.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the defendant acted with intent or acted recklessly. The defendant did not act with intent. Therefore, the defendant acted recklessly.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If deforestation accelerates, endangered species will disappear. Deforestation has accelerated. Therefore, endangered species will disappear.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and C follow analogical reasoning: X and Y share P and Q; Y has R; therefore X has R. The parallel structure transfers a property based on noted similarities.
explanations.A: Uses modus ponens (conditional).
explanations.B: Uses universal instantiation.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Uses disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.E: Uses modus ponens (conditional).

lr.difficultyReason: Modus ponens with a real-world policy context: If condition P holds, outcome Q follows; P holds; therefore Q. The structure is transparent, and distractors use different logical forms or the wrong direction in conditionals.
lr.stimulus: If unemployment rises above five percent, the government must increase job training programs. Unemployment has risen above five percent. Therefore, the government must increase job training programs.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a company pollutes local water sources, it will face legal penalties. This company has faced legal penalties. Therefore, this company pollutes local water sources.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a species loses its habitat, it is at risk of extinction. This species has lost its habitat. Therefore, this species is at risk of extinction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either the new policy is beneficial or it is harmful. The policy is not harmful. Therefore, the policy is beneficial.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All environmental regulations protect public health. This regulation protects public health. Therefore, this regulation is environmental.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most candidates with relevant experience are hired for the position. This candidate has relevant experience. Therefore, this candidate is probably hired.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and B follow modus ponens: If P then Q; P is true; therefore Q is true. The conditional structure and affirmation of the antecedent match.
explanations.A: Affirms consequent (invalid), reversing the conditional direction.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Uses disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.D: Uses categorical logic incorrectly (affirms consequent).
explanations.E: Uses inductive generalization with probabilistic qualifier.

lr.difficultyReason: Two-premise modus tollens in an economic context: If P then Q; not Q; therefore not P. The denial of the consequent triggers denial of the antecedent. Distractors offer affirming consequent, modus ponens, or categorical forms.
lr.stimulus: If a company reduces operating costs, it will increase profitability. This company did not increase profitability. Therefore, this company did not reduce operating costs.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If attendance drops below minimum, the event will be canceled. Attendance has dropped below minimum. Therefore, the event will be canceled.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All efficient supply chains reduce delivery delays. This supply chain reduces delivery delays. Therefore, this supply chain is efficient.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If a student submits work late, the grade will be reduced. This student's grade was not reduced. Therefore, this student did not submit work late.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the contract is legally binding or it contains ambiguities. The contract does not contain ambiguities. Therefore, the contract is legally binding.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most companies that invest in technology see growth. This company sees growth. Therefore, this company probably invests in technology.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and C follow modus tollens: If P then Q; not Q; therefore not P. Denying the consequent permits denying the antecedent in identical form.
explanations.A: Uses modus ponens (affirms antecedent).
explanations.B: Uses categorical logic (universal + particular).
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Uses disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.E: Uses inductive generalization with probability.

lr.difficultyReason: Three-premise conditional chain in a medical context: If A then B; If B then C; A is true; therefore C. The chain is straightforward, and distractors include failed chains, single conditionals, or non-conditional forms.
lr.stimulus: If a patient has high blood pressure, medication will be prescribed. If medication is prescribed, regular monitoring will be required. This patient has high blood pressure. Therefore, regular monitoring will be required.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a witness is credible, the testimony is admissible. The testimony is admissible. Therefore, the witness is credible.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a forest fire spreads to populated areas, evacuation orders will be issued. If evacuation orders are issued, residents must leave. A forest fire has spread to populated areas. Therefore, residents must leave.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All licensed therapists follow ethical guidelines. This person follows ethical guidelines. Therefore, this person is a licensed therapist.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the diagnosis is correct or the patient will need further tests. The diagnosis is correct. Therefore, the patient will not need further tests.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most people with seasonal allergies take antihistamines. Marcus takes antihistamines. Therefore, Marcus probably has seasonal allergies.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and B follow hypothetical syllogism with three components: If P then Q; If Q then R; P; therefore R. The transitive chain through two conditionals matches.
explanations.A: Uses modus ponens with affirmation of consequent (invalid).
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Uses categorical universal instantiation.
explanations.D: Uses disjunctive syllogism with a flawed conclusion structure.
explanations.E: Uses inductive generalization with probabilistic reasoning.

lr.difficultyReason: Universal categorical with negative instantiation: All A are B; X is not B; therefore X is not A. This follows the contrapositive of categorical logic and mirrors the logical form of modus tollens. Distractors offer affirmations, valid but non-parallel forms, or inductive reasoning.
lr.stimulus: All candidates who pass the bar exam will be licensed to practice law. This graduate did not become licensed to practice law. Therefore, this graduate did not pass the bar exam.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All published novels go through editorial review. This manuscript went through editorial review. Therefore, this manuscript is a published novel.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All members of the honor society maintain a GPA above 3.5. This student does not maintain a GPA above 3.5. Therefore, this student is not a member of the honor society.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either the defendant confessed or the evidence is circumstantial. The defendant did not confess. Therefore, the evidence is circumstantial.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If an animal is a mammal, it breathes air. This animal breathes air. Therefore, this animal is a mammal.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most people who study philosophy develop critical thinking skills. This person developed critical thinking skills. Therefore, this person probably studied philosophy.

explanations.correct: Both stimulus and B follow categorical universal with negative instantiation: All A are B; X is not B; therefore X is not A. The contrapositive structure of categorical logic matches exactly.
explanations.A: Affirms consequent (invalid) in a categorical form.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Uses disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.D: Uses modus ponens (affirms antecedent).
explanations.E: Uses inductive generalization with probabilistic language.

lr.difficultyReason: Straightforward modus ponens with transparent conditional structure: if-then premise, affirming antecedent, simple valid conclusion. Correct answer repeats the modus ponens form; distractors use other valid forms (universal instantiation) or invalid patterns.
lr.stimulus: If the corporation issues new stock, then its shareholders will be diluted. The corporation issued new stock. Therefore, the shareholders were diluted.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a chemical reaction reaches a critical temperature, it will accelerate rapidly. This reaction has reached the critical temperature. Therefore, it will accelerate rapidly.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Metals conduct electricity. Copper is a metal. Therefore, copper conducts electricity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If the defendant did not leave the premises, then the witness must be lying. The witness is not lying. Therefore, the defendant left the premises.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All glaciers are retreating due to climate change. The Athabaska Glacier is retreating. Therefore, it is a glacier.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If the patient takes the antibiotic, she will recover. If she recovers, she will return to work. The patient takes the antibiotic. Therefore, she will return to work.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: if P then Q; P; therefore Q (modus ponens). Choice A: if P then Q; P; therefore Q. Identical structure, different subject matter (chemistry vs. corporate finance).
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Uses universal instantiation (all A are B; x is A; therefore x is B), not a conditional modus ponens.
explanations.C: Uses modus tollens (if P then Q; not Q; therefore not P), not modus ponens.
explanations.D: Uses invalid reasoning: all A are B; x is B; therefore x is A (affirming the consequent).
explanations.E: Uses conditional chain (if P then Q; if Q then R; P; therefore R), not simple modus ponens.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple disjunctive syllogism: A or B; not A; therefore B. Clearly valid. Correct answer has identical structure; distractors use conditionals, valid but non-parallel forms, or mismatched strength.
lr.stimulus: Either the supplier will deliver the goods on time, or the project will miss its deadline. The supplier did not deliver the goods on time. Therefore, the project will miss its deadline.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The museum director must have either approved the acquisition or delegated the decision. The director did not approve it. Therefore, the director delegated the decision.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the board approves the budget, then operations will continue. The board approved the budget. Therefore, operations will continue.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most employees prefer remote work. Sarah is an employee. Therefore, Sarah probably prefers remote work.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All musical compositions require a composer. This symphony is a musical composition. Therefore, it has a composer.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The training program is effective if and only if participants pass the certification exam. Participants passed the exam. Therefore, the training program is effective.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A or B; not A; therefore B (disjunctive syllogism). Choice A: A or B; not A; therefore B. Same structure, different context (project delivery vs. museum decisions).
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Modus ponens (if P then Q; P; therefore Q), not disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.C: Universal instantiation with probability marker; different structure from the stimulus.
explanations.D: Universal instantiation (all A are B; x is A; therefore x is B), not disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.E: Biconditional affirmation; not the same as disjunctive syllogism.

lr.difficultyReason: Modus tollens: if P then Q; not Q; therefore not P. Transparent and valid. Correct answer mirrors modus tollens; distractors include modus ponens (structural reversal) and invalid affirming-the-consequent patterns.
lr.stimulus: If the contract is binding, then both parties have legal obligations. Both parties do not have legal obligations. Therefore, the contract is not binding.
lr.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If the defendant was at the crime scene, then the physical evidence would match. The physical evidence does not match. Therefore, the defendant was not at the crime scene.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a language is widely spoken, it will be taught in schools. Latin is not widely spoken. Therefore, Latin is not taught in schools.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The medication must help with pain if patients report feeling better. Patients report feeling better. Therefore, the medication helps with pain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All bacteria are prokaryotes. This organism is a prokaryote. Therefore, it is a bacterium.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If an economy exports more than it imports, it has a trade surplus. Some economies have a trade surplus. Therefore, they export more than they import.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: if P then Q; not Q; therefore not P (modus tollens). Choice A: if P then Q; not Q; therefore not P. Identical structure, different domain (law vs. contracts).
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Denies the antecedent (if P then Q; not P; therefore not Q), which is invalid but a common trap.
explanations.C: Affirms the consequent (if P then Q; Q; therefore P), structurally invalid.
explanations.D: Universal instantiation with invalid affirming-the-consequent (all A are B; x is B; therefore x is A).
explanations.E: Partial affirmation of a conditional with only subset confirmation; not modus tollens.

lr.difficultyReason: Conditional chain: if P then Q; if Q then R; P; therefore R. Transparent and valid. Correct answer uses the same chain structure; distractors use simpler conditionals or branch into analogies.
lr.stimulus: If the server goes offline, then data will not sync. If data does not sync, then users will experience errors. The server went offline. Therefore, users will experience errors.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If the artist receives the commission, she will begin painting. If she begins painting, she will complete the work in time. The artist received the commission. Therefore, she will complete the work in time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the interest rate rises, then inflation decreases. Interest rates have risen. Therefore, inflation has decreased.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All architects design buildings. Frank is an architect. Therefore, Frank designs buildings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the engine is broken or the fuel tank is empty. The engine is not broken. Therefore, the fuel tank is empty.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If a policy is unpopular, the administration will reconsider it. The administration will reconsider the policy. Therefore, the policy is unpopular.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: if P then Q; if Q then R; P; therefore R (conditional chain). Choice A: if P then Q; if Q then R; P; therefore R. Identical structure, different subject (art commission vs. technology).
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Simple modus ponens (if P then Q; P; therefore Q), not a chain.
explanations.C: Universal instantiation (all A are B; x is A; therefore x is B).
explanations.D: Disjunctive syllogism (A or B; not A; therefore B).
explanations.E: Affirms the consequent (if P then Q; Q; therefore P), which is invalid.

lr.difficultyReason: Universal instantiation: all A are B; x is A; therefore x is B. Very straightforward categorical syllogism. Correct answer uses the same form; distractors include conditionals, invalid reversals, or disjunctions.
lr.stimulus: All insects have six legs. A butterfly is an insect. Therefore, a butterfly has six legs.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All peer-reviewed journals are credible sources. The New England Journal of Medicine is a peer-reviewed journal. Therefore, it is a credible source.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If an organism is a mammal, it has a backbone. Dolphins are mammals. Therefore, dolphins have backbones.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some birds migrate south in winter. The robin is a bird. Therefore, the robin migrates south in winter.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rocks are either igneous or sedimentary. This rock is igneous. Therefore, it is not sedimentary.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If a food contains peanuts, it should be labeled as such. Peanut oil may not be labeled. Therefore, peanut oil does not contain peanuts.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: all A are B; x is A; therefore x is B (universal instantiation). Choice A: all A are B; x is A; therefore x is B. Identical structure, different domain (biology vs. academic publishing).
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Uses conditional framing (if-then) rather than universal categorical form.
explanations.C: Partial quantifier (some) rather than universal (all); invalid inference.
explanations.D: Disjunctive reasoning, not universal instantiation.
explanations.E: Conditional with invalid modus tollens application.

lr.difficultyReason: Analogy: X is like Y in respects P and Q; Y has property R; therefore X has R. Clear and transparent. Correct answer uses parallel analogy; distractors use conditional, categorical, or disjunctive forms that obscure the structural match.
lr.stimulus: This management consulting firm is similar to a teaching hospital in its emphasis on mentorship and its commitment to knowledge-sharing. Teaching hospitals produce excellent physicians. Therefore, this consulting firm will produce excellent consultants.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A startup incubator resembles a successful seed fund in its focus on early-stage investment and its hands-on guidance. Seed funds often identify industry leaders. Therefore, this startup incubator will likely identify future leaders.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a company invests in employee development, it will retain talented workers. This company invests heavily in development. Therefore, it will retain talented workers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All professional sports teams require dedication and skill. The local basketball team is a professional team. Therefore, it requires dedication and skill.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the product was defective or the customer misused it. The product was not defective. Therefore, the customer misused it.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If an organization prioritizes community engagement, it builds public trust. If it builds trust, it attracts donors. The nonprofit prioritizes engagement. Therefore, it will attract donors.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: X is like Y in properties P and Q; Y has R; therefore X has R (analogy). Choice A: X is like Y in properties P and Q; Y has R; therefore X has R. Identical analogical structure, different context (incubator vs. consulting firm).
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Modus ponens (if P then Q; P; therefore Q), not analogical reasoning.
explanations.C: Universal instantiation (all A are B; x is A; therefore x is B).
explanations.D: Disjunctive syllogism (A or B; not A; therefore B).
explanations.E: Conditional chain (if P then Q; if Q then R; P; therefore R), not analogy.

lr.difficultyReason: Three-step conditional chain with modus ponens at the end: A→B, B→C, A, therefore C. Traps (B) and (D) share topic or conclusion type but drop a link or reverse a conditional; trap (E) runs a two-premise chain rather than three.
lr.stimulus: If the municipal bond measure passes, the library's endowment will grow. If the library's endowment grows, it will be able to hire a second archivist. The bond measure will pass. So the library will be able to hire a second archivist.
lr.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If the ice on the lake thickens, ice fishing will be permitted. If ice fishing is permitted, the bait shop will reopen. The ice on the lake will thicken. Therefore, the bait shop will reopen.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the tax levy passes, the school will receive new computers. The tax levy will pass. So students will learn to code more quickly.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If a candidate wins the primary, she will appear on the general-election ballot. Senator Park did not win the primary. Therefore, she will not appear on the general-election ballot.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If the rezoning vote succeeds, a new park will be built. If a new park is built, nearby property values will rise. Property values near the proposed park have already risen. Therefore, the rezoning vote will succeed.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If the referendum passes, the museum will expand. The referendum will pass. Therefore, the museum will expand.

explanations.correct: Stimulus is a three-step chain: A→B, B→C, A, ∴ C. (A) matches exactly: thickens→ice fishing, ice fishing→bait shop, thickens, ∴ bait shop reopens. Same conditional directions, same number of premises, same modus-ponens conclusion.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Matches topic (civic vote) and affirms the antecedent, but the conclusion ("students will learn to code more quickly") is an unlicensed new claim — the chain structure is broken.
explanations.C: Denies the antecedent — a two-premise modus tollens-lookalike, not a three-step affirming chain. Conclusion is negative, not positive.
explanations.D: Affirms the consequent of the second conditional to reach the antecedent of the first — reverses the chain's direction. Not the same form.
explanations.E: Single conditional + modus ponens (two premises, not three). Drops the middle link.

lr.difficultyReason: Universal generalization plus particular instantiation plus conditional: "All A are B; all B require C; x is A; therefore x requires C." Mixed forms force students to track both a syllogism and a conditional step.
lr.stimulus: All amphibians are ectothermic. Every ectothermic vertebrate requires an external heat source to regulate its body temperature. The hellbender is an amphibian. Therefore, the hellbender requires an external heat source to regulate its body temperature.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All corporate bonds are debt instruments. Every debt instrument carries some default risk. The Marcor bond is a corporate bond. Therefore, the Marcor bond carries some default risk.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most songbirds migrate. Every migratory bird requires fat reserves before departure. The scarlet tanager is a songbird. Therefore, the scarlet tanager requires fat reserves before departure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All mollusks have soft bodies. The nautilus has a soft body. Therefore, the nautilus is a mollusk.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All granite is igneous. The quarry stone is igneous. Every igneous rock resists weathering. Therefore, the quarry stone resists weathering.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most sonnets have fourteen lines. Every fourteen-line poem contains a volta. "Ozymandias" is a sonnet. Therefore, "Ozymandias" probably contains a volta.

explanations.correct: Stimulus structure: all A are B; all B require C; x is A; ∴ x requires C — two universal premises, one particular instance, universal (non-hedged) conclusion. (A) mirrors each step: all corporate bonds are debt instruments; all debt instruments carry default risk; Marcor is a corporate bond; therefore Marcor carries default risk.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Opens with "most" instead of "all," weakening the first premise's quantifier and breaking the universal-to-particular chain.
explanations.C: Affirms the consequent — having a soft body doesn't make something a mollusk. This is a two-premise flawed argument; the stimulus is valid.
explanations.D: Same premises present but in a different order that converts the middle step (quarry is igneous is asserted directly, not derived), and omits the universal "all granite is igneous" chain properly; closer structurally than B/C/E but mismatches premise order and derivation path.
explanations.E: Hedges with "most" and "probably" — conclusion strength is weakened, so it does not match the stimulus's universal conclusion.

lr.difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism plus conditional: "A or B; A→C; ¬C; ∴ B." Students must recognize that the middle step is a contrapositive application that eliminates one disjunct.
lr.stimulus: Either the manuscript was written by Beaumont or it was written by Fletcher. If Beaumont wrote the manuscript, the paper would bear a Kentish watermark. The paper does not bear a Kentish watermark. Therefore, Fletcher wrote the manuscript.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Either the diamond came from the Karowe mine or it came from the Letseng mine. If the diamond came from the Karowe mine, it would contain nitrogen inclusions. The diamond does not contain nitrogen inclusions. Therefore, the diamond came from the Letseng mine.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The sample is either basalt or granite. It is basalt. Therefore, it is not granite.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If the package was shipped from Osaka, it would bear a customs stamp. The package bears a customs stamp. Therefore, the package was shipped from Osaka.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the violin was made by Guarneri or by Stradivari. If Guarneri made it, the f-holes would be asymmetrical. The f-holes are asymmetrical. Therefore, Guarneri made it.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Either the essay was written in 1640 or in 1650. If it was written in 1640, it would reference the regicide. The essay references the regicide. Therefore, the essay was written in 1640.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A∨B; A→C; ¬C; ∴ B. The middle step uses contrapositive (¬C→¬A) to eliminate a disjunct. (A) matches: Karowe∨Letseng; Karowe→nitrogen; ¬nitrogen; ∴ Letseng. Same disjunctive base, same contrapositive move, same positive conclusion about the surviving disjunct.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: A bare disjunctive syllogism with no conditional middle step — two premises, not three.
explanations.C: Affirms the consequent — a classic fallacy; stimulus is valid, so this cannot be parallel.
explanations.D: Affirms the consequent inside the conditional step — concludes the antecedent from the consequent, reversing the contrapositive move.
explanations.E: Same affirming-the-consequent move as D — invalid, and the stimulus is valid.

lr.difficultyReason: Analogy-plus-universal: two shared properties justify inferring a third. Conclusion strength is hedged ("likely"). Students must match both the analogical form and the modal hedge.
lr.stimulus: The economies of Varland and Neufeld share two key features: both are small open economies heavily dependent on commodity exports, and both peg their currencies to the euro. When commodity prices fell last decade, Varland experienced a sharp contraction. Neufeld is now facing a similar commodity price decline, so Neufeld will likely experience a sharp contraction as well.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The novels of Marin and Quilter share two key features: both employ unreliable first-person narrators, and both are set during wartime. Marin's novels have been widely translated. Quilter's novels share these features, so Quilter's novels will likely be widely translated as well.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The cities of Portmouth and Callenby share two key features: both are coastal harbor towns, and both rely on fishing as their primary industry. When a red tide struck Portmouth last year, its fishing yields collapsed. Callenby is now experiencing a red tide, so Callenby's fishing yields will likely collapse as well.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The cities of Portmouth and Callenby are both coastal harbor towns. When a red tide struck Portmouth, its fishing yields collapsed. Therefore, Callenby's fishing yields will collapse if a red tide strikes it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Several coastal cities have collapsed when hit by red tides. Callenby is a coastal city. Therefore, Callenby's fishing yields must collapse.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The cities of Portmouth and Callenby share many features. Portmouth's fishing yields collapsed last year. Therefore, Callenby's fishing yields collapsed last year too.

explanations.correct: Stimulus structure: X and Y share properties P and Q; when condition C struck X, X suffered outcome O; C is now striking Y; ∴ Y will likely suffer O. (B) mirrors each element: Portmouth/Callenby share two features; red tide caused a collapse in Portmouth; red tide now in Callenby; ∴ Callenby will likely collapse. Hedged conclusion preserved.
explanations.A: Matches surface structure of "two shared features," but the outcome being transferred (widely translated) is not triggered by a condition currently recurring in the second case — there is no parallel to the recurring commodity price decline / red tide.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Only one shared feature named; conclusion is a conditional, not a prediction. Missing the second shared property and the present-tense recurrence.
explanations.D: Draws from a general population ("several coastal cities") rather than a pairwise analogy; conclusion uses "must" instead of "likely," mismatching modal force.
explanations.E: Vague premise ("share many features") and past-tense conclusion — stimulus concludes about a future event.

lr.difficultyReason: Contrapositive chain with three steps: A→B, B→C, ¬C, ∴ ¬A. Students must trace two contrapositive moves and match both the negative conclusion and the three-premise count.
lr.stimulus: If a painting is genuinely by Vermeer, it contains ultramarine pigment in the shadow layers. If a painting contains ultramarine pigment in the shadow layers, X-ray fluorescence analysis will detect traces of lapis lazuli. X-ray fluorescence analysis of the disputed painting did not detect traces of lapis lazuli. Therefore, the disputed painting is not genuinely by Vermeer.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a fossil is from the Cambrian period, it predates the emergence of vertebrates. If a fossil predates the emergence of vertebrates, it will contain no hollow bone fragments. The specimen from Well Ridge contains no hollow bone fragments. Therefore, the specimen is from the Cambrian period.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a wine is a genuine Chablis, it comes from the Kimmeridgian limestone soils. If a wine comes from the Kimmeridgian limestone soils, it will exhibit a distinctive mineral note. The wine under review does not exhibit a distinctive mineral note. Therefore, the wine under review is not a genuine Chablis.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If a building is a true Gothic cathedral, it has pointed arches. The building across the square does not have pointed arches. Therefore, it is not a true Gothic cathedral.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a coin is a genuine Roman denarius, it contains a high silver content. The coin in question contains a high silver content. Therefore, it is a genuine Roman denarius.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If a recording is from the 1950s, it is on magnetic tape. If a recording is on magnetic tape, it can be digitized with standard equipment. The studio recording from 1952 can be digitized with standard equipment. Therefore, the studio recording is from the 1950s.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A→B, B→C, ¬C, ∴ ¬A — three premises, chained contrapositive ending in negation of original antecedent. (B) mirrors it precisely: Chablis→Kimmeridgian, Kimmeridgian→mineral note, ¬mineral note, ∴ not Chablis.
explanations.A: Affirms the final consequent (no hollow bones) and concludes the original antecedent — that's affirming the consequent, which is invalid. The stimulus is valid.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Two-premise modus tollens, not a three-premise chain. Drops the middle conditional.
explanations.D: Affirms the consequent in a two-premise argument — invalid.
explanations.E: Three conditionals but ends with affirming-the-consequent move to conclude the antecedent — invalid, and also the conclusion is positive, not negative.

lr.difficultyReason: Universal generalization + conditional + modus ponens. Three-step mixed form requires matching the universal quantifier, conditional chain, and particular conclusion — not just one of these.
lr.stimulus: Every language that distinguishes grammatical gender marks it on nouns. If a language marks gender on nouns, it also marks gender on adjectives that modify those nouns. Icelandic distinguishes grammatical gender. Therefore, Icelandic marks gender on adjectives that modify nouns.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every jurisdiction that recognizes community property divides marital assets equally at divorce. If a jurisdiction divides marital assets equally at divorce, it also applies the same rule to debts acquired during the marriage. The state of Tarmouth recognizes community property. Therefore, Tarmouth applies the equal-division rule to debts acquired during the marriage.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most jurisdictions that recognize community property divide marital assets equally at divorce. If a jurisdiction divides marital assets equally, it also applies the same rule to debts. The state of Tarmouth recognizes community property. Therefore, Tarmouth probably applies the equal-division rule to debts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every jurisdiction that recognizes community property divides marital assets equally. Tarmouth divides marital assets equally. Therefore, Tarmouth recognizes community property.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a jurisdiction recognizes community property, it divides marital assets equally. Tarmouth divides marital assets equally. Therefore, Tarmouth recognizes community property.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Every jurisdiction that recognizes community property divides marital assets equally at divorce. Tarmouth recognizes community property. Therefore, Tarmouth divides marital assets equally at divorce.

explanations.correct: Stimulus structure: all A are B; B→C; x is A; ∴ x is C — universal premise feeds an instance into a conditional chain. (A) matches: all community-property jurisdictions do X; X→Y; Tarmouth is a community-property jurisdiction; ∴ Tarmouth does Y. Same three-step mixed form with universal conclusion.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Weakens the first premise's quantifier to "most" and hedges the conclusion with "probably" — strength shift.
explanations.C: Affirms the consequent — reverses the universal into a biconditional improperly. Invalid.
explanations.D: Same affirming-the-consequent error, now on a conditional premise. Invalid.
explanations.E: Correct universal-to-particular step but drops the middle conditional — only two premises where the stimulus has three.

lr.difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism with a universal-instantiation middle step: "A or B; every A has property P; this x lacks P; ∴ x is B." Mixed disjunctive + universal forms across three premises.
lr.stimulus: The archaeological layer at Site 9 dates from either the Early Bronze Age or the Middle Bronze Age. Every Early Bronze Age layer at this region's sites contains tin-rich bronze fragments. The layer at Site 9 contains no tin-rich bronze fragments. Therefore, the layer at Site 9 dates from the Middle Bronze Age.
lr.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The fabric swatch was produced in either the 18th or the 19th century. Every 18th-century swatch of this type contains handspun linen fibers. The fabric swatch contains no handspun linen fibers. Therefore, the fabric swatch was produced in the 19th century.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The fabric swatch was produced in either the 18th or the 19th century. Most 18th-century swatches of this type contain handspun linen fibers. The fabric swatch contains no handspun linen fibers. Therefore, the fabric swatch was probably produced in the 19th century.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The fabric swatch was produced in the 18th century. Every 18th-century swatch contains handspun linen fibers. Therefore, the fabric swatch contains handspun linen fibers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every 18th-century swatch contains handspun linen fibers. The fabric swatch contains handspun linen fibers. Therefore, the fabric swatch was produced in the 18th century.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The fabric swatch was produced in the 18th or 19th century. The fabric swatch contains no handspun linen fibers. Therefore, the fabric swatch was produced in the 19th century.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A∨B; all A have P; this x lacks P; ∴ x is B. Three premises, universal + disjunctive middle, positive conclusion about surviving disjunct. (A) matches each step: 18th∨19th; every 18th-century swatch has P; this swatch lacks P; ∴ 19th century.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: "Most" weakens the universal premise and "probably" hedges the conclusion — strength mismatch on both quantifier and modal force.
explanations.C: Categorical syllogism, not a disjunction-elimination argument. Conclusion is about the property, not about which disjunct holds.
explanations.D: Affirms the consequent — invalid; the stimulus is valid.
explanations.E: Drops the universal premise about 18th-century swatches entirely, so the contrapositive move that licenses the elimination is missing.

lr.difficultyReason: Three-step conditional chain with modus tollens: A→B, B→C, ¬C, ∴ ¬A. Requires distinguishing from nearby modus ponens chains and from two-premise contrapositive shortcuts.
lr.stimulus: If a server handles peak traffic without latency spikes, it must have sufficient cache capacity. If a server has sufficient cache capacity, its disk-access logs will show low read frequencies during peak hours. The disk-access logs for server Delta show high read frequencies during peak hours. Therefore, server Delta does not handle peak traffic without latency spikes.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a chef earns a Michelin star, she must source her produce locally. If a chef sources her produce locally, her supplier invoices will show regional farm names. Chef Okafor's supplier invoices show no regional farm names. Therefore, Chef Okafor has not earned a Michelin star.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a chef earns a Michelin star, she must source her produce locally. If a chef sources her produce locally, her supplier invoices will show regional farm names. Chef Okafor's supplier invoices show regional farm names. Therefore, Chef Okafor has earned a Michelin star.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If a chef earns a Michelin star, her supplier invoices show regional farm names. Chef Okafor's supplier invoices show no regional farm names. Therefore, Chef Okafor has not earned a Michelin star.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most chefs who earn a Michelin star source their produce locally. If a chef sources her produce locally, her supplier invoices will show regional farm names. Chef Okafor's supplier invoices show no regional farm names. Therefore, Chef Okafor has probably not earned a Michelin star.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If a chef earns a Michelin star, she must source her produce locally. Chef Okafor sources her produce locally. Therefore, Chef Okafor has earned a Michelin star.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A→B, B→C, ¬C, ∴ ¬A — three premises, chained modus tollens. (A) mirrors each step: Michelin→local sourcing, local sourcing→regional invoices, ¬regional invoices, ∴ ¬Michelin.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Affirms the final consequent (invoices show farm names) and concludes the antecedent — invalid, and the stimulus is valid.
explanations.C: Two-premise modus tollens; drops the middle conditional. Premise count mismatch.
explanations.D: Weakens the first premise to "most" and hedges the conclusion with "probably" — strength shift on both the universal and the modal.
explanations.E: Two-premise affirming-the-consequent-style argument with a positive conclusion — invalid and oppositely directed.

lr.difficultyReason: Mixed form: universal premise about a category, instantiation to a member, and a conditional step that licenses a positive conclusion. Students must match the universal strength and the number of inferential steps.
lr.stimulus: Every virus in the Flaviviridae family replicates using an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. If a pathogen replicates using an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, it is susceptible to nucleoside analog antivirals. The dengue virus belongs to the Flaviviridae family. Therefore, the dengue virus is susceptible to nucleoside analog antivirals.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every statute enacted under the Commerce Clause regulates interstate activity. If a statute regulates interstate activity, it can preempt conflicting state laws. The Mercer Act was enacted under the Commerce Clause. Therefore, the Mercer Act can preempt conflicting state laws.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Many statutes enacted under the Commerce Clause regulate interstate activity. If a statute regulates interstate activity, it can preempt conflicting state laws. The Mercer Act was enacted under the Commerce Clause. Therefore, the Mercer Act probably can preempt conflicting state laws.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every statute enacted under the Commerce Clause regulates interstate activity. The Mercer Act regulates interstate activity. Therefore, the Mercer Act was enacted under the Commerce Clause.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a statute was enacted under the Commerce Clause, it can preempt conflicting state laws. The Mercer Act can preempt conflicting state laws. Therefore, the Mercer Act was enacted under the Commerce Clause.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Every statute enacted under the Commerce Clause regulates interstate activity. The Mercer Act was enacted under the Commerce Clause. Therefore, the Mercer Act regulates interstate activity.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: all A do P; P→Q; x is A; ∴ x does Q. Three premises, universal + conditional, universal-strength conclusion. (A) matches: all Commerce Clause statutes regulate interstate activity; regulation→preemption; Mercer is a Commerce Clause statute; ∴ Mercer can preempt.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: "Many" weakens the universal, and "probably" hedges the conclusion — strength shift on both premise and conclusion.
explanations.C: Affirms the consequent of the universal — invalid. Stimulus is valid.
explanations.D: Affirms the consequent of the conditional — invalid.
explanations.E: Valid but drops the middle conditional; two premises where the stimulus has three.

lr.difficultyReason: Disjunction with contrapositive elimination producing a negative conclusion about the other disjunct's property: A∨B; A→C; x is ¬B; ∴ x is C. Tests whether students can apply the disjunctive elimination in the opposite direction.
lr.stimulus: Every work in the exhibition is either a lithograph or an etching. If a work is a lithograph, it was printed from a flat stone surface. The work titled "Harbor at Dusk" is not an etching. Therefore, "Harbor at Dusk" was printed from a flat stone surface.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every sonata on the program is either a Classical sonata or a Romantic sonata. If a sonata is Classical, it follows strict sonata-allegro form. The "Hoffmann Sonata" is not a Romantic sonata. Therefore, the "Hoffmann Sonata" follows strict sonata-allegro form.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every sonata on the program is either Classical or Romantic. Most Classical sonatas follow strict sonata-allegro form. The "Hoffmann Sonata" is not Romantic. Therefore, the "Hoffmann Sonata" probably follows strict sonata-allegro form.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every sonata on the program is either Classical or Romantic. If a sonata is Classical, it follows strict sonata-allegro form. The "Hoffmann Sonata" is Classical. Therefore, the "Hoffmann Sonata" follows strict sonata-allegro form.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a sonata is Classical, it follows strict sonata-allegro form. The "Hoffmann Sonata" does not follow strict sonata-allegro form. Therefore, the "Hoffmann Sonata" is not Classical.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Every sonata on the program is either Classical or Romantic. If a sonata is Romantic, it does not follow strict sonata-allegro form. The "Hoffmann Sonata" follows strict sonata-allegro form. Therefore, the "Hoffmann Sonata" is Classical.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A∨B; A→C; x is ¬B; ∴ x is C. The ¬B premise forces x into the A disjunct by elimination, and A→C delivers the positive conclusion. (A) matches exactly: Classical∨Romantic; Classical→strict form; ¬Romantic; ∴ strict form.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Quantifier weakened to "most," conclusion hedged with "probably" — strength shift on both.
explanations.C: Directly asserts the Classical disjunct rather than deriving it by eliminating the other — removes the disjunctive-elimination step. Only two relevant premises.
explanations.D: Pure two-premise modus tollens with no disjunctive premise — drops the disjunction entirely.
explanations.E: Different conditional (Romantic→¬strict) and reaches conclusion by affirming a property to pick the disjunct — the direction of reasoning is reversed.

lr.difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism stimulus with two premise distractors that share topic but use different forms (one adds an extra premise, one reverses the disjunct direction). Students must formalize A ∨ B; ¬A; ∴ B.
lr.stimulus: The budget shortfall must be addressed either by raising taxes or by cutting services. The city council has ruled out raising taxes. Therefore, services must be cut.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A successful harvest requires either sufficient rainfall or irrigation. This season the farm received sufficient rainfall. Therefore, the harvest will be successful.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every patient must receive either medication or surgery to recover. This patient has not responded to medication. Therefore, this patient must receive surgery to recover.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either the contract was signed before the deadline or it is invalid. Several witnesses confirm it was signed before the deadline. Therefore, the contract is probably valid.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The laboratory can produce results only if both the equipment functions and the reagents are fresh. The reagents are fresh. Therefore, the laboratory can produce results.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The defendant is either guilty of fraud or guilty of negligence. Since the defendant is guilty of fraud, the defendant is not guilty of negligence.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is a disjunctive syllogism: A or B; not A; therefore B. Choice B matches exactly — either medication or surgery; medication has failed (not medication); therefore surgery.
explanations.A: Same-topic trap: this affirms one disjunct and concludes the broader goal is achieved, which is affirming the disjunct — a different, valid structure (sufficient condition met), not disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.B: Correct. Disjunctive syllogism: either medication or surgery; not medication; therefore surgery.
explanations.C: Strength-shift trap: the conclusion says 'probably valid' rather than 'must be valid,' weakening the modal force relative to the stimulus.
explanations.D: Wrong form: this is a conjunction stimulus (both P and Q required), not a disjunction. Only one conjunct is confirmed, making the conclusion actually invalid — a form mismatch.
explanations.E: Same structure inverted: this affirms one disjunct and denies the other, which is the fallacy of affirming a disjunct, not disjunctive syllogism.

lr.difficultyReason: Contrapositive stimulus (modus tollens) with distractors that use modus ponens or affirm the consequent — students must distinguish direction of the conditional.
lr.stimulus: If a species is highly specialized, it will struggle when its environment changes. The Arctic fox has not struggled as its environment has changed. Therefore, the Arctic fox is not highly specialized.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a contract is enforceable, it must include consideration. This contract includes consideration. Therefore, this contract is enforceable.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a new technology is widely adopted, it must be affordable. This technology has not been widely adopted. Therefore, this technology is not affordable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If a painting is by Rembrandt, it will display chiaroscuro. This painting does not display chiaroscuro. Therefore, this painting is not by Rembrandt.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a student studies diligently, the student will pass the examination. This student studied diligently. Therefore, this student will pass the examination.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If a metal is exposed to moisture, it will corrode. This metal has corroded. Therefore, this metal was exposed to moisture.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: If P then Q; not Q; therefore not P (modus tollens / contrapositive). Choice C: If Rembrandt then chiaroscuro; no chiaroscuro; therefore not Rembrandt — identical form.
explanations.A: Affirming the consequent fallacy: if P then Q; Q; therefore P. This is invalid and structurally opposite in direction to modus tollens.
explanations.B: Denying the antecedent fallacy: if P then Q; not P; therefore not Q. This is a common trap — the negation is in the wrong position.
explanations.C: Correct. Modus tollens: If Rembrandt → chiaroscuro; not chiaroscuro; therefore not Rembrandt.
explanations.D: Modus ponens: if P then Q; P; therefore Q. Different valid form — affirms the antecedent rather than denying the consequent.
explanations.E: Affirming the consequent: if exposure then corrosion; corrosion occurred; therefore exposure. Invalid form, structurally distinct from modus tollens.

lr.difficultyReason: Universal-to-particular (categorical syllogism: All A are B; x is A; ∴ x is B) with distractors using 'most' or 'some' to create strength-shift traps.
lr.stimulus: Every regulation passed by the legislature that conflicts with the constitution is invalid. The emergency housing decree conflicts with the constitution. Therefore, the emergency housing decree is invalid.
lr.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most medications that interact with anticoagulants are contraindicated for post-operative patients. This antibiotic interacts with anticoagulants. Therefore, this antibiotic is probably contraindicated for post-operative patients.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every metal that conducts electricity can be used in circuit boards. Copper conducts electricity. Therefore, copper can be used in circuit boards.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some tax shelters that exploit offshore accounts are illegal. This investment scheme exploits offshore accounts. Therefore, this investment scheme is illegal.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No language that lacks written records can be fully reconstructed. Ancient Elamite lacks written records. Therefore, Ancient Elamite cannot be fully reconstructed.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Every employee who meets the performance benchmarks receives a bonus. Several employees received bonuses last quarter. Therefore, those employees met the performance benchmarks.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B. Choice B matches: all metals that conduct electricity can be used in circuit boards; copper conducts electricity; therefore copper can be used in circuit boards.
explanations.A: Strength-shift trap: uses 'most' instead of 'every,' downgrading the universal quantifier, making the conclusion only probable rather than certain.
explanations.B: Correct. All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B — perfect universal-to-particular match.
explanations.C: Quantifier trap: 'some A are B; x is A; therefore x is B' is an invalid inference. The existential 'some' does not support a particular conclusion about x.
explanations.D: Same-premise-count but different form: 'No A can B; x is A; therefore x cannot B' — this is a universal negative syllogism (celarent), structurally distinct from the affirmative universal in the stimulus.
explanations.E: Affirming the consequent in categorical form: All A are B; x is B; therefore x is A — the direction is reversed.

lr.difficultyReason: Conditional chain (A → B; B → C; A; ∴ C) with distractors that interrupt the chain or use the chain without affirming the antecedent.
lr.stimulus: Whenever inflation rises sharply, consumer confidence falls. Whenever consumer confidence falls, retail sales decline. Inflation has risen sharply. Therefore, retail sales will decline.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whenever a forest fire occurs, air quality deteriorates. Whenever air quality deteriorates, respiratory illness rates rise. A forest fire has occurred. Therefore, respiratory illness rates will rise.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a diplomat is recalled, tensions between nations increase. If tensions between nations increase, trade is disrupted. Trade has been disrupted. Therefore, a diplomat was recalled.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whenever drought conditions persist, crop yields fall. Crop yields have fallen in the northern region. Therefore, drought conditions must have persisted in the northern region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a software update is released, users must restart their devices. If users restart their devices, unsaved work is lost. A software update was released. Therefore, unsaved work may be lost.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whenever interest rates rise, borrowing costs increase. Whenever borrowing costs increase, housing starts fall. Interest rates have not risen. Therefore, housing starts will not fall.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A → B; B → C; A; ∴ C. Choice A matches exactly: fire → air quality deteriorates → illness rises; fire occurred; therefore illness rises.
explanations.A: Correct. Three-premise conditional chain with antecedent affirmed — identical structure.
explanations.B: Affirming the consequent in the chain: presents A → B; B → C; C; therefore A — the consequent is affirmed to reach the antecedent, which is an invalid form.
explanations.C: This is a two-premise modus tollens chain variant: only one conditional; and the conclusion is reached by affirming the consequent, making it invalid — both count and form diverge.
explanations.D: Strength-shift trap: conclusion says 'may be lost' rather than 'will be lost,' weakening the modal force despite having the correct chain structure.
explanations.E: Denying the antecedent fallacy: A → B; B → C; ¬A; ∴ ¬C. The negation is applied to the antecedent, not the consequent.

lr.difficultyReason: Analogy stimulus (X resembles Y in two key respects; Y has property R; ∴ X has R) with distractors that use only one respect or reverse the direction of analogy.
lr.stimulus: The new compound shares with penicillin both its molecular ring structure and its mechanism of disrupting bacterial cell walls. Penicillin is effective against streptococcal infections. Therefore, the new compound is likely effective against streptococcal infections.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: This bridge design shares with the Golden Gate Bridge both its cable suspension system and its load-distribution geometry. The Golden Gate Bridge has withstood major seismic events. Therefore, this bridge design will likely withstand major seismic events.

choices.label: B
choices.text: This sculpture is made of marble and depicts a reclining figure. Most classical sculptures depict reclining figures. Therefore, this sculpture is probably classical.

choices.label: C
choices.text: This vineyard has the same altitude and rainfall as a celebrated Burgundy vineyard. Wine from the Burgundy vineyard ages well. Therefore, wine from this vineyard will certainly age well.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The new fuel cell shares its hydrogen-oxidation mechanism with conventional batteries. Conventional batteries power electric vehicles effectively. Therefore, the new fuel cell is probably a type of conventional battery.

choices.label: E
choices.text: This novel and the prize-winning novel both explore themes of exile and memory. Therefore, this novel will probably win a prize.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: X shares two properties with Y; Y has result R; therefore X likely has R. Choice A: new bridge shares two structural features with Golden Gate; Golden Gate withstands seismic events; therefore new bridge will likely do so.
explanations.A: Correct. Two shared respects established, then a property of the analogue is transferred to the subject via 'likely' — exact structural match.
