explanations.B: Same-topic trap plus base-rate reversal: notes one shared feature and then reasons backward from a general pattern to classify the particular item, which is a different form.
explanations.C: Strength-shift trap: the conclusion uses 'certainly' rather than 'likely,' escalating the modal force beyond what the analogical form supports.
explanations.D: Conclusion-type mismatch: the conclusion classifies the subject as a type of the analogue ('is a type of conventional battery') rather than attributing a property to it — different logical goal.
explanations.E: Premise-count trap: only one shared property (theme) is noted, and the analogue's prize-winning is presupposed rather than stated as a premise, making the structure deficient.

lr.difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism with three answer-choice traps: one extra premise, one affirms a disjunct, one uses a conjunction instead of disjunction. Students must identify A ∨ B; ¬B; ∴ A.
lr.stimulus: The manuscript was written either in the fourteenth century or in the fifteenth century. Paleographic analysis has established that it was not written in the fifteenth century. Therefore, the manuscript was written in the fourteenth century.
lr.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The volcanic eruption originated either from a shallow magma chamber or from a deep mantle plume. Seismic data confirm it originated from a deep mantle plume. Therefore, it did not originate from a shallow magma chamber.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The artifact was produced either by the Minoan civilization or by the Mycenaean civilization. Isotope analysis rules out Mycenaean origin. Therefore, the artifact was produced by the Minoan civilization.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The policy failure resulted either from poor planning, from inadequate funding, or from weak enforcement. Investigators have ruled out poor planning and inadequate funding. Therefore, the failure resulted from weak enforcement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The signal was transmitted either by satellite or by fiber optic cable, and it was encrypted. The signal was transmitted by satellite. Therefore, the signal was encrypted and transmitted by satellite.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The theorem was proved either by induction or by contradiction. Since the proof used contradiction, the theorem is valid.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A or B; not B; therefore A. Choice B: Minoan or Mycenaean; not Mycenaean; therefore Minoan — perfect disjunctive syllogism match with two disjuncts.
explanations.A: Affirms one disjunct and denies the other — the opposite direction. The conclusion denies rather than affirms the remaining option, though the form is the fallacy of affirming a disjunct.
explanations.B: Correct. Two-disjunct disjunctive syllogism with the second disjunct eliminated.
explanations.C: Premise-count trap: this is a three-disjunct version, requiring two eliminations before concluding. The structure has an extra elimination step not present in the stimulus.
explanations.D: Conjunction trap: introduces an independent conjunct ('and it was encrypted') that makes the premise structure a conjunction with a disjunction, not a simple disjunction.
explanations.E: Conclusion-type mismatch: the conclusion ('the theorem is valid') does not follow from which proof method was used — the reasoning introduces an unsupported claim, making it invalid and structurally mismatched.

lr.difficultyReason: Modus tollens (contrapositive) stimulus in an ethics domain; distractors use modus ponens, denying the antecedent, or affirming the consequent — students must track conditional direction carefully.
lr.stimulus: Any action that violates a person's autonomy without consent is morally impermissible. The proposed surveillance program does not violate anyone's autonomy without consent. Therefore, the proposed surveillance program is not morally impermissible on those grounds.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any ingredient that triggers an allergic reaction in a patient must be excluded from the formulation. Casein triggers an allergic reaction in this patient. Therefore, casein must be excluded from the formulation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Any construction project that exceeds its budget is subject to a compliance review. This project has not exceeded its budget. Therefore, this project is not subject to a compliance review on those grounds.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any judicial ruling that contradicts precedent must be reviewed by the appellate court. This ruling has been reviewed by the appellate court. Therefore, this ruling contradicted precedent.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any policy that reduces greenhouse gas emissions should be adopted. The carbon tax reduces greenhouse gas emissions. Therefore, the carbon tax should be adopted.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Any artist who does not submit work by the deadline is disqualified. This artist has been disqualified. Therefore, this artist did not submit work by the deadline.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: All A are B (impermissible); x is not A (does not violate autonomy without consent); therefore x is not B (not impermissible) — modus tollens on the universal: denying membership in the trigger class to deny membership in the consequence class.
explanations.A: Modus ponens: All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B — affirms the antecedent rather than denying it.
explanations.B: Correct. All A are B; x is not A; therefore x is not B — same form as the stimulus, denying the antecedent class to deny the consequent class (valid here because 'any' makes B conditional solely on A).
explanations.C: Affirming the consequent in categorical form: All A must B; x did B; therefore x is A — invalid and directionally reversed.
explanations.D: Modus ponens: All A should be adopted; x is A; therefore x should be adopted — correct form is different (antecedent affirmed).
explanations.E: Affirming the consequent: All not-submit are disqualified; x is disqualified; therefore x did not submit — reversed conditional direction.

lr.difficultyReason: Conditional chain where the antecedent is negated at the conclusion step; tests whether students can track a two-step chain and correctly apply the affirmed antecedent, with distractors that break the chain or shift strength.
lr.stimulus: Whenever a river's sediment load increases, its delta expands. Whenever a delta expands, coastal wetlands are displaced. The sediment load of the Nile River has increased. Therefore, coastal wetlands along the Nile will be displaced.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whenever a government subsidizes an industry, domestic production rises. Whenever domestic production rises, import reliance falls. The government has subsidized the steel industry. Therefore, import reliance in steel will fall.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Whenever a central bank raises interest rates, borrowing slows. Borrowing has slowed in the current economy. Therefore, the central bank has raised interest rates.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whenever a language loses native speakers, it becomes endangered. Whenever it becomes endangered, preservation efforts increase. Preservation efforts for Cornish have increased. Therefore, Cornish has lost native speakers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whenever a composer writes in a minor key, the piece evokes melancholy. This piece evokes melancholy. Therefore, the composer wrote it in a minor key.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whenever a drought occurs, water restrictions are imposed. Water restrictions have not been imposed in this region. Therefore, a drought has not occurred in this region.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A → B; B → C; A; ∴ C. Choice A: subsidy → production rises → import reliance falls; subsidy occurred; therefore import reliance falls — identical three-premise conditional chain.
explanations.A: Correct. Two conditionals chained, antecedent of the first affirmed, conclusion is the consequent of the second.
explanations.B: Affirming the consequent: A → B; B; therefore A. Only one conditional used, and the direction is reversed.
explanations.C: Affirming the consequent at the end of a chain: A → B; B → C; C; therefore A — the chain runs backward from the final consequent.
explanations.D: Single conditional with affirming the consequent: A → B; B; therefore A. Both premise count and direction mismatch.
explanations.E: Modus tollens on a single conditional: A → B; ¬B; therefore ¬A. Only one premise and uses contrapositive, not chain.

lr.difficultyReason: Universal negative syllogism (No A are B; x is A; ∴ x is not B) with distractors using affirmative universals, strength-softening, or reversed quantifiers.
lr.stimulus: No algorithm that relies solely on historical data can accurately predict unprecedented market events. The firm's trading algorithm relies solely on historical data. Therefore, the firm's trading algorithm cannot accurately predict unprecedented market events.
lr.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No surgical procedure performed without informed consent is ethically permissible. This procedure was performed without informed consent. Therefore, this procedure is not ethically permissible.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most diagnostic tests that rely on a single biomarker are unreliable. This test relies on a single biomarker. Therefore, this test is probably unreliable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No poem written in strict meter can capture the randomness of spoken language. This poem does not capture the randomness of spoken language. Therefore, this poem was written in strict meter.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All governance frameworks that lack independent oversight are prone to corruption. This framework lacks independent oversight. Therefore, this framework is prone to corruption.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some investment strategies that ignore macroeconomic trends produce poor returns. This strategy ignores macroeconomic trends. Therefore, this strategy will produce poor returns.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: No A are B; x is A; therefore x is not B. Choice A: No consent-free procedure is ethically permissible; this procedure lacks consent; therefore it is not permissible — identical universal negative syllogism.
explanations.A: Correct. Universal negative premise + singular affirming the subject category = singular negative conclusion.
explanations.B: Quantifier-shift trap: uses 'most' instead of 'no,' reducing the universal negative to a probabilistic claim and softening the conclusion to 'probably.'
explanations.C: Affirming the consequent of a universal negative in categorical form: No A is B; x is not B; therefore x is A — reversed direction, invalid.
explanations.D: Affirmative universal trap: 'All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B' — the premise is affirmative, not negative, giving a structurally distinct syllogism.
explanations.E: Existential quantifier trap: 'Some A are B; x is A; therefore x is B' — an invalid inference from 'some,' mismatching both quantifier type and validity.

lr.difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism combined with a conditional conclusion (A ∨ B; ¬A; B → C; ∴ C) slightly extending the standard two-premise form; distractors omit one step or reverse the elimination.
lr.stimulus: The exhibit was funded either through private donations or through a government grant. It was not funded through private donations. Any exhibit funded through a government grant is subject to public audit. Therefore, the exhibit is subject to public audit.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The suspect traveled either by train or by car. The suspect traveled by train. Any suspect who travels by train passes through a monitored station. Therefore, the suspect passed through a monitored station.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The package was shipped either by air or by sea. It was not shipped by air. Any package shipped by sea is subject to customs inspection. Therefore, the package is subject to customs inspection.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The grant was awarded either for research or for outreach. It was awarded for research. Research grants require annual reporting. Outreach grants do not require annual reporting. Therefore, this grant requires annual reporting.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The building was designed either by a licensed architect or by an unlicensed contractor. Any building designed by an unlicensed contractor is a code violation. Therefore, the building may be a code violation.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The film was screened either at a festival or at a commercial venue. It was not screened at a festival. Commercial venues charge admission fees. Therefore, the film probably generated revenue.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A ∨ B; ¬A; therefore B; B → C; therefore C — disjunctive syllogism feeding a conditional. Choice B: air or sea; not air; therefore sea; sea → customs inspection; therefore customs inspection. Exact three-premise match.
explanations.A: Affirms rather than eliminates a disjunct: 'traveled by train' is asserted directly (not via elimination of the other disjunct), so the disjunctive syllogism step is absent.
explanations.B: Correct. Eliminates one disjunct (not air), derives the other (sea), then applies the conditional (sea → customs) to reach the conclusion.
explanations.C: Premise-count and conclusion-type trap: adds an extra contrasting conditional for outreach (not in the stimulus structure) and includes an irrelevant fourth premise, making it a more complex argument form.
explanations.D: Missing elimination step: the disjunction is stated but neither disjunct is eliminated — the argument leaps directly to a weakened probable conclusion without completing the disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.E: Strength-shift and conclusion-mismatch: conclusion is 'probably generated revenue' rather than the direct consequence required by the structure, and 'generated revenue' is not the direct consequent of 'commercial venue' but an additional inference.

lr.difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism (A or B; not A; therefore B). Students must formalize the stimulus and distinguish it from conditionals and contrapositives in the distractors. Topic varies across choices to prevent content matching.
lr.stimulus: Either the budget shortfall was caused by increased spending or it was caused by a decline in tax revenue. The auditors confirmed that spending did not increase during the relevant period. Therefore, the budget shortfall was caused by a decline in tax revenue.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If the bridge collapsed due to metal fatigue, then it was inspected improperly. The bridge did collapse due to metal fatigue. Therefore, it was inspected improperly.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The patient's symptoms result from either a viral infection or an allergic reaction. Laboratory tests have ruled out any viral infection. Therefore, the symptoms result from an allergic reaction.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whenever production costs rise, retail prices increase. Retail prices have not increased. Therefore, production costs have not risen.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All volcanic eruptions produce ash deposits or lava flows. The eruption at Mount Crale produced lava flows. Therefore, it produced no ash deposits.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The construction delay was caused by poor planning. Poor planning is always attributable to management failure. Therefore, the construction delay was attributable to management failure.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is a disjunctive syllogism: A or B; not A; therefore B. Choice B has the same structure: viral infection or allergic reaction; not viral infection; therefore allergic reaction. Both premises and conclusion match exactly.
explanations.A: This is modus ponens (A → B; A; therefore B) — a conditional argument, not a disjunctive syllogism. Different structure.
explanations.B: Correct. Matches disjunctive syllogism perfectly.
explanations.C: This is modus tollens / contrapositive (A → B; not B; therefore not A). The structure is a denied consequent, not elimination of a disjunct.
explanations.D: This treats an 'or' as exclusive and affirms one disjunct to deny the other — a formal fallacy. The stimulus is valid; this is not structurally parallel.
explanations.E: This is a conditional chain (A → B; B → C; therefore A → C) applied to a particular case — different structure from disjunctive syllogism.

lr.difficultyReason: Modus tollens (contrapositive) stimulus: A → B; not B; therefore not A. Distractors include modus ponens, disjunctive syllogism, and a topic-matching trap. Students must identify the denied consequent structure.
lr.stimulus: If a new drug has been approved by the regulatory agency, then it has passed clinical trials. The drug Veritam has not passed clinical trials. Therefore, Veritam has not been approved by the regulatory agency.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All approved medications must meet safety standards. Veritam meets safety standards. Therefore, Veritam is an approved medication.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If a sculpture is displayed in the national gallery, it has been authenticated by an expert. The sculpture known as Blue Form has not been authenticated by any expert. Therefore, Blue Form is not displayed in the national gallery.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either the building is structurally sound or it must be demolished. The building is not structurally sound. Therefore, it must be demolished.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a product is certified organic, it was grown without synthetic pesticides. This tomato was grown without synthetic pesticides. Therefore, this tomato is certified organic.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Whenever a law is challenged in court, it receives public scrutiny. This law has received public scrutiny. Therefore, it was challenged in court.

explanations.correct: The stimulus uses modus tollens: displayed → authenticated; not authenticated; therefore not displayed. Choice B mirrors this exactly: gallery → authenticated by expert; not authenticated; therefore not in gallery.
explanations.A: Commits the fallacy of affirming the consequent (all A→B; x is B; therefore x is A). The stimulus is valid modus tollens; this is invalid.
explanations.B: Correct. Modus tollens matching the stimulus perfectly.
explanations.C: Disjunctive syllogism (A or B; not A; therefore B). Different argument form.
explanations.D: Affirms the consequent (certified → no pesticides; no pesticides; therefore certified) — invalid and structurally different.
explanations.E: Also affirms the consequent (challenged → scrutiny; scrutiny; therefore challenged) — invalid fallacy, not parallel to valid modus tollens.

lr.difficultyReason: Universal-to-particular instantiation (All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B). Distractors include a scope-shift trap and a reversed-universal trap. Students must confirm both universality and category membership.
lr.stimulus: Every treaty ratified by the Senate becomes binding international law. The Accord of Lismore was ratified by the Senate. Therefore, the Accord of Lismore is binding international law.
lr.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Most volcanic islands have fertile soil due to mineral-rich lava. Kela Island is a volcanic island. Therefore, Kela Island probably has fertile soil.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All peer-reviewed studies are subject to editorial scrutiny. Some nutritional claims are not subject to editorial scrutiny. Therefore, some nutritional claims are not based on peer-reviewed studies.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every musical composition registered with the copyright office is legally protected. The piece titled Nocturne in F is registered with the copyright office. Therefore, Nocturne in F is legally protected.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All rivers that originate in glaciers carry sediment. The Vorlan River carries sediment. Therefore, the Vorlan River originates in a glacier.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some languages with tonal systems are found in Southeast Asia. Mandarin has a tonal system. Therefore, Mandarin is found in Southeast Asia.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B (universal instantiation). Choice C: All registered works are legally protected; Nocturne in F is registered; therefore it is legally protected. Perfect structural match.
explanations.A: Uses 'most' rather than 'all,' and the conclusion uses 'probably' — both the quantifier strength and conclusion modality differ from the stimulus.
explanations.B: This is a universal syllogism eliminating a class (All A → B; some C are not B; therefore some C are not A) — different structure, more complex.
explanations.D: Affirms the consequent (all glacier-origin → sediment; carries sediment; therefore glacier-origin) — invalid, unlike the valid stimulus.
explanations.E: Uses 'some' instead of 'all' and draws a particular conclusion from a particular premise — different quantifier logic.
explanations.C: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Conditional chain (A → B; B → C; A; therefore C). Distractors share a chain-like surface structure but misorder links or introduce a disjunct. Students must track both the chain and the affirmed antecedent.
lr.stimulus: Whenever a city's population grows rapidly, housing demand outpaces supply. Whenever housing demand outpaces supply, rental prices rise sharply. The population of Denverton is growing rapidly. Therefore, rental prices in Denverton will rise sharply.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If soil acidity increases, nitrogen-fixing bacteria die off. If nitrogen-fixing bacteria die off, crop yields decline. The soil acidity in the Farlow Valley has increased. Therefore, crop yields in the Farlow Valley will decline.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Whenever interest rates rise, consumer spending falls. Consumer spending in Westmark has fallen. Therefore, interest rates in Westmark have risen.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If a company loses market share, it either cuts costs or raises prices. Redmont Industries has lost market share. Therefore, Redmont Industries will cut costs or raise prices.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Overfishing leads to ecosystem collapse. Ecosystem collapse leads to loss of biodiversity. Loss of biodiversity leads to species extinction. Overfishing is occurring in the Naral Sea. Therefore, species extinction will occur in the Naral Sea.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If deforestation increases, soil erosion accelerates. Soil erosion is not accelerating in the Pelmore region. Therefore, deforestation is not increasing in the Pelmore region.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is a two-link conditional chain plus affirmed antecedent: A→B; B→C; A; therefore C. Choice A matches exactly: soil acidity → bacteria die; bacteria die → yields decline; acidity increased; therefore yields decline.
explanations.B: This affirms the consequent of a single conditional — a fallacy, and only one premise rather than a two-link chain.
explanations.C: This is a single conditional leading to a disjunctive conclusion (A → B or C) — the stimulus has a two-link chain, not a disjunctive consequent.
explanations.D: Three-link chain (A→B→C→D) rather than two — same family but different premise count, violating the structural match.
explanations.E: Modus tollens on a single conditional (A→B; not B; therefore not A) — denies consequent rather than affirming antecedent through a chain.
explanations.A: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Analogy argument (X and Y share properties P and Q; Y has R; therefore X has R). Distractors use universal instantiation or inductive generalization, which are easy to conflate with analogical reasoning.
lr.stimulus: The Karven Bridge and the Telston Overpass were both built using the same steel alloy and the same suspension design. Engineers have determined that the Telston Overpass is vulnerable to harmonic oscillation failure. Therefore, the Karven Bridge is also vulnerable to harmonic oscillation failure.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All languages in the Dravidian family share a subject-object-verb word order. Tamil is a Dravidian language. Therefore, Tamil has subject-object-verb word order.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Novel X and Novel Y were both written in the same era and employ the same unreliable-narrator technique. Novel Y has been found to contain intentional anachronisms. Therefore, Novel X also contains intentional anachronisms.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Medrano Glacier and the Pelso Glacier are both receding. Most glaciers that recede are in regions experiencing elevated temperatures. Therefore, the Medrano Glacier is probably in a region experiencing elevated temperatures.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either compound A or compound B inhibits the enzyme. Compound A has been shown not to inhibit the enzyme in this sample. Therefore, compound B inhibits the enzyme in this sample.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Crestwood fire was caused by dry conditions and high winds. Fires caused by dry conditions and high winds spread rapidly. Therefore, the Crestwood fire spread rapidly.

explanations.correct: The stimulus argues by analogy: X and Y share properties P and Q; Y has property R; therefore X has R. Choice B exactly mirrors this: Novel X and Novel Y share era and technique; Novel Y has anachronisms; therefore Novel X does too.
explanations.A: This is universal instantiation (All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B), not an analogy between two particular things sharing stated properties.
explanations.C: Combines a shared property with a probabilistic inference from a majority claim — different structure and uses 'probably,' weakening the conclusion relative to the stimulus.
explanations.D: Disjunctive syllogism (A or B; not A; therefore B) — entirely different argument form.
explanations.E: This is universal instantiation: the fire has properties P and Q; all things with P and Q have R; therefore this fire has R. Not an analogy between two particular objects.
explanations.B: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Contrapositive with a negated antecedent setup: All A that are B are C; x is not C; therefore x is not both A and B. Distractors include a correct-topic but wrong-direction trap and an affirmation trap.
lr.stimulus: Every physician who prescribes off-label medications is required to document the rationale. Dr. Harwell has not documented any rationale. Therefore, Dr. Harwell has not prescribed any off-label medications.
lr.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every contractor who uses substandard materials must pay a penalty. Brisco Construction has paid a penalty. Therefore, Brisco Construction used substandard materials.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every architect who submits a design to the competition must include a cost estimate. Lena Forst did not include a cost estimate. Therefore, Lena Forst did not submit a design to the competition.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any student who fails two exams is placed on academic probation. Marko has been placed on academic probation. Therefore, Marko failed two exams.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All species listed as endangered receive federal protection. The Borrelia moth is not listed as endangered. Therefore, the Borrelia moth does not receive federal protection.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Every pilot certified for international routes must pass a language proficiency exam. Captain Vasil has passed the language proficiency exam. Therefore, Captain Vasil is certified for international routes.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is modus tollens on a universal: All A→B; x is not B; therefore x is not A. Choice B: all architects who submit → include cost estimate; Forst did not include cost estimate; therefore Forst did not submit. Perfect match.
explanations.A: Affirms the consequent (all users of substandard → penalty; paid penalty; therefore used substandard) — invalid fallacy, unlike the valid stimulus.
explanations.C: Also affirms the consequent (fails two → probation; on probation; therefore failed two) — invalid, structurally different.
explanations.D: This is actually a valid inference but uses 'not A; therefore not B' (denies antecedent) — a different and invalid form. Does not match modus tollens.
explanations.E: Affirms the consequent (certified → passed exam; passed exam; therefore certified) — invalid and structurally distinct.
explanations.B: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism with negated second disjunct (A or B; not B; therefore A). Distractors include negating the first disjunct (which would also yield B — testing whether students track which disjunct is denied) and a conditional trap.
lr.stimulus: The decline in the monarch butterfly population is due either to loss of milkweed habitat or to widespread pesticide exposure. Research has shown that milkweed habitat has actually expanded in recent years. Therefore, the decline is due to widespread pesticide exposure.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The server outage was caused either by a hardware malfunction or by a software error. Diagnostics confirmed a hardware malfunction. Therefore, no software error caused the outage.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the harvest fails, the cooperative will take out loans. The cooperative has not taken out loans. Therefore, the harvest has not failed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The team's poor performance results either from inadequate training or from low morale. An investigation found no evidence of low morale. Therefore, the poor performance results from inadequate training.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Either the painting is a forgery or it was produced before 1850. The painting was produced before 1850. Therefore, the painting is not a forgery.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rising sea temperatures cause coral bleaching. Coral bleaching has been observed on the Narova Reef. Therefore, sea temperatures near the Narova Reef have been rising.

explanations.correct: The stimulus eliminates one disjunct to conclude the other: A or B; not A (habitat expanded, so loss of habitat is ruled out); therefore B. Choice C: inadequate training or low morale; no low morale; therefore inadequate training. Exact match.
explanations.A: Affirms one disjunct (A or B; A is confirmed) and concludes not B — this treats 'or' as exclusive, which is invalid for standard inclusive disjunction. The stimulus denies a disjunct, not affirms one.
explanations.B: Modus tollens on a single conditional (A→B; not B; therefore not A) — different form.
explanations.D: Same trap as A: affirms one disjunct to deny the other — invalid and structurally different from the stimulus's denial of a disjunct.
explanations.E: Affirms the consequent (temperature rises → bleaching; bleaching observed; therefore temperatures rising) — invalid fallacy, different form.
explanations.C: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Two-premise conditional modus ponens applied to a class claim: All A that are B have C; this thing is A and B; therefore it has C. Distractors include a reversed-universal (C→A) and a topic-match trap on a different form.
lr.stimulus: Any technology that processes personal data and operates across national borders is subject to international privacy regulations. This social media platform processes personal data and operates across national borders. Therefore, this social media platform is subject to international privacy regulations.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any organism that reproduces asexually and lacks a nucleus is classified as a prokaryote. This bacterium reproduces asexually and lacks a nucleus. Therefore, this bacterium is classified as a prokaryote.

choices.label: B
choices.text: This social media platform has been found to violate privacy regulations. Any platform that violates privacy regulations is eventually fined. Therefore, this platform will eventually be fined.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most technologies operating across national borders face regulatory challenges. This platform operates across national borders. Therefore, this platform probably faces regulatory challenges.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some data-processing companies are subject to international privacy regulations. This social media company processes data. Therefore, this social media company is subject to international privacy regulations.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Any device subject to international privacy regulations must use end-to-end encryption. This application uses end-to-end encryption. Therefore, this application is subject to international privacy regulations.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is: All things that are [A and B] are C; x is [A and B]; therefore x is C. Choice A: All organisms that [reproduce asexually and lack a nucleus] are prokaryotes; this bacterium [reproduces asexually and lacks a nucleus]; therefore it is a prokaryote. Exact match with two conjunctive conditions.
explanations.B: This is a single-condition modus ponens (violates → fined), not a two-conjunct universal. Also, it shares topic with the stimulus — a content-matching trap.
explanations.C: Uses 'most' instead of 'any/all,' yielding a probabilistic conclusion ('probably') — quantifier and conclusion strength differ from the stimulus.
explanations.D: Uses 'some' as the universal premise, making the inference invalid (some A are C; x is A; therefore x is C is a fallacy). Structurally different.
explanations.E: Affirms the consequent (subject to regulations → encryption; uses encryption; therefore subject to regulations) — invalid fallacy, different structure.
explanations.A: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Argument from elimination using an exhaustive list: A, B, or C must be true; not A; not B; therefore C. Distractors include two-option disjunctions and a modus tollens trap. Students must match the three-option exhaustive structure.
lr.stimulus: The gallery's missing painting was removed by a staff member, a visitor, or a contractor working on the premises. Security footage rules out any staff member, and badge records confirm no contractor was present that day. Therefore, the painting was removed by a visitor.
lr.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The signal failure was caused by weather interference or equipment degradation. Tests showed no weather interference. Therefore, the failure was caused by equipment degradation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The delegation will meet in Geneva, Vienna, or Brussels. The Geneva venue is unavailable, and the Vienna venue has been rejected by one party. Therefore, the meeting will be held in Brussels.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If the stock price drops, the company will issue bonds. The company has not issued bonds. Therefore, the stock price has not dropped.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every ancient coin in the collection was minted in Rome, Athens, or Carthage. This coin was minted in Athens. Therefore, this coin is an ancient coin in the collection.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Either the new policy will reduce costs or it will improve efficiency. The policy has not reduced costs. Therefore, it will improve efficiency.

explanations.correct: The stimulus eliminates two of three exhaustive options to conclude the third: A or B or C; not A; not B; therefore C. Choice B: Geneva, Vienna, or Brussels; not Geneva; not Vienna; therefore Brussels. Three-option exhaustive elimination matches perfectly.
explanations.A: Only two disjuncts (A or B; not A; therefore B) — a standard disjunctive syllogism missing the third option that defines the stimulus's structure.
explanations.C: Modus tollens (A→B; not B; therefore not A) — entirely different form with no disjunction.
explanations.D: Affirms the consequent in a universal (all collection coins are from A/B/C; this is from B; therefore it is a collection coin) — invalid and different structure.
explanations.E: Two-option disjunction, like A — does not match the three-option exhaustive elimination of the stimulus.
explanations.B: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Argument combining a general principle with a comparative particular: If X has more of property P than Y, and Y is sufficient for outcome O, then X also achieves O. Distractors include a premise-count trap and a threshold confusion trap.
lr.stimulus: Any soil with a pH below 5.5 is too acidic to support wheat cultivation. The soil in the northern fields has a pH of 4.8, which is lower than 5.5. Therefore, the northern fields cannot support wheat cultivation.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A building requires at least twelve support columns to meet safety codes. The Farnam structure has only nine support columns. Therefore, the Farnam structure does not meet safety codes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most clinical trials require a minimum of one hundred participants to yield statistically valid results. This trial enrolled eighty participants. Therefore, this trial probably did not yield statistically valid results.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If an applicant scores below 70 on the licensing exam, the applicant fails. If the applicant fails, a re-examination is required. Applicant Moro scored 65. Therefore, Moro must undergo re-examination.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Holvane River is too shallow for commercial navigation. The Trest Canal is even shallower than the Holvane River. Therefore, the Trest Canal is also too shallow for commercial navigation.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No wine produced in the Caldera region contains more than 13% alcohol. This bottle is produced in the Caldera region. Therefore, this bottle does not contain more than 13% alcohol.

explanations.correct: The stimulus applies a threshold rule to a particular case: anything below threshold T cannot achieve O; x is below T; therefore x cannot achieve O. Choice A: anything with fewer than 12 columns fails codes; Farnam has 9 (below 12); therefore Farnam fails codes. Exact structural match including the explicit threshold comparison.
explanations.B: Uses 'most' rather than a universal rule, and concludes 'probably' — both the quantifier and the conclusion's modal force differ from the stimulus.
explanations.C: Two-link conditional chain (below 70 → fails; fails → re-exam; scored 65; therefore re-exam) — an extra inferential step not present in the stimulus.
explanations.D: Analogy by comparative degree (X is too Y; Z is even more Y than X; therefore Z is also too Y) — a comparative analogy, not a threshold-rule application to a particular value.
explanations.E: Universal instantiation (no Caldera wine exceeds 13%; this is Caldera wine; therefore it doesn't exceed 13%) — different form: no threshold comparison, just category membership.
explanations.A: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism stimulus (A or B; ¬A; ∴ B) with distractors that share legal subject matter but use modus ponens or invalid forms, requiring students to formalize the structure.
lr.stimulus: The defendant either acted in self-defense or committed an unprovoked assault. The evidence conclusively rules out self-defense. Therefore, the defendant committed an unprovoked assault.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The soil sample contains either limestone or granite. Laboratory analysis has confirmed that the sample contains no limestone. Therefore, the sample contains granite.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the reactor core overheats, a meltdown will occur. The reactor core has overheated. Therefore, a meltdown will occur.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most treaties either create obligations or confer rights. This treaty creates obligations. Therefore, it probably does not confer rights.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The suspect could not have committed the robbery, since the robbery required physical strength and the suspect lacks physical strength.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Either the painting is a forgery or it was produced before 1800. Experts believe it was produced before 1800. Therefore, it is not a forgery.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is a disjunctive syllogism: A or B; ¬A; ∴ B. Choice A matches exactly — either limestone or granite; no limestone; therefore granite. Both premises and conclusion have the same form.
explanations.A: Correct. Disjunctive syllogism: A or B; ¬A; ∴ B — identical structure to the stimulus.
explanations.B: Trap: modus ponens (if A then B; A; ∴ B). Valid but a different logical form from the stimulus.
explanations.C: Trap: same-topic distractor using 'most' (a probabilistic quantifier) rather than an exhaustive disjunction, and the conclusion does not follow with certainty.
explanations.D: Trap: modus tollens or reductio structure (B requires A; ¬A; ∴ ¬B). Different form and no explicit disjunction.
explanations.E: Trap: inverts the disjunctive syllogism — the surviving disjunct is affirmed (belief in B), and the conclusion denies A. This treats disjunction as exclusive and reasons backward, which is invalid.

lr.difficultyReason: Contrapositive stimulus (A → B; ¬B; ∴ ¬A) with distractors using the same medical domain or affirming the consequent, requiring students to distinguish modus tollens from modus ponens.
lr.stimulus: Any patient who undergoes the surgical procedure will require post-operative physical therapy. This patient did not undergo post-operative physical therapy. Therefore, this patient did not undergo the surgical procedure.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every licensed architect must pass the national examination. Sonja has passed the national examination. Therefore, Sonja is a licensed architect.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All certified organic farms must rotate their crops annually. The Greenfield farm did not rotate its crops this year. Therefore, the Greenfield farm is not a certified organic farm.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If a language has tonal phonemes, its speakers must distinguish pitch carefully. Mandarin speakers distinguish pitch carefully. Therefore, Mandarin is a tonal language.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whenever inflation rises sharply, central banks raise interest rates. The central bank has raised interest rates. Therefore, inflation has risen sharply.

choices.label: E
choices.text: A patient requires physical therapy only if the injury is severe. This patient's injury is severe. Therefore, this patient requires physical therapy.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: All A → B; ¬B; ∴ ¬A (modus tollens / contrapositive). Choice B: All certified organic farms → rotate crops; Greenfield did not rotate; ∴ Greenfield is not certified organic. Perfect structural match.
explanations.A: Trap: affirms the consequent (All A → B; B; ∴ A). Invalid form that inverts the conditional direction.
explanations.B: Correct. Modus tollens — universal conditional with denial of consequent yielding denial of antecedent.
explanations.C: Trap: same as A — affirms the consequent. Uses linguistics domain to disguise the form.
explanations.D: Trap: same form as A and C — affirms the consequent. Economics domain disguises the structural error.
explanations.E: Trap: same-topic (physical therapy) distractor using modus ponens (A → B; A; ∴ B), not modus tollens.

lr.difficultyReason: Conditional chain (A → B; B → C; A; ∴ C) stimulus in ethics domain; distractors break the chain at different points or reverse a conditional, requiring careful tracking of three steps.
lr.stimulus: Whenever a corporation knowingly deceives consumers, it violates its ethical obligations. Any company that violates its ethical obligations should be subject to regulatory oversight. NovaChem knowingly deceived consumers. Therefore, NovaChem should be subject to regulatory oversight.
lr.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a river floods its banks, downstream farmland is damaged. If farmland is damaged, crop yields decline. The Arno River flooded its banks. Therefore, crop yields along the Arno will decline.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Companies that pollute waterways face heavy fines. NovaChem faces heavy fines. Therefore, NovaChem has polluted a waterway.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any business that overcharges customers should be audited. Businesses that are audited often improve their practices. Dalton Co. overcharged customers. Therefore, Dalton Co. will probably improve its practices.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Regulatory oversight is imposed on companies that violate consumer-protection statutes. Companies subject to oversight must file quarterly reports. Therefore, companies that violate consumer-protection statutes must file quarterly reports.

choices.label: E
choices.text: When athletes use banned substances, they violate sporting rules. Violating sporting rules results in disqualification. Therefore, athletes who use banned substances face disqualification.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A → B; B → C; A (particular); ∴ C (particular). Choice A: floods → farmland damaged; farmland damaged → yields decline; Arno flooded (particular); ∴ yields decline (particular). Three-step chain applied to a specific case — exact match.
explanations.A: Correct. Conditional chain with a specific instantiation, mirroring the stimulus precisely.
explanations.B: Trap: affirms the consequent (All polluters → fines; fines; ∴ polluter). Invalid form.
explanations.C: Trap: 'often improve' introduces probability ('probably'), shifting conclusion strength from certainty to likelihood — strength-shift trap.
explanations.D: Trap: correct conditional chain but lacks a particular instantiation; the conclusion is a universal generalization, not a particular case. Same-topic distractor.
explanations.E: Trap: valid conditional chain (A → B; B → C; ∴ A → C) but stays at the universal level — no specific athlete is named. Premise count and conclusion type differ.

lr.difficultyReason: Universal-to-particular (All A are B; x is A; ∴ x is B) stimulus in linguistics domain; distractors use the same universal premise structure but apply it invalidly or shift to probabilistic language.
lr.stimulus: All languages classified as ergative-absolutive assign the same grammatical case to the subjects of intransitive verbs and the objects of transitive verbs. Basque is classified as an ergative-absolutive language. Therefore, Basque assigns the same grammatical case to the subjects of intransitive verbs and the objects of transitive verbs.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every element in the halogen group reacts readily with alkali metals to form salts. Chlorine is an element in the halogen group. Therefore, chlorine reacts readily with alkali metals to form salts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most Romance languages derive the majority of their vocabulary from Latin. Portuguese is a Romance language. Therefore, Portuguese probably derives the majority of its vocabulary from Latin.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Languages with complex morphology are rarely adopted as lingua francas. Swahili has relatively simple morphology. Therefore, Swahili may serve as a lingua franca.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All endangered languages lack government protection. Ubykh lacks government protection. Therefore, Ubykh is an endangered language.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some tonal languages are found in sub-Saharan Africa. Yoruba is a tonal language. Therefore, Yoruba is probably found in sub-Saharan Africa.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: All A are B; x is A; ∴ x is B — a valid universal instantiation. Choice A matches: All halogens react with alkali metals; chlorine is a halogen; ∴ chlorine reacts. Same form, certain conclusion.
explanations.A: Correct. Universal-to-particular instantiation with a certain conclusion.
explanations.B: Trap: strength-shift — uses 'most' (not 'all') in the first premise, so the conclusion is 'probably' rather than certain. Structural mismatch.
explanations.C: Trap: uses a negative universal ('rarely') and draws a permissive conclusion ('may'), neither matching the affirmative universal nor the certain conclusion of the stimulus.
explanations.D: Trap: affirms the consequent — All A → B; x has B; ∴ x is A. Invalid form despite the universal premise.
explanations.E: Trap: 'some' in the first premise and 'probably' in the conclusion — both quantifier and strength differ from the stimulus.

lr.difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism in economic policy domain; distractors include one that affirms a disjunct (invalid) and one that uses a biconditional disguised as a disjunction.
lr.stimulus: The budget shortfall must be addressed either by raising taxes or by cutting public services. The legislature has decided that taxes will not be raised. Therefore, public services will be cut.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The vaccine trial will be conducted either in the spring or in the autumn. Funding constraints have ruled out a spring trial. Therefore, the trial will be conducted in the autumn.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Either the new highway reduces commute times or it increases suburban sprawl. The highway will increase suburban sprawl. Therefore, commute times will not be reduced.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If the central bank cuts interest rates, consumer borrowing will increase. The central bank has cut interest rates. Therefore, consumer borrowing will increase.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Economists agree that growth requires either investment or consumption. Investment has increased this quarter. Therefore, growth will occur this quarter.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The government can reduce the deficit only by raising taxes. Since raising taxes is politically infeasible, the deficit will not be reduced.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A or B; ¬A; ∴ B. Choice A: spring or autumn; ¬spring; ∴ autumn. Identical disjunctive syllogism structure.
explanations.A: Correct. Disjunctive syllogism — exclusive options, one eliminated, the other concluded.
explanations.B: Trap: affirms one disjunct (sprawl increases) and then denies the other, treating the disjunction as exclusive and reasoning backward — invalid form.
explanations.C: Trap: modus ponens (if A then B; A; ∴ B). Valid but structurally different — no disjunction.
explanations.D: Trap: affirms one disjunct (investment) to conclude the overall goal (growth) — does not eliminate a disjunct. Same economic domain is a surface lure.
explanations.E: Trap: uses 'only if' (biconditional or necessary condition), not a disjunction. The form is A only if B; ¬B; ∴ ¬A (modus tollens), not disjunctive syllogism.

lr.difficultyReason: Modus tollens in history domain; distractors include modus ponens with similar historical content and an invalid contrapositive reversal, requiring careful attention to conditional direction.
lr.stimulus: If the Byzantine Empire had maintained control of the Silk Road trade routes, its treasury would have remained solvent. Historical records show that the Byzantine treasury did not remain solvent. Therefore, the Byzantine Empire did not maintain control of the Silk Road trade routes.
lr.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If the printing press had been widely adopted in China during the Song Dynasty, literacy rates would have increased dramatically. Literacy rates did not increase dramatically during the Song Dynasty. Therefore, the printing press was not widely adopted in China during the Song Dynasty.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the Roman aqueducts had been maintained, urban populations would have remained stable. The Roman aqueducts were maintained for several centuries. Therefore, urban populations remained stable during that period.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Had the Mongols continued their westward expansion, Western Europe would have been conquered. Western Europe was not conquered by the Mongols. Therefore, the Mongols did not continue their westward expansion indefinitely.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If the Meiji Restoration had failed, Japan would not have industrialized rapidly. Japan did industrialize rapidly. Therefore, the Meiji Restoration did not fail.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If trade networks had flourished in medieval Europe, cultural exchange would have increased. Trade networks did flourish in medieval Europe during certain periods. Therefore, cultural exchange increased during those periods.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: If A then B; ¬B; ∴ ¬A (modus tollens). Choice A: If printing press adopted then literacy increased; literacy did not increase; ∴ printing press not widely adopted. Exact structural match.
explanations.A: Correct. Modus tollens — denial of consequent yields denial of antecedent.
explanations.B: Trap: modus ponens (if A then B; A; ∴ B). Valid but different form from the stimulus.
explanations.C: Trap: same modus tollens structure — A → B; ¬B; ∴ ¬A — and appears to match. However, the antecedent ('continued indefinitely') is not the same as the original conditional's antecedent, and the conclusion adds the hedge 'indefinitely,' introducing a strength shift. Choice A remains the cleaner match.
explanations.D: Trap: if ¬A then ¬B; B; ∴ A — this is actually valid (contrapositive of ¬A → ¬B is B → A) but the form differs from the stimulus (the antecedent is negated in the conditional). Surface similarity to modus tollens but structurally distinct.
explanations.E: Trap: modus ponens. Same-domain (medieval Europe) content lure.

lr.difficultyReason: Analogy stimulus (X resembles Y in two relevant respects; Y has property R; ∴ X has R) in arts domain; distractors share surface features of the analogy but differ in the number of shared properties cited or reverse the analogical direction.
lr.stimulus: The newly discovered manuscript shares two key features with authenticated works by the composer: its harmonic language and its instrumentation. Since authenticated works by the composer are known to display a recurring modal cadence pattern, the newly discovered manuscript almost certainly displays a recurring modal cadence pattern as well.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: This fossil shares its skeletal proportions and dental structure with the known species Megalodon. Since Megalodon is known to have been apex predator, this fossil almost certainly belonged to an apex predator as well.

choices.label: B
choices.text: This ceramic vessel resembles ancient Greek amphorae. Since ancient Greek amphorae were used to store olive oil, this vessel was probably used to store olive oil.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The newly identified plant specimen has unusual leaf geometry. Other plants with unusual leaf geometry tend to thrive in arid environments. Therefore, this specimen probably thrives in arid environments.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Authenticated works by this sculptor show a preference for marble. Since the newly discovered statue is made of marble, it was almost certainly created by this sculptor.

choices.label: E
choices.text: This symphony shares its key signature and tempo markings with works by Beethoven. Beethoven's works are widely performed today. Therefore, this symphony is widely performed today.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: X shares two specific properties with Y; Y is known to have R; ∴ X almost certainly has R. Choice A: fossil shares two properties (skeletal proportions and dental structure) with Megalodon; Megalodon has R (apex predator); ∴ fossil almost certainly has R. Exact match in analogy structure, property count, and conclusion strength.
explanations.A: Correct. Two shared properties cited, known property of the analog transferred to the subject, 'almost certainly' conclusion strength matches.
explanations.B: Trap: only one shared property (resembles amphorae), not two — premise count mismatch. Also weakens analogy.
explanations.C: Trap: one shared property (leaf geometry) cited; the analog is a category ('other plants'), not a specific named entity. Structure is closer to universal-to-particular than analogy.
explanations.D: Trap: affirms the consequent — Y (authenticated sculptor) has property B (marble); X has B; ∴ X is Y. Inverts the analogical direction.
explanations.E: Trap: two shared properties cited, matching the stimulus premise count, but the transferred property (widely performed) is incidental rather than intrinsic to the shared features — and the conclusion lacks 'almost certainly,' introducing a strength shift.

lr.difficultyReason: Universal-to-particular with a negative universal ('No A is B; x is A; ∴ x is not B') in policy domain; distractors flip the universal to affirmative or use 'some,' requiring attention to quantifier polarity.
lr.stimulus: No policy that relies exclusively on voluntary compliance has ever succeeded in reducing industrial pollution. The proposed carbon-offset scheme relies exclusively on voluntary compliance. Therefore, the proposed carbon-offset scheme will not succeed in reducing industrial pollution.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No antibiotic that targets only gram-positive bacteria is effective against tuberculosis. Streptomycin targets only gram-positive bacteria. Therefore, streptomycin is not effective against tuberculosis.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some regulations that rely on voluntary compliance have failed to reduce emissions. This regulation relies on voluntary compliance. Therefore, this regulation will probably fail to reduce emissions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All renewable-energy mandates require government subsidies. The wind-power initiative requires government subsidies. Therefore, the wind-power initiative is a renewable-energy mandate.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No tax incentive has ever eliminated a harmful industry practice. Corporate tax credits are a form of tax incentive. Therefore, corporate tax credits will not eliminate harmful industry practices.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Voluntary compliance schemes rarely achieve full industry participation. The proposed scheme relies on voluntary compliance. Therefore, the proposed scheme will probably not achieve full industry participation.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: No A is B; x is A; ∴ x is not B — universal negative instantiation. Choice A: No antibiotic that targets only gram-positive bacteria is effective against tuberculosis; streptomycin targets only gram-positive bacteria; ∴ streptomycin is not effective. Perfect structural match.
explanations.A: Correct. Universal negative ('No A is B') applied to a particular instance, yielding a certain negative conclusion.
explanations.B: Trap: strength-shift — 'some' replaces the universal negative, and 'probably' replaces the certain conclusion. Quantifier and conclusion strength both differ.
explanations.C: Trap: affirms the consequent (All A → B; x has B; ∴ x is A). Invalid form despite using a universal premise.
explanations.D: Trap: same-domain (policy/voluntary compliance) content lure. The structure matches at first glance, but the subject of the universal premise ('tax incentive') is broader than the particular instance ('corporate tax credits'), making the instantiation imprecise — this is a subtle premise-count mismatch.
explanations.E: Trap: strength-shift — 'rarely' and 'probably' replace the universal negative and certain conclusion.

lr.difficultyReason: Conditional chain in technology domain (A → B; B → C; ¬C; ∴ ¬A) combining a chain with modus tollens; distractors break the chain or apply modus tollens at the wrong node.
lr.stimulus: If the new operating system is deployed company-wide, all legacy software will need to be upgraded. If all legacy software is upgraded, the IT department's budget will be exceeded. The IT department's budget was not exceeded. Therefore, the new operating system was not deployed company-wide.
lr.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If the dam is constructed upstream, the wetlands downstream will be flooded. If the wetlands are flooded, the migratory bird population will collapse. The migratory bird population did not collapse. Therefore, the dam was not constructed upstream.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the clinical trial succeeds, the drug will receive regulatory approval. If the drug receives regulatory approval, it will be commercially released. The clinical trial succeeded. Therefore, the drug will be commercially released.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If the server farm is expanded, electricity costs will rise. Electricity costs have risen. Therefore, the server farm was expanded.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If the new software is deployed, legacy systems will require upgrades. Legacy systems have not required upgrades. Therefore, the new software was not deployed.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If network bandwidth is increased, data transfer speeds improve. If data transfer speeds improve, user satisfaction rises. Network bandwidth was not increased. Therefore, user satisfaction did not rise.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A → B; B → C; ¬C; ∴ ¬A — a conditional chain with modus tollens applied to the final consequent. Choice A: dam → wetlands flooded; wetlands flooded → bird population collapses; birds did not collapse; ∴ dam not constructed. Exact three-conditional-link structure with modus tollens at the end.
explanations.A: Correct. Conditional chain plus modus tollens on the final consequent — mirrors the stimulus in premise count, chain direction, and conclusion form.
explanations.B: Trap: modus ponens applied to a two-step chain (A → B; B → C; A; ∴ C). Valid but different — the argument runs forward, not backward via modus tollens.
explanations.C: Trap: affirms the consequent (A → B; B; ∴ A). Invalid form, and only one conditional link rather than two.
explanations.D: Trap: valid modus tollens (A → B; ¬B; ∴ ¬A) but only one conditional link — missing the chained intermediate step. Same-topic (software deployment) content lure.
explanations.E: Trap: denies the antecedent (A → B; B → C; ¬A; ∴ ¬C). Invalid form — denial of the antecedent is a formal fallacy.

lr.difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism embedded within a broader argument (three premises total) in the arts/history domain; distractors use the same domain or reduce to a two-premise disjunction without the supplementary premise.
lr.stimulus: The fresco in the chapel was painted either during the early Renaissance or during the High Renaissance. Art historians agree that its technique is inconsistent with the High Renaissance. Moreover, any artwork whose technique is inconsistent with a given period was not created during that period. Therefore, the fresco was painted during the early Renaissance.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The unidentified mineral sample is either feldspar or quartz. Its refractive index is inconsistent with quartz. Any mineral whose refractive index is inconsistent with a given mineral type is not that mineral type. Therefore, the sample is feldspar.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The poem was written either by Keats or by Shelley. Literary scholars believe it was most likely written by Keats. Therefore, the poem was probably written by Keats.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The artifact is either Minoan or Mycenaean in origin. Its decoration is inconsistent with Mycenaean craftsmanship. Therefore, the artifact is Minoan in origin.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The painting was created either before or after the artist's exile. If it was created before the exile, it would display the artist's early palette. The painting does not display the early palette. Therefore, it was created after the exile.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The mural was executed either in fresco or in tempera. Only a master painter could execute a fresco of this scale. This mural was executed by a master painter. Therefore, this mural was executed in fresco.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A or B; technique inconsistent with B; any technique inconsistent with a period means not created in that period (universal rule); ∴ A. Three premises — disjunction, observational premise, universal rule — before the conclusion. Choice A matches exactly: disjunction (feldspar or quartz), observational premise (refractive index inconsistent with quartz), universal rule (inconsistent refractive index ≠ that mineral); ∴ feldspar.
explanations.A: Correct. Three-premise structure — disjunction plus observational premise plus explicit universal rule — yielding disjunctive syllogism conclusion. All three premises match in form and count.
explanations.B: Trap: 'most likely' introduces probability rather than eliminating a disjunct through a rule; conclusion is 'probably,' shifting modal strength. No universal rule premise.
explanations.C: Trap: only two premises (disjunction and observational claim) — the explicit universal rule is missing, reducing premise count. Surface similarity to the stimulus is high, making this an effective distractor.
explanations.D: Trap: three premises, but the structure is a conditional chain with modus tollens (A → B; ¬B; ∴ ¬A) rather than a disjunctive syllogism with an embedded universal rule.
explanations.E: Trap: affirms one disjunct by establishing a necessary condition and then affirming it — structurally invalid (affirming the consequent within the disjunction resolution). 'Only a master painter could' means master → fresco, not fresco → master.

lr.difficultyReason: The stimulus uses a disjunctive syllogism (A or B; not A; therefore B). Distractors share topical surface features or use valid but structurally different forms (e.g., modus ponens, contrapositive). Students must formalize the argument to avoid being misled by subject-matter overlap.
lr.stimulus: Either the medication caused the patient's rash or the rash resulted from an allergic reaction to a food. The patient has not eaten any allergenic foods in the past week. Therefore, the medication caused the rash.
lr.questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Either the defendant committed the fraud alone or had an accomplice. Investigators found no evidence of an accomplice. Therefore, the defendant committed the fraud alone.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the bridge collapses, either faulty materials or poor design is to blame. The design was certified as sound. Therefore, faulty materials caused the collapse.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The patient's rash is severe. All severe rashes require immediate treatment. Therefore, the patient's rash requires immediate treatment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If the medication is discontinued, the rash will clear up. The rash has not cleared up. Therefore, the medication has not been discontinued.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The patient could have developed the rash from either medication or stress. Both the medication and a stressful event occurred last week. Therefore, it is unclear which caused the rash.

explanations.correct: Both the stimulus and choice A follow disjunctive syllogism: A or B; not B; therefore A. The stimulus eliminates food allergy and concludes medication; choice A eliminates the accomplice and concludes the defendant acted alone. Structure matches perfectly.
explanations.A: Correct. Disjunctive syllogism: (fraud alone) or (had accomplice); no accomplice; therefore fraud alone. Identical logical form to the stimulus.
explanations.B: Same topic area (causes and elimination) but adds a conditional premise ('If the bridge collapses…'), making it a conditional chain with elimination rather than a pure disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.C: This is a universal-to-particular inference (All severe rashes → treatment; this rash is severe; therefore treatment). Different logical form from the stimulus's disjunctive syllogism.
explanations.D: This is modus tollens: If medication discontinued → rash clears; rash has not cleared; therefore medication not discontinued. Different logical form, even though the subject matter resembles the stimulus.
explanations.E: The argument does not eliminate either disjunct and instead withholds a conclusion. This is not a disjunctive syllogism and does not parallel the stimulus.

lr.difficultyReason: The stimulus is a conditional chain (A → B; B → C; A; therefore C). Distractors include a contrapositive, a topic-matching invalid form, and a universal-to-particular instantiation. Students who only recognize the conclusion may select the topic-similar wrong answer.
lr.stimulus: Whenever a government imposes price controls, shortages eventually develop. Whenever shortages develop, black markets emerge. The current government has imposed price controls. Therefore, black markets will eventually emerge.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a forest fire goes uncontrolled, it depletes soil nutrients. Depleted soil nutrients prevent forest regrowth. A fire in the northern district is uncontrolled. Therefore, forest regrowth in the northern district will be prevented.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Price controls distort market signals. Distorted market signals are undesirable. Therefore, price controls should be abolished.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whenever inflation rises, central banks raise interest rates. Interest rates have not been raised. Therefore, inflation has not risen.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All economies that impose price controls eventually transition to free markets. Country X has imposed price controls. Therefore, Country X will eventually transition to a free market.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some governments that impose price controls succeed in stabilizing prices. This government has imposed price controls. Therefore, this government may succeed in stabilizing prices.

explanations.correct: Both the stimulus and choice A employ a conditional chain (A → B; B → C; A is true; therefore C). Stimulus: price controls → shortages → black markets; controls imposed; therefore black markets emerge. Choice A: fire uncontrolled → soil depleted → regrowth prevented; fire is uncontrolled; therefore regrowth prevented.
explanations.A: Correct. Three-step conditional chain with affirmation of the antecedent. Matches the stimulus's structure exactly.
explanations.B: Only two premises, no instantiated case. The conclusion ('should be abolished') introduces a normative element absent from the stimulus. Different form.
explanations.C: This is modus tollens applied to a conditional (if inflation rises → rates rise; rates not raised; therefore inflation not risen). The stimulus affirms the antecedent; this denies the consequent.
explanations.D: This is a universal-to-particular instantiation (All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B) with only two inferential steps, not a three-link chain. Missing the middle conditional step.
explanations.E: Uses 'some' rather than 'whenever/all,' weakening the premise. The conclusion ('may succeed') is weaker than the stimulus's definite conclusion. Strength mismatch.

lr.difficultyReason: The stimulus uses modus tollens (A → B; not B; therefore not A). Distractors include a disjunctive syllogism with the same subject domain, a modus ponens, and a same-topic invalid argument. Students who recognize 'if–then' structure but not direction of inference may pick the modus ponens trap.
lr.stimulus: If the archaeological site is more than 3,000 years old, the pottery fragments found there will exhibit a particular type of oxidation pattern. The pottery fragments do not exhibit that oxidation pattern. Therefore, the site is not more than 3,000 years old.
lr.questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a star is in the main sequence, its core temperature exceeds ten million degrees. This star's core temperature does not exceed ten million degrees. Therefore, this star is not in the main sequence.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the pottery fragments are ancient, they are fragile. These pottery fragments are ancient. Therefore, these pottery fragments are fragile.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Either the site is Bronze Age or it is Iron Age. The site is not Iron Age. Therefore, the site is Bronze Age.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most ancient sites contain pottery. This site contains pottery. Therefore, this site is probably ancient.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If the site lacks an oxidation pattern, it is less than 3,000 years old. The site lacks the oxidation pattern. Therefore, the site is less than 3,000 years old.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is modus tollens: If P → Q; not Q; therefore not P. Choice A matches exactly: if main sequence → core temp > 10M; core temp not > 10M; therefore not main sequence.
explanations.A: Correct. Modus tollens with identical two-premise structure and denial of the consequent leading to denial of the antecedent.
explanations.B: This is modus ponens (If P → Q; P; therefore Q), the opposite inferential direction from the stimulus. Surface similarity to the stimulus's subject matter is a trap.
explanations.C: Disjunctive syllogism (A or B; not B; therefore A). Valid, but a different logical form from the stimulus's modus tollens.
explanations.D: Reversed base-rate reasoning ('most A have B; x has B; therefore x is probably A'). This is a flawed argument and does not match the valid modus tollens of the stimulus.
explanations.E: Though it reaches a similar conclusion, this is modus ponens (If lacks pattern → < 3,000 years; lacks pattern; therefore < 3,000 years). The conditional is constructed differently — the absence of the pattern is directly stated as the antecedent, not derived.

lr.difficultyReason: The stimulus uses universal instantiation (All A are B; x is A; therefore x is B). One distractor uses 'most' instead of 'all,' creating a strength-shift trap. Another uses the same subject but reverses the universal claim. Students must track quantifier strength carefully.
lr.stimulus: All legislative bills that pass without a supermajority are subject to gubernatorial veto. The education reform bill passed without a supermajority. Therefore, the education reform bill is subject to gubernatorial veto.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every chemical compound that contains chlorine is potentially hazardous to marine life. This new industrial solvent contains chlorine. Therefore, this solvent is potentially hazardous to marine life.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most bills that bypass committee review are subject to floor amendments. This bill bypassed committee review. Therefore, this bill is probably subject to floor amendments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The education reform bill was hastily drafted. Hastily drafted bills often contain errors. Therefore, the education reform bill likely contains errors.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If a bill is vetoed, the legislature can override the veto with a two-thirds majority. The legislature does not have a two-thirds majority. Therefore, any vetoed bill will stand.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No bill lacking bipartisan support has ever been enacted without controversy. This bill lacks bipartisan support. Therefore, if enacted, this bill will be controversial.

explanations.correct: Both the stimulus and choice A use universal instantiation: All/every A are B; x is A; therefore x is B. The universal claim is categorical ('all'/'every'), the particular is identified, and the conclusion is certain. Structure matches perfectly.
explanations.A: Correct. Every chlorine-containing compound is hazardous; this solvent contains chlorine; therefore it is hazardous. Same universal-to-particular form with matching conclusion strength.
explanations.B: Uses 'most' instead of 'all,' weakening the universal premise, and 'probably' in the conclusion. Strength-shift trap — the conclusion's certainty does not match the stimulus.
explanations.C: Uses 'often' (not 'all'), and 'likely' in the conclusion. Same strength-shift trap as B. Also matches topic (legislative bills) to lure students away from structural analysis.
explanations.D: This is modus tollens (if veto → can override; cannot override; therefore veto stands). Different logical form, though it uses legislative vocabulary.
explanations.E: Contains a conditional conclusion ('if enacted, will be controversial'), which is not a simple categorical conclusion. The stimulus concludes categorically, not conditionally.

lr.difficultyReason: The stimulus uses a contrapositive derivation embedded in an argument: a conditional plus its contrapositive application. Distractors use modus ponens with the same antecedent-consequent vocabulary, which tempts students who misread the direction of the inference.
