choices.text: Repeat offenders who completed the safety course reported that it increased their awareness of traffic hazards.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the five years before the law was enacted, traffic violations had remained relatively stable.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Many cities have enacted similar mandatory safety course requirements.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The traffic safety course covers a wide range of driving scenarios.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some people who violate traffic laws do not repeat their offenses.

explanations.correct: By establishing that violations had been stable before the law, this rules out the alternative that some other external factor (better roads, improved vehicles, fewer drivers) caused the decline. This strengthens the causal claim.
explanations.A: Suggests a mechanism but doesn't rule out alternatives or establish the law specifically caused the decline.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Whether other cities have similar laws doesn't establish this law caused this city's decline.
explanations.D: Describes the course but doesn't connect it to causation of the decline.
explanations.E: About general patterns of re-offense, not about the specific law's effect.

lr.difficultyReason: Straightforward technological causal claim where the alternative is that the result predates the intervention. Correct answer establishes timing to rule out pre-existing conditions.
lr.stimulus: The software company implemented a new code-review process to reduce bugs in its applications. The number of reported bugs decreased by 35 percent in the three months after implementation. Therefore, the new code-review process caused the reduction.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new code-review process requires developers to document their changes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the twelve months before the new process was implemented, the number of reported bugs had been increasing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some applications are more prone to bugs than others.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Code-review processes are industry best practices.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The company's customers reported increased satisfaction with product reliability.

explanations.correct: By showing an upward trend in bugs before the process was implemented, this rules out the alternative that the bug reduction was part of a pre-existing trend. This strengthens the causal link to the new process.
explanations.A: Describes the process but doesn't establish it caused the reduction.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: General variation in bug-proneness doesn't address whether this process caused this reduction.
explanations.D: Industry practice doesn't establish causation for this specific company's results.
explanations.E: Customer satisfaction follows from fewer bugs but doesn't establish the process caused the reduction.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple causal claim in a linguistic/communication context. Correct answer rules out that the improvement was caused by something other than the grammar intervention.
lr.stimulus: A writing instructor introduced daily grammar instruction in her composition class. After six weeks, students' written essays showed significantly fewer grammatical errors. Thus, the grammar instruction caused the improvement in essay quality.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students in the class had completed fewer writing assignments before the grammar instruction began.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Writing proficiency is determined by many factors beyond grammatical accuracy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Before the grammar instruction began, students' essays showed no significant change in grammatical error rates across successive assignments.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The instructor provided feedback on grammar in addition to daily instruction.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some students in the class had prior instruction in grammar.

explanations.correct: By establishing that error rates were stable before instruction began, this rules out the alternative that students were improving on their own or that the improvement reflects natural maturation. This strengthens the causal claim.
explanations.A: Fewer assignments might weaken the argument by suggesting limited practice before instruction.
explanations.B: While true, this acknowledges multiple factors but doesn't establish the grammar instruction caused the improvement.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Feedback might be an alternative mechanism or confounding factor.
explanations.E: Prior experience doesn't address whether the current instruction caused the improvement.

lr.difficultyReason: Causal argument about health intervention with one obvious alternative: the condition improving on its own. Correct answer rules this out.
lr.stimulus: A clinic began administering a new treatment for a chronic skin condition. Patients receiving the treatment showed improvement in 80 percent of cases within four weeks. Therefore, the new treatment is responsible for the improvement.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new treatment was developed after years of clinical research.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patients with the chronic skin condition who did not receive the new treatment showed no improvement in the same four-week period.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The skin condition affects thousands of people worldwide.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some patients experienced minor side effects from the treatment.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Topical treatments are more commonly used than oral treatments for skin conditions.

explanations.correct: By establishing a control comparison where untreated patients showed no improvement, this rules out the alternative that the condition improves naturally over time. This directly strengthens the causal claim.
explanations.A: Research effort doesn't establish efficacy in practice.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Prevalence is irrelevant to whether the treatment caused the improvement.
explanations.D: Side effects might relate to safety but don't establish causation of improvement.
explanations.E: Treatment preferences don't address whether this particular treatment caused the improvement.

lr.difficultyReason: Predictive/causal claim in historical context. Correct answer confirms the mechanism by which the policy is presumed to work, strengthening the argument.
lr.stimulus: A museum installed improved climate-control systems in its rare manuscript collection room. Since the installation, the rate of deterioration of the manuscripts has slowed significantly. Therefore, the climate-control system is responsible for the slowdown.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The previous climate-control system was over fifty years old.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Temperature and humidity fluctuations are a primary cause of manuscript deterioration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Many museums have upgraded their climate-control systems in recent years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some of the manuscripts in the collection are from the eighteenth century.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The museum has also improved its security systems.

explanations.correct: By establishing that temperature and humidity fluctuations cause deterioration, this confirms the mechanism by which the new climate control would reduce deterioration. This strengthens the causal claim.
explanations.A: The age of the old system is irrelevant to whether the new system caused the improvement.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Whether other museums upgraded doesn't establish causation for this museum.
explanations.D: Age of manuscripts doesn't explain the slowdown in deterioration.
explanations.E: Security improvements address a different preservation concern.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal inference where the alternative explanation is explicit and ruled out by the correct answer. The argument assumes that absence of evidence is evidence of absence.
lr.stimulus: The office break room has been unusually quiet this week. The most likely explanation is that several members of the morning coffee group have taken vacation time. However, it could also be that the office cooling system broke down, causing employees to stay at their desks rather than linger in the break room.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument that the quiet break room is due to vacation time rather than a broken cooling system?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The office cooling system is regularly inspected and maintained by a professional contractor.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The office break room temperature has been normal all week.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vacation time is most commonly taken during the summer months.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The morning coffee group typically consists of five employees.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Employees have not reported any complaints about the break room this week.

explanations.correct: By confirming that the cooling system was working normally, this rules out the alternative explanation for the quiet break room. The argument asserts that vacation time is the most likely cause; showing that the competing cause (broken cooling system) did not occur strengthens the conclusion.
explanations.A: While maintenance history is mentioned, this does not confirm the system was working this particular week, so it does not rule out the break-down alternative.
explanations.B: Correct. This directly eliminates the competing cause.
explanations.C: This is about general vacation patterns and does not address whether these specific employees took time off this week.
explanations.D: Accurate but irrelevant to whether they were actually absent this week.
explanations.E: The absence of complaints is consistent with either explanation and does not strengthen the case for vacation time over a cooling problem.

lr.difficultyReason: Straightforward medical/health causal claim. The correct answer confirms a load-bearing premise: that the mechanism actually produces the claimed effect.
lr.stimulus: Dr. Patel observed that patients who take daily walks show improved blood pressure readings after eight weeks. She concludes that regular walking reduces high blood pressure. The effect is likely due to increased cardiovascular fitness that comes from regular aerobic exercise.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens Dr. Patel's reasoning?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eight weeks is a sufficient period to observe measurable improvements in cardiovascular fitness from daily walking.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some patients with high blood pressure do not benefit from medication.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Blood pressure readings can fluctuate due to stress and diet.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Walking is less strenuous than running as a form of aerobic exercise.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Patients who walk daily report feeling more relaxed.

explanations.correct: Dr. Patel's argument rests on the assumption that eight weeks is long enough for walking to produce cardiovascular improvements that then lower blood pressure. Confirming this timeline strengthens her causal chain from walking to fitness to lower blood pressure.
explanations.A: Correct. This validates the temporal component of her proposed mechanism.
explanations.B: Medication is not mentioned in her argument, so this is irrelevant.
explanations.C: While true, this introduces alternative factors but does not strengthen her walk-causation claim.
explanations.D: Walking being less intense than running does not support the claim that walking itself reduces blood pressure.
explanations.E: Feeling relaxed is a side effect, not the same as confirming the cardiovascular mechanism she proposes.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple economic causal argument. The alternative explanation (supply reduction, not demand) is explicit; ruling it out strengthens the demand-side conclusion.
lr.stimulus: The price of coffee has risen by 30% over the past year. This increase is likely due to increased global demand for coffee as emerging markets consume more. A competing theory suggests that the price rise is caused by poor harvests reducing supply.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to support the argument that increased demand is driving the coffee price rise?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coffee yields in major producing countries were normal or above normal this year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The global coffee market is heavily influenced by commodity speculators.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Emerging market populations are growing faster than developed market populations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tea prices have also risen over the past year.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Coffee is an essential commodity in many developed countries.

explanations.correct: By showing that harvests were normal or above normal, this eliminates the supply-shortage alternative explanation. If supply was not constrained, then demand-side factors become the more plausible driver of price increases.
explanations.A: Correct. This rules out the competing supply-reduction theory.
explanations.B: Speculation might affect price but doesn't address whether demand or supply is the primary driver.
explanations.C: While relevant to emerging markets generally, this does not directly confirm increased coffee demand or rule out the supply explanation.
explanations.D: Tea price changes are independent of coffee and do not strengthen the demand argument.
explanations.E: Essential status doesn't explain why price rose this particular year or rule out supply constraints.

lr.difficultyReason: Straightforward policy argument with a single observable alternative. Correct answer confirms that the policy mechanism works as intended.
lr.stimulus: The state is considering raising the speed limit on rural highways from 55 to 65 mph. Traffic safety officials predict this will increase accident rates because drivers will spend less time in careful attention. However, the change might instead improve safety if it reduces the gap between posted limits and actual driving speeds.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the officials' prediction that raising the speed limit will increase accidents?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rural highways have fewer pedestrians than urban streets.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most drivers on rural highways are currently driving at speeds below 65 mph.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Accident rates correlate strongly with driver inattention rather than with the gap between posted and actual speeds.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Speed limit signs on rural highways are clearly visible and well-maintained.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rural highways carry less traffic than interstate highways.

explanations.correct: The officials argue that higher speeds cause reduced attention and thus more accidents. Confirming that inattention (not gap-reduction) is the dominant causal factor in accidents strengthens their prediction that raising limits will increase accidents.
explanations.A: Pedestrian presence is not relevant to the speed-limit argument.
explanations.B: If drivers are already below 65, then raising the limit may not change actual speeds, which would weaken rather than strengthen the officials' prediction.
explanations.C: Correct. This confirms the mechanism by which speed increases lead to accidents.
explanations.D: Sign visibility doesn't address whether higher speeds cause more accidents.
explanations.E: Traffic volume is independent of the speed-safety relationship.

lr.difficultyReason: Single-link causal argument in environmental science. The correct answer rules out a competing cause of the observed phenomenon.
lr.stimulus: Biologists studying a forest noticed that the population of native songbirds has declined significantly over the past five years. They attribute this decline to invasive bird species that compete for nesting sites. An alternative explanation is that pesticide use in nearby agricultural areas has poisoned the songbirds' insect food sources.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the biologists' conclusion about the cause of the songbird decline?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pesticide use in the agricultural areas near the forest has remained constant over the past decade.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Invasive bird species have historically been unsuccessful at establishing populations in temperate forests.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Native songbirds have adaptations that allow them to use alternative nesting sites.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insect populations in the forest have remained stable over the past five years.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Native songbirds are an important part of the forest ecosystem.

explanations.correct: By confirming that insect populations—the songbirds' primary food source—have remained stable, this rules out the pesticide-poisoning alternative explanation. If food availability was unchanged, the decline must be due to another cause, namely competition from invasive species.
explanations.A: Constant pesticide use over a decade does not rule out whether it affected songbirds specifically in the past five years.
explanations.B: Historical failure does not explain why invasive species are suddenly present now.
explanations.C: Adaptability would not explain a sharp population decline.
explanations.D: Correct. This eliminates the food-source alternative.
explanations.E: Ecological importance is irrelevant to what caused the observed decline.

lr.difficultyReason: Straightforward legal/ethics argument with a single obvious alternative cause. Correct answer rules it out by confirming an assumption.
lr.stimulus: The defendant's fingerprints were found at the crime scene. The prosecutor argues this proves the defendant was present at the time of the crime. However, the defense attorney suggests that the fingerprints were planted by police during their investigation.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the prosecutor's argument that the defendant's presence is established by the fingerprints?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The defendant had a motive to commit the crime.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Police chain-of-custody procedures for evidence at the crime scene were strictly followed and documented.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The defendant had previously visited the location where the crime occurred.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fingerprints can be obtained from many surfaces at a crime scene.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The defendant could not provide an alibi for the time of the crime.

explanations.correct: The defense suggests the fingerprints were planted. By confirming that chain-of-custody procedures were strictly followed, this rules out the planting explanation and strengthens the conclusion that the defendant's presence is evidenced by the fingerprints.
explanations.A: Motive supports guilt but not the specific claim that fingerprints prove presence.
explanations.B: Correct. This eliminates the planting alternative.
explanations.C: Prior visits are irrelevant to when these fingerprints were left.
explanations.D: Surface availability does not speak to whether these particular prints are genuine.
explanations.E: Lack of alibi supports guilt generally but doesn't address fingerprint authenticity.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple linguistic/cognitive argument about learning. The correct answer confirms a key premise of the causal mechanism.
lr.stimulus: Children who are read to frequently develop larger vocabularies than children who are rarely read to. This is probably because reading exposes children to a wider variety of words than everyday conversation does.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most supports the argument about the cause of vocabulary differences?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Parents who read to their children tend to have larger vocabularies themselves.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Books contain a greater diversity of word types and usage than occurs in typical spoken conversation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Children who develop large vocabularies early tend to perform better academically.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some children who are not read to still develop large vocabularies.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reading ability and vocabulary size are correlated in adults.

explanations.correct: The argument proposes that reading causes larger vocabularies because books contain more diverse words than conversation. Confirming this premise—that books do indeed contain greater word diversity—strengthens the proposed mechanism.
explanations.A: Parents' own vocabularies might be a confound, not a confirmation of the reading mechanism.
explanations.B: Correct. This validates the key premise that books provide more word exposure.
explanations.C: Academic outcomes are irrelevant to why reading builds vocabulary.
explanations.D: Exceptions do not undermine a general causal claim.
explanations.E: Adult reading and vocabulary are outside the scope of the child-reading argument.

lr.difficultyReason: Historical causal argument. The correct answer rules out a specific alternative explanation for an observed outcome.
lr.stimulus: The Roman Empire's military declined in the fourth century. Historians argue that economic strain from defending vast borders drained resources needed for military maintenance and innovation. Others suggest the decline was simply due to the leadership of weak emperors.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the economic explanation for the military decline?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Several emperors in the fourth century were competent military strategists.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tax revenues decreased significantly during the same period that military strength declined.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Weak leadership had occurred in earlier centuries without causing permanent military decline.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Empire's borders were roughly the same in the fourth century as they had been in previous centuries.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neighboring barbarian tribes possessed superior weaponry compared to Roman forces.

explanations.correct: By showing that weak leadership alone did not cause permanent decline in the past, this weakens the 'weak emperors' alternative and strengthens the case that economic factors were the distinguishing cause in the fourth century.
explanations.A: Competent emperors would support the leadership explanation, not weaken it.
explanations.B: While this shows a correlation, declining revenues themselves do not rule out leadership as the culprit.
explanations.C: Correct. This shows weak leadership is insufficient to cause permanent decline, supporting the economic explanation as the special factor in the fourth century.
explanations.D: Border stability would suggest defense costs stayed constant, which doesn't clarify causation.
explanations.E: Barbarian superiority would explain external military pressure but not the internal economic strain argument.

lr.difficultyReason: Technology adoption argument with a single clear alternative. The correct answer confirms the causal mechanism.
lr.stimulus: Sales of e-readers have increased dramatically in the past decade. Publishers believe this trend is driven by consumers' preference for the convenience of digital reading. However, critics argue the growth is instead due to aggressive marketing and price cuts by electronics retailers.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the publishers' argument about consumer preference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: E-reader prices have remained relatively stable over the past five years.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Survey data shows that consumers cite convenience as the primary reason for choosing e-readers over print books.

choices.label: C
choices.text: E-reader battery life has improved significantly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Advertising budgets for e-readers have increased substantially in recent years.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Print book sales have remained stable rather than declining sharply.

explanations.correct: The publishers claim that consumer preference for convenience drives sales. Direct evidence that consumers identify convenience as their primary purchase motivation strongly supports this causal claim.
explanations.A: Stable prices would actually undermine the marketing/price-cut alternative, but this is weaker than direct preference evidence.
explanations.B: Correct. This directly confirms that convenience preference is the stated reason for the purchase decision.
explanations.C: Battery improvements support that e-readers are convenient but don't rule out marketing as the driver.
explanations.D: Increased advertising strengthens the critics' marketing explanation, not the publishers'.
explanations.E: Stable print sales tell us nothing about why e-readers grew in preference.

lr.difficultyReason: Arts/education causal argument with one obvious alternative. Correct answer rules out the competing explanation.
lr.stimulus: An arts academy reports that students who participate in music training show higher academic achievement in math and science. The academy suggests that music training develops cognitive skills transferable to these subjects. A rival explanation is that only academically strong students choose to take music lessons.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most supports the academy's causal claim about music training?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students at the academy come from diverse socioeconomic backgrounds.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Music training was randomly assigned to some students while others received standard curriculum, and the trained group showed greater math and science gains.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Students who do well in music often do well in other subjects.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Music teachers at the academy hold advanced degrees in music.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The academy has been in operation for over twenty years.

explanations.correct: By showing that music training was randomly assigned—not chosen by pre-existing high-achievers—and that this group showed greater gains, this eliminates the selection-bias alternative. Random assignment proves the correlation is causal rather than due to self-selection.
explanations.A: Socioeconomic diversity is irrelevant to whether music causes academic gains.
explanations.B: Correct. Random assignment and subsequent gains rule out the self-selection alternative.
explanations.C: This correlation still allows for selection bias: strong students choose music and do well in other subjects.
explanations.D: Teacher qualifications don't address whether training causes the observed gains.
explanations.E: Institutional longevity is irrelevant to the causal mechanism.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal inference with one visible alternative explanation. Correct answer rules out the alternative — that seasonal weather caused the crop yield increase — by confirming the fertilizer was responsible.
lr.stimulus: A new fertilizer was introduced in Plainville last year, and crop yields increased by 25 percent that season. Farmers are attributing the improved yields to the fertilizer.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument that the fertilizer caused the yield increase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Farmers in neighboring towns who did not use the new fertilizer experienced no significant increase in crop yields last year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The new fertilizer is less expensive than other fertilizers currently on the market.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Weather conditions in Plainville last year were typical for the region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Crop yields in Plainville have been declining steadily for the past decade.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The new fertilizer has been tested on vegetables as well as grains.

explanations.correct: If neighboring farmers without the new fertilizer saw no yield increase, this rules out a shared alternative explanation (regional weather or market factors) and strengthens the causal claim that the fertilizer itself was responsible for Plainville's improvement.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Irrelevant — cost does not address the causal claim.
explanations.C: Irrelevant — typical weather would not explain a 25% increase, so this does not strengthen the fertilizer hypothesis.
explanations.D: Does not address last year's causal question; also potentially weakens by suggesting other factors may be at play.
explanations.E: Irrelevant — the fact that fertilizer works on vegetables does not address the causal question for grains in Plainville.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal inference: increased reading comprehension scores at the school with the new program imply the program caused the gains. One obvious alternative: students' prior ability improved independently. Correct answer rules out the alternative.
lr.stimulus: Lincoln High School implemented a new reading intervention program this year. Students' reading comprehension scores increased by an average of 15 percent compared to last year. The school administrator concludes that the program was responsible for the improvement.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the administrator's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The reading comprehension scores of students at other schools in the district remained essentially unchanged this year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The new reading program was adapted from a program that had been successful at a different school.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some students at Lincoln High School did not fully participate in the reading program.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reading comprehension is more important to academic success than other language skills.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Teachers at Lincoln High School were given additional professional development in reading instruction.

explanations.correct: If reading comprehension scores at other schools remained unchanged, this rules out the alternative that district-wide or regional factors caused the improvement at Lincoln, strengthening the claim that the program itself was responsible.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Accurate but irrelevant — the program's pedigree does not prove it caused this year's gains at Lincoln.
explanations.C: Weakens rather than strengthens — incomplete participation would reduce the program's effect.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — the importance of reading comprehension does not address causation.
explanations.E: Introduces a confounding variable; the professional development (not the program itself) might have caused the improvement, thus weakening rather than strengthening.

lr.difficultyReason: Causal claim: price increase caused a drop in coffee sales. Alternative explanation: consumer preference shifted. Correct answer rules out the alternative by confirming consumers still want coffee.
lr.stimulus: A coffee shop raised the price of its coffee by 20 percent last month, and sales volume dropped by 30 percent. The owner concludes that the price increase caused the decline in sales.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the owner's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A new competing coffee shop opened nearby just before the price increase.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Other coffee shops in the area did not raise their prices last month.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The average customer at the shop purchases coffee five days a week.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The quality of the coffee remained the same after the price increase.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Coffee sales in the city overall increased slightly last month.

explanations.correct: If competing shops did not raise prices, their prices are now relatively lower. Customers switching to competitors due to relative price is consistent with price sensitivity — it directly supports the price-caused-the-decline claim.
explanations.A: Introduces a confounding variable — competition might have caused the sales drop, not the price increase.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Irrelevant — purchase frequency does not explain why customers stopped buying at a higher price.
explanations.D: Rules out quality decline as an alternative, which is helpful; but B is stronger because it shows customers had lower-priced alternatives.
explanations.E: Contradicts the owner's claim — if city sales rose but this shop's fell, something other than market demand (like price) was the cause, but this fact alone doesn't strengthen the owner's specific conclusion relative to alternatives.

lr.difficultyReason: Causal inference: a new medication caused a reduction in headache symptoms. Alternative: placebo effect or regression to the mean. Correct answer rules out placebo by confirming blind trial or mechanism.
lr.stimulus: In a clinical trial, patients who took a new migraine medication reported a 40 percent reduction in headache frequency over three months. Researchers conclude that the medication directly caused this improvement.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the researchers' conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Patients in a control group who received a placebo reported no significant reduction in headache frequency.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The new migraine medication is easier to take than existing migraine treatments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some patients discontinued use of the medication due to minor side effects.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Migraines are a common condition affecting millions of people worldwide.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Previous studies have shown that stress reduction can lower migraine frequency.

explanations.correct: A placebo-controlled comparison directly addresses the alternative explanation of placebo effect. If the control group showed no improvement while the treatment group did, this strengthens the causal claim that the medication (not just patient expectation) caused the improvement.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Accurate but irrelevant — ease of use does not prove efficacy or causation.
explanations.C: Weakens rather than strengthens — dropout due to side effects complicates the causal narrative.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — prevalence of migraines does not address causation in this trial.
explanations.E: Introduces an alternative explanation: stress reduction (not the medication) might have caused the improvement, thus weakening the claim.

lr.difficultyReason: Predictive causal claim: new environmental regulation will reduce pollution. Alternative: regulation won't be enforced or industry will adapt. Correct answer confirms either enforcement or effectiveness.
lr.stimulus: City officials have enacted strict new emissions limits on industrial manufacturing facilities. Environmental advocates predict that these regulations will lead to a measurable reduction in air pollution levels within two years.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the environmental advocates' prediction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The city has hired additional inspectors to monitor compliance with the new emissions limits.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some manufacturing facilities in the city may relocate to other states.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Current pollution levels in the city exceed federal air quality standards.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Citizens have expressed strong support for environmental regulations.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Industrial emissions account for only a portion of the city's total air pollution.

explanations.correct: Additional inspectors strengthen the claim by addressing a key unstated assumption: that regulations will be actively enforced. Enforcement capability directly supports the prediction that the regulations will produce the expected improvement.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Weakens — if facilities relocate, compliance may be easier (no actual pollution reduction) or the economic base is harmed; either way, uncertainty about effectiveness.
explanations.C: Relevant background but does not strengthen the prediction; we already know pollution is a problem.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — public support does not ensure the regulations will reduce pollution.
explanations.E: Weakens — if industrial emissions are only part of the problem, regulations on industry alone may not achieve measurable overall reduction.

lr.difficultyReason: Causal claim: a technology caused a change in user behavior. Alternative: users already wanted this behavior change. Correct answer rules out the alternative.
lr.stimulus: Since the introduction of mobile payment applications, cash transactions have declined sharply in urban areas. Mobile payment providers attribute this trend to the convenience of their technology.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the mobile payment providers' claim?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In rural areas without widespread access to mobile payment technology, cash transactions have remained stable.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some consumers prefer the security features of mobile payment systems.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mobile payment applications offer rewards and incentives to users.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Banks have also reduced the number of automated teller machines in urban areas.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mobile payment technology was developed by several competing companies.

explanations.correct: Geographic comparison: rural areas without the technology show stable cash use, while urban areas with it show sharp decline. This rules out the alternative that consumer preferences shifted across the board, and supports the claim that the technology itself drove the change.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Accurate but does not address causation; security preference could have existed before the technology.
explanations.C: Accurate but does not address causation; incentives are a feature, not proof that convenience (not incentives) drove the change.
explanations.D: Introduces a confounding variable — ATM reduction might have caused the cash decline.
explanations.E: Irrelevant — the number of competing companies does not address the causal mechanism.

lr.difficultyReason: Causal inference: early language exposure caused higher proficiency. Alternative: genetics or family background. Correct answer rules out the alternative.
lr.stimulus: Children who began learning a second language before age five demonstrate higher proficiency in that language by age ten compared to children who started learning it at age seven. Linguists attribute this difference to the cognitive advantages of early language exposure.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the linguists' explanation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Children from bilingual families who began learning their second language after age seven eventually achieve the same proficiency as children who started earlier.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The second language was taught using the same curriculum and methods to both age groups.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Children who learn a second language early also tend to have larger overall vocabularies.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Language proficiency is important for academic success in bilingual schools.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some children who started learning a second language before age five did not achieve high proficiency.

explanations.correct: By confirming that both groups received identical instruction, this rules out the alternative that differences in teaching quality or method caused the proficiency gap, and strengthens the claim that early exposure itself (a cognitive advantage) was the causal factor.
explanations.A: Contradicts the empirical observation and thus weakens the argument.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Consistent with the early-exposure hypothesis but does not rule out confounding variables (e.g., family background).
explanations.D: Irrelevant — importance of proficiency does not address causation.
explanations.E: Weakens — exceptions suggest early exposure alone is not sufficient, casting doubt on the causal claim.

lr.difficultyReason: Causal claim: a policy change caused an outcome. Alternative: some other factor was responsible. Correct answer rules out the alternative.
lr.stimulus: After implementing mandatory ethics training for all employees, a corporation reported a 35 percent decrease in workplace misconduct complaints. Management credits the ethics training with this improvement.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens management's claim?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Comparable corporations that did not implement ethics training continued to receive similar levels of misconduct complaints.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The ethics training program has been accredited by a professional organization.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Employees who completed the ethics training reported feeling more confident in their roles.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Workplace misconduct includes violations of both company policy and legal standards.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some employees did not attend all sessions of the mandatory ethics training.

explanations.correct: If comparable corporations without the training saw no decrease, this rules out the alternative that industry-wide or economic factors reduced complaints, and strengthens the claim that the training program itself was responsible.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Relevant to program quality but does not prove it caused the complaint reduction.
explanations.C: Accurate but does not address misconduct reduction; employee confidence does not necessarily translate to lower complaints.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — the scope of misconduct definition does not address causation.
explanations.E: Weakens — incomplete participation would reduce the training's effect.

lr.difficultyReason: Analogical strength claim: an artwork's popularity indicates its artistic merit. Alternative: popularity reflects marketing, not merit. Correct answer confirms the link.
lr.stimulus: Art critics have long debated whether popular works of art possess genuine artistic merit. A recent exhibition of classical paintings that are widely appreciated by the public has received praise from professional art critics as well. This suggests that popularity and artistic merit often align.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens this conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The exhibition received significant promotional marketing and media attention.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Many unpopular paintings in museums have also been praised by professional art critics.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Professional art critics have varying opinions about what constitutes artistic merit.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The classical paintings in the exhibition are valued highly by collectors worldwide.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The general public and professional critics often disagree about contemporary artworks.

explanations.correct: If unpopular paintings also receive critical praise, this demonstrates that critical acclaim is not limited to popular works. Combined with the given data (popular works also receive critical praise), this suggests the alignment is genuine rather than coincidental, strengthening the conclusion that popularity and merit can align.
explanations.A: Weakens — if marketing drove the exhibition's popularity (rather than merit), this undermines the alignment claim.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Irrelevant — disagreement about merit criteria does not address the alignment question.
explanations.D: Consistent with popularity/merit alignment but does not prove the alignment; collector value might be driven by investment, not merit.
explanations.E: Contradicts the alignment claim by suggesting public and critical opinions diverge, especially for contemporary work.

lr.difficultyReason: Causal inference: legal precedent caused a change in judicial practice. Alternative: judges changed their interpretation for other reasons. Correct answer rules out the alternative.
lr.stimulus: A landmark court decision was handed down in State X last year. Since then, judges in State X have applied the new legal standard established by that decision in 80 percent of relevant cases. Legal scholars conclude that the precedent has strongly influenced judicial behavior.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the scholars' conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Before the landmark decision, judges in State X applied similar legal standards in fewer than 20 percent of relevant cases.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Judges in neighboring states have also increased their application of the new legal standard.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The landmark decision was written by a respected judge with extensive legal experience.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some judges in State X have declined to apply the new legal standard in their decisions.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The new legal standard addresses an issue that has been debated for many decades.

explanations.correct: The sharp increase from under 20% to 80% application directly demonstrates that judicial behavior changed after the landmark decision, strengthening the causal claim that the precedent itself (not pre-existing judicial trends) drove the change.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Weakens — if neighboring judges (without the precedent) also increased application, an external factor (not the precedent) may be responsible.
explanations.C: Irrelevant — the judge's credentials do not prove the precedent influenced behavior.
explanations.D: Weakens — exceptions suggest the precedent did not fully drive behavior.
explanations.E: Irrelevant — the age of the debate does not address whether the precedent caused the behavioral shift.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal inference with one visible alternative. The argument claims a policy change caused improved enrollment; the correct answer rules out a competing explanation (demographic shift), making the causal claim more plausible.
lr.stimulus: Mountain Vista High School implemented a new mentorship program pairing freshman students with upperclassmen in their intended majors. The following year, enrollment in advanced mathematics courses increased by 12 percent. Therefore, the mentorship program most likely caused the increase in mathematics enrollment.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Other high schools in the state have also reported increases in advanced mathematics enrollment during the same period.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The number of freshmen at Mountain Vista High School remained stable from the year before the program to the year after its implementation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The mentorship program at Mountain Vista High School is the most expensive extracurricular initiative the school has ever funded.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Mentorship programs are more effective than traditional study groups at improving student achievement.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Students who participated in the mentorship program reported that the program improved their confidence.

explanations.correct: If the overall freshman population remained stable, the 12 percent increase in math enrollment cannot be explained by an influx of new students. This rules out a key alternative explanation and strengthens the inference that the mentorship program caused the increase.
explanations.A: Weakens or is neutral — if other schools also saw increases without the program, it suggests a wider trend unrelated to Mountain Vista's specific intervention.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Irrelevant — cost does not address whether the program caused the enrollment increase.
explanations.D: Accurate but irrelevant — generic claim about mentorship effectiveness does not confirm this specific program caused this specific enrollment gain.
explanations.E: Addresses student confidence, not enrollment causation; does not rule out alternative explanations for why enrollment increased.

lr.difficultyReason: Strengthen by confirming a load-bearing assumption about drug mechanism. Trap (A) sounds supportive but merely describes correlation; trap (D) strengthens a neighboring claim about a different patient group.
lr.stimulus: A recent clinical trial found that patients with chronic migraines who took the new drug theralin reported, on average, four fewer migraine days per month than patients who took a placebo. Theralin blocks a neuropeptide that researchers have long suspected of triggering vascular inflammation in the brain. The trial's lead investigator concluded that theralin probably reduces migraine frequency by suppressing this vascular inflammation.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Patients who experienced the greatest reduction in migraine days also reported fewer headaches overall during the trial period.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The manufacturer of theralin funded the clinical trial as part of its application for regulatory approval.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Theralin has been approved to treat several inflammatory conditions unrelated to the central nervous system.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Patients who suffer episodic rather than chronic migraines also report fewer migraine days when taking drugs that target neuropeptides.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Brain imaging of trial participants taking theralin showed markedly lower levels of vascular inflammation than imaging of those taking the placebo.

explanations.correct: The investigator's causal story has two links: theralin suppresses vascular inflammation, and that suppression is what reduces migraines. (E) directly confirms the first link with imaging evidence, making the inflammation mechanism substantially more plausible.
explanations.A: Accurate but irrelevant — fewer headaches is a near-restatement of fewer migraines and doesn't speak to the inflammation mechanism.
explanations.B: If anything, weakens by raising a conflict-of-interest concern.
explanations.C: Accurate but irrelevant — approval for unrelated inflammatory conditions doesn't establish that theralin reduces brain inflammation or that such reduction is what prevents migraines.
explanations.D: Strengthens a different conclusion — about episodic migraine patients, not the chronic-migraine group the investigator's claim concerns.
explanations.E: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Closes an analogical gap between two policy regimes. Trap (C) introduces an unwarranted comparison to a third jurisdiction; trap (E) is an alternative-cause distractor disguised as support.
lr.stimulus: Ethicist: When the city of Vellmar imposed a small fee on single-use plastic bags at grocery stores, consumption of such bags fell by nearly 80 percent within a year. Our city council is now considering a similar fee. Critics claim the fee would be ineffective here because our residents are more affluent than Vellmar's and less sensitive to small charges. But the critics are mistaken: the fee will probably reduce plastic bag consumption in our city too.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the ethicist's argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The city council is also considering a ban on single-use plastic straws at restaurants.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Vellmar also ran a public-awareness campaign about ocean pollution shortly before imposing the fee.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A neighboring city with a larger economy than the ethicist's imposed a similar fee and saw consumption fall by over 90 percent.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Grocery stores in Vellmar donated part of the bag-fee revenue to local environmental charities.

choices.label: E
choices.text: In Vellmar, the reduction in bag use was greatest among the city's wealthiest residents.

explanations.correct: The critics' objection is that affluent residents are insensitive to small charges. (E) directly undermines that premise by showing the wealthiest in Vellmar actually responded the most, closing the analogical gap between the two cities.
explanations.A: Irrelevant — plastic straws are a separate policy and don't bear on whether the bag fee will work.
explanations.B: Introduces an alternative cause — the awareness campaign, not the fee, may have driven Vellmar's drop.
explanations.C: Unwarranted comparison — the neighboring city introduces a new variable (larger economy) and doesn't address the affluence objection.
explanations.D: Introduces an alternative cause — the charitable donation could explain Vellmar's reduction, weakening the analogy rather than strengthening it.
explanations.E: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Rules out a prominent alternative cause in an economic argument. Trap (D) strengthens a sister claim about wages rather than hiring; trap (A) is the opposite answer, concessive to the alternative.
lr.stimulus: When the minimum wage in the state of Karell rose from $12 to $15 last year, critics predicted significant job losses in the restaurant industry. But restaurant employment in Karell actually grew by 3 percent over the same period. Economists have therefore concluded that moderate minimum-wage increases probably do not cause the hiring reductions critics feared.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most supports the economists' conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In years immediately preceding the wage increase, restaurant employment in Karell had been declining slightly.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Restaurant employment grew even more sharply in states that raised their minimum wage by similar amounts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Karell's overall economy experienced no unusual growth in the year the minimum wage rose.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The average hourly wage at Karell restaurants, including tips, rose by more than the minimum-wage increase alone would predict.

choices.label: E
choices.text: A few large restaurant chains closed locations in Karell during the year of the wage increase.

explanations.correct: A natural alternative is that Karell's economy was booming and masked what would otherwise have been job losses. (C) rules out that alternative by showing no unusual growth, so the minimum-wage increase is more plausibly responsible for the stable hiring.
explanations.A: Opposite answer — prior declines suggest there should have been further declines absent the wage increase, making the reversal harder to attribute to the wage change's neutrality.
explanations.B: Unwarranted comparison — other states' experiences don't by themselves rule out Karell-specific confounds.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Strengthens a different conclusion — about wage dynamics, not about hiring effects.
explanations.E: If anything, weakens, by suggesting some employment contraction did occur.

lr.difficultyReason: Bolsters an unstated premise linking recidivism to a specific program feature. Trap (B) is accurate but irrelevant; trap (E) strengthens a different conclusion about a dissimilar population.
lr.stimulus: The Kessington County jail began allowing inmates awaiting trial to participate in a voluntary job-training program. Of those who participated, only 14 percent were re-arrested within two years of release, compared with 29 percent of inmates who did not participate. Officials conclude that the program probably reduces re-arrest rates by giving former inmates marketable skills.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the officials' conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Among program participants who were re-arrested, most had failed to complete the full training curriculum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The program is funded primarily by a grant from the state's Department of Corrections.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Program participants who found employment within six months of release had re-arrest rates below 5 percent.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Participants and non-participants had similar criminal histories and demographic profiles before entering the program.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Among inmates serving post-conviction sentences, those who participated in a similar program also had lower re-arrest rates.

explanations.correct: The comparison between participants and non-participants is only meaningful if they were similar to begin with. (D) rules out the alternative that participants were already less likely to re-offend, making the causal claim substantially more plausible.
explanations.A: If anything, weakens — it suggests completion rather than mere enrollment matters, which the officials' conclusion doesn't track.
explanations.B: Accurate but irrelevant — the funding source has no bearing on whether the program reduces re-arrest.
explanations.C: Tempting but introduces a different causal mechanism (employment), which the officials didn't claim.
explanations.D: Correct.
explanations.E: Strengthens a different conclusion — about post-conviction inmates, not the pretrial population at issue.

lr.difficultyReason: Rules out an alternative cause in an environmental argument. Trap (C) is the opposite answer; trap (A) strengthens a sister claim about a different wetland.
lr.stimulus: Since the installation of a new filtration system at the textile plant upstream, the concentration of heavy metals in the Prellan wetlands has dropped by more than half. Researchers at the regional ecological institute conclude that the filtration system is probably responsible for the improved water quality.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A wetland thirty kilometers downstream from a similar textile plant has also shown declining heavy metal concentrations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Heavy metals tend to bind to sediment, which is periodically flushed from wetlands during seasonal floods.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Several other industrial facilities along the river reduced their output during the same period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The textile plant's owners have publicly committed to installing similar systems at their other facilities.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rainfall in the Prellan watershed during the year after the system's installation was consistent with the long-term average.

explanations.correct: A natural alternative is that unusual rainfall diluted the wetland's metal concentrations. (E) rules out that alternative, making the filtration system the more plausible cause of the observed drop.
explanations.A: Strengthens a different conclusion — about another wetland and another plant, not the Prellan causal claim.
explanations.B: Opposite answer — suggests a natural flushing mechanism that could account for the improvement.
explanations.C: Opposite answer — introduces an alternative cause (the other facilities) that could explain the drop independently of the filtration system.
explanations.D: Accurate but irrelevant — future commitments don't bear on past water quality.
explanations.E: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Confirms a load-bearing premise in a technological argument. Trap (B) is an unwarranted comparison; trap (E) strengthens a neighboring claim about security rather than accuracy.
lr.stimulus: A new machine-learning system for reading chest X-rays detected early-stage lung cancer in 92 percent of cases in its training dataset, compared with 78 percent for board-certified radiologists. The system's developers conclude that deploying the system at clinical sites will probably improve early cancer detection for actual patients.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In a recent trial at three hospitals unaffiliated with the developers, the system correctly identified early-stage lung cancer in 90 percent of X-rays.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Radiologists who use an older decision-support tool tend to detect cancer slightly more often than those who do not.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The system produces a visual heatmap highlighting regions of the X-ray it considers suspicious.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The developers hold several patents on machine-learning architectures for medical imaging.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The system has been certified by regulators as meeting current standards for patient data security.

explanations.correct: The developers' leap is from training-dataset accuracy to clinical performance. (A) confirms the key premise that the system generalizes to unfamiliar patients at unfamiliar sites, which is exactly what a deployment argument requires.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Unwarranted comparison — introduces a different tool with a different performance profile, without anchoring the new system's clinical prospects.
explanations.C: Accurate but irrelevant to whether the system's detection rate will hold in clinical practice.
explanations.D: Accurate but irrelevant — patents don't speak to diagnostic accuracy.
explanations.E: Strengthens a different conclusion — about data security, not detection performance.

lr.difficultyReason: Confirms a methodological assumption in a linguistic argument. Trap (E) is a plausible-sounding alternative cause; trap (B) strengthens a claim about reading comprehension, not vocabulary acquisition.
lr.stimulus: Researchers tested two groups of adult learners of Spanish. Group A studied new vocabulary using spaced repetition flashcards over six weeks; Group B studied the same vocabulary by rereading passages containing the words. On a retention test given three months later, Group A recalled significantly more vocabulary than Group B. The researchers conclude that spaced repetition is probably a more effective long-term vocabulary study method than rereading.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the researchers' conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Group A participants reported spending slightly less total time studying than Group B participants.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Both groups showed comparable gains on a reading-comprehension test given at the end of the six-week study period.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Spaced repetition has been shown to improve retention of mathematical formulas in a separate study of secondary-school students.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Before the study, the two groups scored similarly on a baseline Spanish vocabulary test.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Group A used mobile apps for their flashcards, while Group B used printed passages.

explanations.correct: The researchers' comparison assumes the two groups were starting from comparable Spanish knowledge. (D) confirms that assumption, ruling out the alternative that Group A simply knew more Spanish to begin with.
explanations.A: Tempting but ambiguous — the conclusion is about method effectiveness, not efficiency, and less total study time could equally cut against Group A's retention.
explanations.B: Strengthens a different conclusion — about reading comprehension rather than long-term vocabulary retention.
explanations.C: Unwarranted comparison — extends to a different subject and a different population.
explanations.D: Correct.
explanations.E: Introduces an alternative cause — a format difference (apps vs. print) that could independently explain the retention gap.

lr.difficultyReason: Rules out an alternative explanation in a historical argument. Trap (C) is accurate but irrelevant; trap (A) strengthens a different conclusion about a later period.
lr.stimulus: Historians have long debated why grain prices in the Roman province of Egypt fell sharply during the reign of Emperor Trajan. One historian has recently argued that the decline was driven by Trajan's construction of new irrigation canals, which increased the amount of land under cultivation. Tax records from the period show a substantial rise in grain shipments from Egyptian ports.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most supports the historian's argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Grain prices in Egypt rose again within a generation after Trajan's death.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Papyrus records indicate that many Egyptian landowners opposed the canal projects as disruptive to existing estates.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Trajan also commissioned major building projects in Rome, including a new forum and market complex.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some of the new canals were constructed by reusing materials from older, abandoned irrigation networks.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The province's population did not grow substantially during Trajan's reign, so demand for grain remained steady.

explanations.correct: A natural alternative explanation for falling prices is declining demand. (E) rules that out by showing demand was steady, leaving the supply-side explanation (more cultivated land from canals) as the more plausible cause.
explanations.A: Strengthens a different conclusion — about a later period and reversal, which doesn't bear on why prices fell under Trajan.
explanations.B: If anything, weakens — landowner opposition suggests the canal plan may have been less effective than assumed.
explanations.C: Accurate but irrelevant — building projects in Rome don't address Egyptian grain prices.
explanations.D: Accurate but irrelevant to whether the canals increased cultivable land.
explanations.E: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Confirms a premise about cause and effect in a policy argument. Trap (D) is the opposite answer; trap (E) is accurate but irrelevant.
lr.stimulus: City planner: Since the Oakridge district installed protected bicycle lanes along its main commercial street two years ago, the number of cyclists using that street has doubled, while the number of reported collisions between cyclists and motor vehicles has fallen by 40 percent. The city council should conclude that installing similar protected lanes elsewhere would probably make cycling safer in those areas as well.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, provides the most support for the planner's argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Oakridge district has a younger population on average than other districts in the city.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Oakridge residents reported feeling safer walking on their commercial street after the lanes were installed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Protected lanes in other cities of comparable size have produced similar reductions in cyclist-vehicle collisions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Motor vehicle traffic on Oakridge's main commercial street fell by 25 percent over the same two-year period.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The protected lanes in Oakridge were funded by a federal transportation grant.

explanations.correct: The planner extrapolates from Oakridge to other districts. (C) confirms that protected lanes produce similar effects in comparable settings, shoring up the analogical leap to 'other areas.'
explanations.A: Introduces an alternative cause — younger populations could cycle more safely independently of the lanes, weakening the causal claim.
explanations.B: Strengthens a different conclusion — about pedestrian safety, not cyclist safety.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Opposite answer — fewer cars could independently explain fewer collisions, undermining the claim that the lanes themselves made cycling safer.
explanations.E: Accurate but irrelevant — funding source has no bearing on the safety effect.

lr.difficultyReason: Confirms a premise about audience response in an arts argument. Trap (A) strengthens a different conclusion about ticket revenue; trap (E) is an alternative-cause distractor.
lr.stimulus: Theater critic: The Midvale Playhouse's decision to stage shorter, ninety-minute productions rather than its traditional three-hour offerings has been a success. Subscription renewals have risen for three consecutive seasons, reversing a long decline. The playhouse should continue this shorter format to sustain audience loyalty.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the critic's argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In subscriber surveys, renewing patrons most often cite the shorter running time as the reason they continued their subscriptions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Individual ticket sales at the playhouse have also increased since the shorter productions began.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A neighboring theater that kept its traditional format has seen flat subscription numbers over the same period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ninety-minute productions have become more common among regional theaters nationwide.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The playhouse hired a new artistic director in the same season it introduced the shorter format.

explanations.correct: The critic attributes rising renewals to the shorter format. (A) confirms that patrons themselves credit the shorter running time, directly tying the cited effect to the proposed cause.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Strengthens a different conclusion — about overall revenue, not about whether the shorter format is driving subscriber loyalty.
explanations.C: Accurate but weak as support — the neighboring theater's flatness has many possible causes and doesn't pin the renewal rise on format specifically.
explanations.D: Accurate but irrelevant — national trends don't establish Midvale causation.
explanations.E: Introduces an alternative cause — the new artistic director could be the real driver of renewal gains.

lr.difficultyReason: Rules out an alternative cause in a medical prevention argument. Trap (D) is plausible support but strengthens a different population's claim; trap (B) is accurate but irrelevant.
lr.stimulus: A cardiologist observed that her patients who had been taking a daily low-dose aspirin for at least five years were less likely to have a first heart attack than those who had not taken aspirin. She concluded that daily low-dose aspirin probably reduces the risk of a first heart attack.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the cardiologist's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aspirin is inexpensive and widely available without a prescription.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patients taking daily aspirin also reported lower incidences of common headaches.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Patients in the two groups had similar rates of smoking, hypertension, and family history of heart disease.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Among patients who had already suffered one heart attack, those who took daily aspirin had fewer subsequent heart attacks.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Daily aspirin has been linked in other studies to a slightly increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding.

explanations.correct: A reader should suspect that aspirin takers are simply healthier or more risk-averse to begin with. (C) rules out that alternative by equalizing the groups on key cardiac risk factors, isolating aspirin as the plausible cause.
explanations.A: Accurate but irrelevant to whether aspirin reduces risk.
explanations.B: Accurate but irrelevant — headache rates don't bear on first-heart-attack risk.
explanations.C: Correct.
explanations.D: Strengthens a different conclusion — about recurrent rather than first heart attacks.
explanations.E: If anything, weakens, by suggesting a countervailing harm.

lr.difficultyReason: Bolsters an ethical argument by confirming an unstated empirical assumption. Trap (A) is accurate but irrelevant to the moral claim; trap (C) strengthens a different, more permissive conclusion.
lr.stimulus: Ethicist: Animal welfare advocates argue that factory farming is unethical because it causes substantial suffering to farm animals. Some philosophers reply that this suffering is ethically insignificant because farm animals such as chickens and pigs lack the cognitive capacity for suffering in any morally relevant sense. But this reply is probably mistaken, and advocates are right to criticize the practice.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the ethicist's argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Neuroscientific studies have shown that chickens and pigs possess brain structures that mediate pain experience in much the same way as those of species whose suffering is widely recognized as morally significant.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Factory-farmed meat is generally cheaper for consumers than meat from smaller, non-industrial farms.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some philosophers hold that even animals that clearly can suffer may permissibly be killed for food under humane conditions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Several countries have enacted laws restricting certain factory-farming practices, citing animal-welfare concerns.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Consumer surveys indicate that most meat buyers prefer not to think about the conditions under which farm animals are raised.

explanations.correct: The ethicist must rebut the philosophers' empirical premise that chickens and pigs lack the capacity for morally relevant suffering. (A) directly undercuts that premise with neuroscientific evidence, making the ethicist's conclusion more likely.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Accurate but irrelevant — price doesn't speak to the moral question at issue.
explanations.C: Strengthens a different conclusion — one that permits humane killing, which is not the ethicist's claim.
explanations.D: Accurate but weak support — legal enactments reflect opinion rather than settle the philosophical dispute.
explanations.E: Accurate but irrelevant — consumer psychology doesn't bear on the moral status of the animals.

lr.difficultyReason: Closes an analogical gap in a legal argument. Trap (C) strengthens a neighboring claim about appellate review; trap (E) is accurate but irrelevant.
lr.stimulus: Defense attorney: My client was convicted largely on testimony from a single eyewitness who identified him in a lineup conducted under poor lighting and considerable stress. Courts in this jurisdiction have overturned convictions in at least three comparable cases where a single stressed eyewitness's identification was the central evidence. The appellate court should therefore probably overturn my client's conviction.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most supports the defense attorney's argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The prosecutor who tried the client's case has a higher-than-average conviction rate in this jurisdiction.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The client has maintained his innocence consistently throughout the trial and subsequent appeals.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The appellate court has overturned convictions in several cases involving improper jury instructions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In each of the three overturned cases, the appellate court cited research showing that stress and poor lighting substantially reduce eyewitness accuracy.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The client has no prior criminal record in this or any other jurisdiction.

explanations.correct: The attorney's argument relies on the analogy between this case and the three overturned cases. (D) confirms the ground of that analogy — that the same features (stress, poor lighting) were the basis for overturning — making the comparison much stronger.
explanations.A: Accurate but irrelevant — the prosecutor's record doesn't bear on appellate reversal.
explanations.B: Accurate but irrelevant — a defendant's protestations don't affect appellate standards.
explanations.C: Strengthens a different conclusion — about jury-instruction reversals, not eyewitness-based reversals.
explanations.D: Correct.
explanations.E: Accurate but irrelevant to whether the eyewitness identification is legally adequate.

lr.difficultyReason: Confirms a mechanism in an environmental argument. Trap (A) is the opposite answer; trap (D) strengthens a different conclusion about a distinct species.
lr.stimulus: After the state banned the use of a common agricultural pesticide, the population of the tricolor skipper butterfly in nearby meadows rose sharply for the first time in a decade. Entomologists conclude that the pesticide had probably been suppressing the butterfly's population.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the entomologists' conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Some farmers who had used the banned pesticide have switched to alternatives that entomologists consider less harmful to pollinators.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Monarch butterfly populations in the same region also increased after the ban took effect.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Weather conditions in the meadows during the year of the ban were similar to those in earlier years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Laboratory tests show that even trace amounts of the banned pesticide are lethal to tricolor skipper larvae.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The banned pesticide had been marketed primarily as a treatment for aphids and other insect pests.

explanations.correct: The entomologists posit that the pesticide suppressed the butterflies. (D) supplies a mechanism — lethality to larvae at trace doses — that directly connects the pesticide to population suppression.
explanations.A: Opposite answer — if alternatives are in use, some of the new chemicals (not just the ban) could be affecting the population.
explanations.B: Strengthens a different conclusion — about a different species, suggesting at most a general effect rather than anchoring the tricolor skipper claim.
explanations.C: Helpful but weaker: rules out one alternative (weather) but doesn't tie the pesticide to the effect the way a mechanism does.
explanations.D: Correct.
explanations.E: Accurate but irrelevant — the pesticide's marketed target doesn't establish its effect on butterflies.

lr.difficultyReason: Rules out an alternative explanation in a technology-adoption argument. Trap (B) is accurate but irrelevant; trap (E) strengthens a different conclusion about a different demographic.
