The owner attributes growth to the menu alone, but improved staffing could have increased service quality and customer capacity, thereby driving revenue growth independently of the vegetarian options.
explanations.A: Irrelevant to whether the menu expansion caused the revenue increase; cost of preparation does not explain the rise in overall revenue.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Other restaurants offering vegetarian options does not explain why this particular restaurant's revenue grew; if anything, it might suggest competition, but doesn't weaken the causal claim about the owner's own expansion.
explanations.D: Supports the relevance of the vegetarian addition; if vegetarian customers spend equally, they contribute proportionally to revenue growth.
explanations.E: Irrelevant; the question is not whether vegetarian options dominate the menu, but whether their addition caused revenue growth.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple causal claim in a medical context. The stimulus links a drug dosage increase to symptom improvement; the correct answer introduces timing or alternative causation.
lr.stimulus: A pharmaceutical company conducted a study in which patients taking a pain reliever at the recommended dosage reported an average pain reduction of 30%. When the dosage was increased by 50%, patients reported an average pain reduction of 50%. The company claims that the increased dosage is the cause of the improved pain relief.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the pharmaceutical company's claim?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Patients in the higher-dosage group were aware that they were receiving a larger dose.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The study lasted six months, which is a sufficient timeframe for a drug's effects to stabilize.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pain relievers at all dosages interact negatively with certain other medications.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The higher-dosage group began the study one month after their initial pain episodes, whereas the standard-dosage group was enrolled immediately after symptoms onset.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The higher dosage is associated with mild gastrointestinal side effects in some patients.

explanations.correct: If the higher-dosage group started the study one month after symptom onset, their pain may have naturally diminished over that month before the study began. This timing difference provides an alternative explanation for the observed improvement in pain reduction and undermines the claim that dosage alone caused the better outcome.
explanations.A: Strengthens the causal claim; awareness that they received a higher dose is not evidence that the dose itself didn't work — it could even reinforce the effect through placebo, but the effect is still real.
explanations.B: Irrelevant to whether dosage caused the improvement; establishing a stable timeframe doesn't address competing explanations.
explanations.C: Irrelevant; drug interactions don't explain why one dosage works better than another in the same population.
explanations.D: Correct.
explanations.E: Irrelevant to the causal mechanism; side effects do not address whether increased dosage improves pain relief.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal claim in an economic context. The stimulus links a tax cut to business expansion; the correct answer offers a confounding factor.
lr.stimulus: After the city council enacted a 15% property tax reduction for businesses, commercial expansion in the downtown district increased significantly over the next year. City officials attribute this expansion directly to the tax cut, arguing that lower taxes freed up capital for reinvestment.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the officials' argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The 15% property tax reduction applies only to businesses that expanded their facilities.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A major technology corporation announced plans to relocate its regional headquarters to the downtown district three months before the tax cut was enacted.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Previous tax reductions in the city have had minimal impact on commercial expansion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Many businesses in the downtown district report that the tax reduction was welcomed but not decisive in their expansion decisions.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The commercial expansion rate in surrounding municipalities remained flat during the same year.

explanations.correct: If the technology corporation announced its relocation before the tax cut was enacted, the expansion was likely already planned and anticipated. This provides an alternative explanation for the observed commercial growth, independent of the tax reduction. The expansion would have occurred even without the tax cut.
explanations.A: Irrelevant; whether the tax cut applied before or after expansion does not address whether it caused the expansion.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Weakens by undermining the general causal link, but doesn't directly contradict the officials' specific claim about this expansion.
explanations.D: While businesses say the tax cut wasn't decisive, this is a weak weakener because 'welcome but not decisive' is ambiguous and doesn't rule out that it contributed.
explanations.E: Strengthens the claim; if surrounding areas stayed flat while the downtown expanded, the tax cut appears more influential.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal claim about student performance. The stimulus attributes test score gains to a new teaching method; the correct answer introduces an alternative cause.
lr.stimulus: A school district implemented a new reading curriculum focused on phonetic instruction. In the year following implementation, standardized reading test scores for third-grade students increased by an average of 12 percentile points. The superintendent concludes that the new curriculum is responsible for the improved test performance.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the superintendent's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The increase in test scores was consistent across all demographic groups in the district.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Third-grade teachers received extensive professional development and coaching specific to the new curriculum.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Phonetic instruction is based on decades of educational research supporting its effectiveness.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In the same year the new curriculum was adopted, the district also reduced class sizes from 25 to 20 students.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Several other districts that adopted the same curriculum also saw increased reading test scores.

explanations.correct: Reducing class size from 25 to 20 is a significant confounding variable. Smaller class sizes are known to improve academic outcomes independently, so the 12-percentile-point gain may result from the smaller classes rather than the new curriculum itself.
explanations.A: Strengthens by showing the effect was robust and not limited to one group; consistency actually supports the causal claim.
explanations.B: Strengthens; teacher training supports the idea that the curriculum was properly implemented and thus caused the gains.
explanations.C: Strengthens by lending credibility to the curriculum's causal potential.
explanations.D: Correct.
explanations.E: Strengthens by providing corroborating evidence across multiple districts.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple causal claim about environmental policy. The stimulus links a pesticide ban to bird population recovery; the correct answer offers a competing explanation.
lr.stimulus: An environmental agency banned the use of a pesticide known to harm bird populations. Two years after the ban took effect, the population of songbirds in the region increased by 40%. The agency attributes this increase directly to the pesticide ban.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the agency's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The songbird population had been declining steadily for the previous decade before the ban.

choices.label: B
choices.text: During the same two-year period, several new wildlife preserves were established in the region, providing additional habitat for songbirds.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The pesticide was widely used by agricultural operations throughout the region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Songbird populations in regions where the pesticide was still legal remained stable during the same period.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The pesticide had been banned in other regions with similar results.

explanations.correct: The establishment of new wildlife preserves provides an alternative explanation for the 40% population increase. Increased habitat alone could drive population growth, independent of or in addition to the pesticide ban. This undermines the agency's claim that the ban was the direct cause.
explanations.A: Strengthens by confirming that conditions improved after the ban; prior decline makes the recovery more attributable to the ban.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Supports the causal claim; widespread use makes the ban's impact more plausible.
explanations.D: Strengthens by showing a contrast; regions without the ban saw no increase, suggesting the ban caused the increase in the region studied.
explanations.E: Strengthens by providing corroborating evidence in other regions.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal claim about technology adoption. The stimulus links a software update to productivity gains; the correct answer introduces a temporal confound.
lr.stimulus: A company rolled out a new software system designed to streamline workflow. In the three months following the rollout, employee productivity increased by 18% on average. Management concludes that the new software is responsible for the productivity improvement.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens management's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The company provides regular training to employees on new software systems.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Three months after the software rollout, the company also implemented a new performance bonus system tied to productivity metrics.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The software system had been thoroughly tested before rollout and was found to be reliable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Different departments experienced similar productivity gains despite using the software in different ways.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The software required employees to change their established work processes.

explanations.correct: If a performance bonus system was also implemented at the same time, this provides an alternative explanation for the productivity increase. Employees may have worked harder due to the incentive structure rather than because of the software's efficiency.
explanations.A: Strengthens by suggesting the software was properly adopted and thus more likely to drive gains.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Strengthens; reliability supports the idea that the software functioned as intended and caused the gains.
explanations.D: Strengthens by showing consistent results across departments; this supports the causal link.
explanations.E: Irrelevant; requiring process change does not explain whether the software caused productivity gains.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal claim about legal policy. The stimulus links a stricter enforcement policy to crime reduction; the correct answer offers an alternative explanation.
lr.stimulus: A police department implemented a strict enforcement policy targeting minor infractions such as traffic violations and disorderly conduct. Within one year, reported felony crimes in the jurisdiction decreased by 25%. Department officials attribute this decline to the deterrent effect of strict enforcement.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the officials' argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Police officers conducting traffic stops reported that they were more aware of criminal activity in their jurisdiction.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the same year the strict enforcement policy was implemented, unemployment in the jurisdiction decreased by 12%.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The strict enforcement policy required training of officers to recognize patterns associated with serious crimes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Other jurisdictions that adopted similar strict enforcement policies also reported reductions in felony crimes.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Crime prevention advocates had long argued that strict enforcement of minor infractions would reduce serious crimes.

explanations.correct: If unemployment decreased by 12% in the same year, this provides an alternative explanation for the crime reduction. Improved economic conditions and employment are known to reduce crime independently of enforcement policies. The crime decrease may result from economic improvement rather than the strict enforcement policy.
explanations.A: Strengthens by suggesting officers gained the ability to detect crime through the increased enforcement activity.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Strengthens by supporting the idea that the policy was implemented with the intent and capability to reduce serious crimes.
explanations.D: Strengthens by providing corroborating evidence across multiple jurisdictions.
explanations.E: Strengthens by providing expert support for the causal claim; advocates predicted this outcome.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal claim about medical intervention. The stimulus links a new exercise regimen to weight loss; the correct answer introduces a confounding change.
lr.stimulus: A fitness clinic introduced a new high-intensity interval training regimen. Participants in the program lost an average of 18 pounds over eight weeks. The clinic's director concludes that the intensity and design of the new training regimen is the primary cause of this weight loss.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the director's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: High-intensity interval training is known to burn more calories per unit of time than moderate-intensity continuous exercise.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Participants in the program were also required to follow a structured low-calorie meal plan provided by the clinic.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The clinic's facility was upgraded with new exercise equipment concurrent with the introduction of the training regimen.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Participants reported high satisfaction with the training program and indicated they intended to continue exercising.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Most participants had not engaged in regular exercise for at least two years prior to enrolling in the program.

explanations.correct: If participants followed a structured low-calorie meal plan simultaneously with the exercise regimen, dietary change provides an alternative explanation for the weight loss. The 18-pound loss may result from calorie restriction rather than the training regimen's intensity and design.
explanations.A: Strengthens by supporting that the high-intensity approach is physiologically effective for calorie burning.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Irrelevant; new equipment does not provide an alternative explanation for weight loss, though it might support the claim.
explanations.D: Irrelevant to causation; participant satisfaction does not explain what caused the weight loss.
explanations.E: Strengthens by suggesting participants were deconditioned and thus more likely to benefit from a new training stimulus.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal claim about historical event. The stimulus links a new marketing campaign to sales growth; the correct answer introduces a market-wide confound.
lr.stimulus: A beverage company launched an aggressive marketing campaign featuring celebrity endorsements. In the following quarter, the company's sales increased by 35%. The marketing director attributes this growth to the campaign's persuasive power and the appeal of the celebrity endorsers.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the marketing director's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The celebrity chosen for the campaign had a large and loyal fan base.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Industry-wide beverage sales increased by 30% during the same quarter due to favorable weather and increased outdoor consumption.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The company's television advertisements were aired during prime-time slots with high viewership ratings.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Competitors did not launch similarly high-profile marketing campaigns during the same period.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The beverage company had previously used celebrity endorsements without achieving significant sales growth.

explanations.correct: If the entire beverage industry experienced a 30% sales increase in the same quarter, this provides an alternative explanation for the company's 35% increase. The growth may be attributable to favorable market conditions (weather, outdoor consumption) rather than the marketing campaign. The campaign's impact is unclear when industry-wide growth is accounted for.
explanations.A: Strengthens by explaining why the celebrity endorsement would have been persuasive.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Strengthens by supporting the campaign's reach and persuasive potential.
explanations.D: Strengthens by suggesting the company had a competitive advertising advantage.
explanations.E: Weakens but is not the best answer; it attacks past performance but doesn't directly explain the current increase.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal claim about language acquisition. The stimulus links a language immersion program to student proficiency; the correct answer introduces a selection bias.
lr.stimulus: A school district implemented a new language immersion program in which all instruction in mathematics and science is conducted in Spanish. After one year, students in the immersion program scored 22 percentage points higher on Spanish proficiency assessments than students in the traditional program. The superintendent concludes that the immersion approach is responsible for this superior proficiency.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the superintendent's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students in the immersion program reported greater confidence in their ability to communicate in Spanish.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The immersion program requires students to complete an entrance assessment, and only students with prior Spanish language exposure were admitted.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The immersion program employed native Spanish speakers as teachers in the mathematics and science courses.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Research on language immersion has consistently demonstrated its effectiveness across multiple studies and school contexts.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Teachers in both programs used interactive, student-centered instructional techniques.

explanations.correct: If only students with prior Spanish language exposure were admitted to the immersion program, the higher proficiency scores may result from the students' pre-existing language background rather than the immersion approach itself. This selection bias undermines the causal claim that the program design caused the improvement.
explanations.A: Supports the efficacy of the program; greater confidence correlates with the program's potential effectiveness.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Strengthens by supporting the quality of instruction in the program.
explanations.D: Strengthens by providing external evidence for the immersion method's effectiveness.
explanations.E: Irrelevant; both programs using the same teaching techniques doesn't explain the performance difference.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal claim with one obvious alternative explanation. The argument attributes a business outcome to one factor (new marketing strategy), and the correct answer supplies a competing cause (change in consumer preferences) that would account for the result without the claimed cause.
lr.stimulus: A marketing director at a retail chain observed that after implementing a new advertising strategy emphasizing customer testimonials, sales increased by 25% over the following quarter. The director concluded that the new advertising strategy directly caused the sales increase.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The retail chain had used customer testimonials in advertisements five years prior.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A major competitor closed its store in the area during the same quarter that the new advertising strategy was implemented.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Several employees of the retail chain reported that they appreciated the new advertising strategy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The advertising budget was increased by 15% at the same time the new strategy was introduced.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Customer testimonials are generally considered an effective form of advertising by marketing professionals.

explanations.correct: This answer provides an alternative explanation for the 25% sales increase that does not depend on the new advertising strategy. If a major competitor closed, the sales increase could result from customers switching to this chain, not from the testimonial-based ads.
explanations.A: Irrelevant historical fact. That the strategy was used before doesn't address whether it caused the recent increase.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Employee appreciation is irrelevant to whether the strategy caused the sales increase.
explanations.D: Actually strengthens rather than weakens. An increased budget might support the argument that the strategy (with more resources) drove sales up.
explanations.E: Supports the plausibility of the strategy working; does not undermine the causal claim.

lr.difficultyReason: Straightforward causal overreach. A physician attributes a patient's improvement to a new medication, and the correct weakener shows the improvement may have a different cause (natural recovery from a viral infection).
lr.stimulus: A physician prescribed an antiviral medication to a patient who had contracted a viral infection. After one week of taking the medication, the patient's symptoms subsided significantly. The physician concluded that the antiviral medication was responsible for the patient's recovery.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The antiviral medication has been shown in clinical trials to reduce the duration of viral infections by an average of three days.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most patients infected with this particular viral infection experience a significant subsidence of symptoms within one to two weeks even without treatment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The patient reported that the medication was easy to take and had tolerable side effects.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Other patients who have taken the same antiviral medication reported improved symptoms within the same time frame.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The patient also received nutritional counseling during the same week she took the medication.

explanations.correct: This answer undermines the causal claim by showing that the observed symptom subsidence is consistent with the natural course of the infection, regardless of medication. If most patients recover on this timeline without treatment, the physician cannot confidently attribute this particular patient's recovery to the drug.
explanations.A: Strengthens by showing the drug does reduce infection duration in clinical settings.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Irrelevant to causation; the patient's experience of side effects doesn't address whether the drug caused recovery.
explanations.D: Strengthens by corroborating the drug's effect in other cases.
explanations.E: Introduces a potential alternative cause, but nutritional counseling is a weaker competitor than natural recovery; (B) is a clearer weakener.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple causal claim about environmental policy with one clear competing explanation. The stimulus attributes increased bird populations to a conservation program; the correct answer shows a confounding factor (mild winters) that could account for the increase independently.
lr.stimulus: An environmental organization implemented a habitat restoration program in a wetland area. Over the next two years, ornithologists observed a 40% increase in the number of migratory birds visiting the wetland. The organization concluded that the habitat restoration program caused the increase in bird populations.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Migratory birds are sensitive to changes in weather patterns and food availability.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The habitat restoration program involved planting native vegetation and removing invasive species.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The two winters preceding the bird count were significantly milder than the historical average for the region.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Habitat restoration programs in other wetlands have also resulted in increases in migratory bird populations.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The organization's budget for the restoration program was significantly larger than originally planned.

explanations.correct: Milder winters would naturally reduce bird mortality and could easily account for increased populations without any contribution from the habitat restoration. This provides a competing causal explanation that undermines the organization's conclusion.
explanations.A: General background fact about bird behavior; doesn't provide an alternative cause for this specific increase.
explanations.B: Describes what the program did; supports rather than weakens the idea that it could have caused the increase.
explanations.D: Strengthens by showing the program's effectiveness in other locations.
explanations.E: Budget information is irrelevant to whether the program actually caused the bird increase.
explanations.C: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Direct single-cause causal claim in economics. A company attributes profit growth to cost-cutting, and the correct answer shows another factor (increased market demand) explains the profit without relying on the stated cause.
lr.stimulus: A manufacturing company reduced its production costs by 20% through automation and workforce restructuring. The company's profit margin increased by 18% in the following fiscal year. The chief financial officer attributed this profit increase entirely to the cost-cutting measures.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously undermines the argument's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The average profit margin in the manufacturing industry remained stable during the same fiscal year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Industry-wide demand for the company's product increased substantially during the fiscal year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The automation process required significant capital investment in new machinery and training.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Several of the company's competitors also implemented cost-cutting measures during the same period.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The company's revenues had been declining for three years before the cost-cutting measures were implemented.

explanations.correct: If demand increased substantially, the company would have earned higher profits regardless of cost cuts. This provides an alternative explanation for the profit increase that does not depend on the restructuring, thereby weakening the CFO's attribution.
explanations.A: Irrelevant; other companies' margins don't address what caused this company's increase.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Acknowledges a cost of the program but doesn't undermine the claim that it still increased net profit margins.
explanations.D: Irrelevant; competitors' actions don't explain this company's profit increase.
explanations.E: Provides context but doesn't identify an alternative cause for the profit increase.

lr.difficultyReason: Causal claim in linguistics about language learning. Stimulus attributes improved language proficiency to immersion methodology; correct answer shows the improvement could result from increased study time rather than the methodology itself.
lr.stimulus: A language school introduced a full immersion methodology in which students spoke only the target language during classroom hours. Within three months, the school's students showed a measurable improvement in oral proficiency compared to the previous year's cohort. The school's director concluded that the immersion methodology was responsible for the improvement.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students in the immersion program spent significantly more hours per week in structured study than students in the previous cohort.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some students found the immersion methodology challenging and reported high levels of classroom anxiety.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Immersion methodology has been recognized as an effective approach to language learning in peer-reviewed studies.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The students' native languages are similar in grammatical structure to the target language.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The director had previously taught at another school where immersion was also used.

explanations.correct: If the immersion cohort spent significantly more study hours than the previous cohort, their improvement could result from increased practice time rather than the immersion method itself. This confounding variable undermines the causal claim.
explanations.B: Irrelevant; student anxiety doesn't explain whether the methodology caused the improvement.
explanations.C: Strengthens by providing external evidence for the methodology's effectiveness.
explanations.D: Background information about native-language similarity; doesn't address the causal claim.
explanations.E: Biographical detail irrelevant to the causal conclusion about the current program.
explanations.A: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Straightforward causal claim in technology. A software company attributes user engagement increase to a UI redesign; the correct weakener shows the increase coincided with a marketing campaign that could account for the outcome.
lr.stimulus: A software company redesigned the user interface of its flagship application to be more intuitive. In the month following the redesign, the company recorded a 35% increase in daily active users. The company's product manager concluded that the interface redesign drove the user engagement increase.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Users generally prefer intuitive interfaces over complex ones.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The company launched a major advertising campaign promoting the application the same week the redesign was released.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Several months before the redesign, the company's daily active user count had been declining steadily.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The company did not change its pricing structure at the time of the redesign.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some users reported that they found the new interface confusing at first.

explanations.correct: The advertising campaign launched simultaneously with the redesign could fully account for the 35% user increase. This provides an alternative explanation that undermines the product manager's attribution to the UI redesign alone.
explanations.A: General statement about user preferences; doesn't identify an alternative cause for this specific increase.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Provides context about prior decline but doesn't identify an alternative cause for the recent increase.
explanations.D: Absence of a price change doesn't support the UI redesign as the causal factor.
explanations.E: Some initial confusion is irrelevant to whether the overall redesign drove engagement up.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple causal claim in ethics/policy. A hospital administrator attributes a reduction in readmission rates to a new patient-education program; the correct answer shows a competing cause (improved medications) explains the outcome.
lr.stimulus: A hospital implemented a new patient-education program designed to improve patient adherence to treatment plans. Six months later, the hospital's 30-day readmission rate had decreased by 12% compared to the previous year. The hospital administrator concluded that the patient-education program was responsible for reducing readmissions.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The hospital also increased the frequency of follow-up appointments during the same period.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patient-education programs have been shown to improve health outcomes in other hospitals as well.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The pharmacy adopted new medications with fewer side effects and better patient tolerance during the same six-month period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The hospital's staff members received training on the patient-education program prior to its implementation.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some patients reported that they found the education materials difficult to understand.

explanations.correct: If the pharmacy introduced medications with better tolerance and fewer side effects, this could explain the decreased readmission rate independently of the education program. This competing cause weakens the administrator's causal attribution.
explanations.A: More frequent follow-ups is itself an intervention that could strengthen the education program's effect; however, (C) is a clearer independent explanation.
explanations.B: Strengthens by showing the program's track record elsewhere.
explanations.D: Staff training is part of implementing the program; doesn't undermine the causal claim.
explanations.E: Some patient difficulty doesn't address whether the program caused the readmission reduction overall.
explanations.C: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal claim in history/education. A school principal attributes improved test scores to a new curriculum; the correct answer shows a confounding factor (composition change in the student body) explains the improvement.
lr.stimulus: A high school adopted a new mathematics curriculum emphasizing conceptual understanding over rote memorization. The following year, students' average scores on the state mathematics standardized test increased by 8 percentage points. The principal concluded that the new curriculum was responsible for the improvement in test performance.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously undermines the argument's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The state mathematics standardized test is widely recognized as a valid measure of student mathematical proficiency.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A significant number of low-performing students transferred to a vocational school during the same school year.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mathematics teachers at the school received professional development training on the new curriculum.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Other schools in the district did not adopt the new curriculum and did not experience significant test score increases.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The principal had been an advocate for curriculum reform prior to becoming a school administrator.

explanations.correct: If low-performing students left the school, the remaining cohort would naturally score higher on average, regardless of curriculum changes. This compositional change provides an alternative explanation that undermines the principal's causal claim.
explanations.A: Confirms test validity; supports rather than weakens the argument.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Supports the implementation of the new curriculum and its potential effectiveness.
explanations.D: Strengthens by suggesting the curriculum, not some regional factor, drove the improvement.
explanations.E: Biographical information irrelevant to whether the curriculum caused the improvement.

lr.difficultyReason: Direct causal attribution in arts/cultural policy. A museum director attributes increased visitor attendance to a new exhibition; the correct answer shows a competing cause (holiday season timing) explains the attendance spike.
lr.stimulus: A museum opened a special exhibition of impressionist paintings. In the month following the exhibition's opening, museum attendance increased by 45% compared to the same month in the previous year. The museum director concluded that the impressionist exhibition was the cause of the attendance increase.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Impressionist paintings are among the most popular art styles with museum visitors.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The museum reduced its general admission fee by 25% during the month of the special exhibition.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The museum's special exhibitions have historically had a modest effect on monthly attendance.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The exhibition opened during the major holiday shopping season, when retail activity and public entertainment visits typically increase.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The museum had hosted impressionist exhibitions twice before, and both had attracted significant attendance.

explanations.correct: If the exhibition opened during the holiday season, when people naturally visit museums and entertainment venues more frequently, the 45% increase could result from seasonal patterns rather than the exhibition's appeal. This provides an alternative explanation.
explanations.A: Strengthens by showing impressionist works would draw interest.
explanations.B: Provides an alternative cause (lower price) for the increase, but holiday timing is a stronger competing explanation.
explanations.C: Weakens the causal claim, but (D) is more directly explanatory.
explanations.E: Strengthens by showing the exhibition type has worked before.
explanations.D: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple causal claim in law/criminal justice. A district attorney attributes a crime-rate decline to a new enforcement policy; the correct answer shows a competing factor (demographic shift in the community) explains the reduction.
lr.stimulus: A district attorney's office implemented a policy of aggressive prosecution for minor drug offenses. Within one year, the recorded crime rate in the jurisdiction decreased by 20%. The district attorney concluded that the aggressive prosecution policy was responsible for the crime reduction.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Aggressive prosecution policies have been criticized by civil rights advocates as unfairly targeting certain populations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The jurisdiction experienced substantial demographic changes during the same year, with young adults moving out of the area in large numbers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Other jurisdictions that did not adopt aggressive prosecution policies also experienced crime-rate increases.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The aggressive prosecution policy did not apply to serious felonies, only to minor drug offenses.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Police departments in the jurisdiction also increased patrols during the same period the new prosecution policy was implemented.

explanations.correct: A substantial outmigration of young adults would naturally reduce crime rates regardless of enforcement policies, since younger populations typically have higher crime involvement. This demographic shift provides a competing explanation for the decline.
explanations.A: Ethical criticism doesn't address whether the policy actually caused the crime reduction.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Irrelevant; what other jurisdictions did doesn't explain this jurisdiction's crime decline.
explanations.D: Establishes the policy's scope but doesn't identify an alternative cause for the decline.
explanations.E: Increased patrols might reinforce the prosecution policy's effect; doesn't weaken the causal claim.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal claim with one obvious alternative explanation. Stimulus: price increase caused lower sales. Correct answer introduces a confounding variable (competitor entered market) that provides an obvious alternative cause.
lr.stimulus: In the past year, the widget division of Acme Corporation reduced production by 20% immediately after implementing a 15% price increase on its main product. Company executives concluded that the price increase caused the reduction in sales. The reduction forced the company to scale back manufacturing, explaining the 20% drop in production volume.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Acme Corporation's widget division had reduced production in previous years without implementing price increases.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A major competitor launched a heavily marketed new widget product in the same month the price increase took effect.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The widget division's profit margin increased despite the reduction in sales volume.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most industries experience some fluctuation in sales volume year to year.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Acme Corporation's other product divisions did not implement price increases during the same period.

explanations.correct: If a competitor launched a new product around the same time as the price increase, the sales decline could be explained by lost market share to the competitor rather than by the price increase itself. This alternative explanation undermines the conclusion that the price increase caused the sales reduction.
explanations.A: While this shows production reductions occurred before, it does not explain away the current decline or suggest an alternative cause for this year's reduction. It's consistent with price increases being the cause this time.
explanations.B: Correct. This provides a plausible competing explanation for the sales drop.
explanations.C: Increased profit margins despite lower volume may actually support the price increase as beneficial, rather than weakening the argument that it caused the decline.
explanations.D: This generic fact about industry volatility does not explain this specific sales drop or suggest the price increase was not the cause.
explanations.E: What other divisions did is irrelevant to whether the price increase caused the widget division's sales decline.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple predictive argument with one obvious confounding variable. Stimulus claims a museum's free-admission policy caused increased attendance. Correct answer shows attendance rose for a separate, independent reason.
lr.stimulus: The City Museum implemented a new free-admission policy last month. Since the policy's introduction, attendance at the museum has increased by 35%. The director credits the free-admission policy with driving this increase in visitors, arguing that removing the price barrier has made the museum more accessible to the public.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Other museums in the city do not charge admission fees.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The museum had introduced several new exhibits featuring renowned artwork during the same month the free-admission policy took effect.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Free-admission policies typically increase attendance at cultural institutions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The museum's operating costs increased after implementing the free-admission policy.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Surveys show that price is an important factor in people's decisions about museum attendance.

explanations.correct: If new exhibits featuring renowned artwork were introduced in the same month as the free-admission policy, the attendance increase could be attributed to the new exhibits rather than the removal of admission fees. This provides an alternative explanation for the 35% rise in visitors.
explanations.A: What other museums charge is irrelevant to why this museum's attendance increased.
explanations.B: Correct. This offers a competing explanation for the attendance surge.
explanations.C: This actually strengthens the argument by confirming that free policies generally drive attendance.
explanations.D: Cost increases to the museum do not explain why attendance went up; this is about the museum's finances, not visitor motivation.
explanations.E: This would support the argument that the price barrier removal drove the increase; it strengthens rather than weakens.

lr.difficultyReason: Straightforward analogical argument where the conclusion overreaches similarity between two cases. Stimulus claims one technology will succeed because a similar technology succeeded. Correct answer reveals a disanalogy that breaks the analogy.
lr.stimulus: The transition to hybrid vehicles in the automotive market succeeded because consumers recognized both environmental and financial benefits. Smartphone manufacturers should have equal success transitioning consumers to foldable phones, since foldable phones offer similar technological advantages and aesthetic benefits. Thus, the foldable phone transition will follow the same successful trajectory as the hybrid vehicle transition.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Foldable phones currently have a higher price point than most conventional smartphones.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Hybrid vehicles require relatively minimal changes to driving habits and infrastructure.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some early adopters of hybrid vehicles reported experiencing mechanical problems.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Foldable phones have been available to consumers for several years now.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Smartphone manufacturers have successfully introduced other technological innovations in the past.

explanations.correct: The argument assumes that because both offer 'technological and aesthetic benefits,' they will succeed similarly. However, a critical disanalogy emerges: hybrid vehicles required minimal changes to infrastructure and habit, while foldable phones—if they require new behaviors or ecosystem adjustments—present a different adoption barrier. This breaks the analogy and weakens the conclusion.
explanations.A: A price premium could explain slower adoption, but this is compatible with eventual success, so it only moderately weakens. (B) is more direct.
explanations.B: Correct. This highlights a key difference: hybrids fit seamlessly into existing driving patterns, whereas foldable phones might require greater behavioral changes, breaking the analogy.
explanations.C: Early mechanical problems plagued hybrids too; this is not a disanalogy.
explanations.D: The availability timeline doesn't explain why the adoption trajectories differ or strengthen the analogy.
explanations.E: Past innovation success doesn't guarantee the foldable phone will follow the hybrid path, and doesn't address the analogy.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal claim with obvious alternative explanation. Stimulus argues that switching suppliers caused cost reduction; correct answer introduces timing confound (new efficiency program launched simultaneously).
lr.stimulus: A manufacturing firm switched to a new supplier for its component parts last year. Since making this switch, the firm's production costs have dropped by 12 percent. Therefore, switching to the new supplier was the cause of the cost reduction.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The new supplier's components are more durable than those from the previous supplier.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Unrelated to the supplier switch, the firm implemented a new manufacturing efficiency program at the same time it switched suppliers.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The firm's competitors have also switched to the same new supplier in recent years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The new supplier is located in a region with lower labor costs than the previous supplier's region.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The firm's profit margins have increased along with the cost reduction.

explanations.correct: By introducing an alternative cause operating at the same time as the supplier switch, this answer undermines the conclusion that the switch itself caused the cost reduction. The cost drop could instead result from the efficiency program.
explanations.A: This fact supports the value of the new supplier but does not address whether the supplier switch caused the observed cost reduction.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: This is consistent with the supplier being a good choice but does not weaken the causal claim.
explanations.D: This actually strengthens the argument by providing a mechanism (lower labor costs) explaining why the supplier switch would reduce costs.
explanations.E: This is consistent with the cost reduction being beneficial but does not address its cause.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal claim with one obvious alternative explanation. The stimulus argues that a policy caused a specific outcome; the correct answer introduces a straightforward confounding variable that occurred at the same time.
lr.stimulus: After City Council approved a new traffic-reduction initiative in March, traffic congestion in downtown declined by 20% over the following six months. Clearly, the traffic-reduction initiative was responsible for the decrease in congestion.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The traffic-reduction initiative was supported by environmental groups.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A major employer relocated out of downtown in April, significantly reducing the number of commuters in the area.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Traffic congestion typically decreases during the summer months.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Other cities have implemented similar traffic-reduction initiatives with mixed results.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The City Council had previously considered and rejected a traffic-reduction initiative five years earlier.

explanations.correct: B introduces an alternative explanation for the observed decrease in congestion. If a major employer relocated out of downtown in April—shortly after the initiative was approved—that relocation could fully account for the 20% reduction, undermining the claim that the initiative itself was responsible.
explanations.A: Accurate but irrelevant. The source of support for the initiative does not address whether it actually caused the congestion reduction.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Weakens the argument only marginally and does not establish a competing causal explanation. Seasonal variation is a general pattern; it does not show that this specific reduction was caused by something other than the initiative.
explanations.D: Out of scope. The success or failure of similar initiatives in other cities does not speak to whether this initiative caused the downtown reduction.
explanations.E: Irrelevant. A previous rejected proposal has no bearing on whether the March initiative caused the congestion decrease.

lr.difficultyReason: Straightforward causal overreach. A single temporal correlation (two events coincide) is mistaken for causation. The correct answer offers an obvious alternative cause.
lr.stimulus: Dr. Chen observed that patients who took a new herbal supplement reported fewer migraines in the week following their first dose. Therefore, the supplement directly reduces migraine frequency.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously undermines Dr. Chen's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Some patients reported that they felt optimistic about the supplement's efficacy before taking their first dose.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Migraine frequency naturally varies week to week, and many patients experience spontaneous improvement regardless of any treatment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The supplement contains several ingredients that are known to aid digestion.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Other herbal supplements have been shown to reduce migraines in some patients.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Dr. Chen also studied the effects of the supplement on other common ailments such as insomnia and joint pain.

explanations.correct: B provides an alternative explanation for the observed improvement. If migraines naturally fluctuate and patients often experience spontaneous remission, the reported reduction may have nothing to do with the supplement. This directly undermines the causal claim.
explanations.A: Introduces placebo effect, which, though relevant to medical efficacy, is more of a strengthener (shows the supplement works through some mechanism). Does not establish an alternative explanation.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Accurate but irrelevant. The supplement's digestive properties do not address whether it causes migraine reduction.
explanations.D: Out of scope. Other supplements' efficacy does not speak to whether this supplement caused the migraine reduction in Dr. Chen's observation.
explanations.E: Irrelevant. Studying side effects or applications to other conditions does not weaken the claim about migraines.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple predictive or causal argument where a single factor is claimed to drive a result. The correct answer shows that the result can occur without that factor, or that the factor is absent when the result occurs.
lr.stimulus: After the museum installed interactive displays featuring touchscreen technology, visitor attendance increased by 30% within three months. The museum director concluded that the interactive displays were the primary reason for the surge in attendance.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The interactive displays were designed by a team of experienced technology consultants.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A major news outlet ran a feature story about the museum's renovation project one week after the displays were installed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Touchscreen technology has become increasingly affordable for museums in recent years.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Similar museums in other regions have not experienced comparable attendance increases.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The museum's admission price remained unchanged during the three-month period.

explanations.correct: B introduces an alternative explanation for the attendance surge. The major news story could have independently driven the 30% increase. This undercuts the director's attribution of the surge solely to the interactive displays.
explanations.A: Accurate but irrelevant. The credentials of the designers do not address whether the displays caused the attendance increase.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Out of scope. General trends in touchscreen pricing do not explain why attendance rose at this particular museum.
explanations.D: Introduces a comparative that weakens by disanalogy, but does not rule out that the displays caused the increase at this museum.
explanations.E: Irrelevant. Stable pricing does not address what caused the attendance boost.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal claim with one obvious alternative explanation. Stimulus attributes sales increase to local flour; correct answer introduces a clear confounder (new storefront).
lr.stimulus: A regional bakery switched to locally sourced flour last month, and sales increased by 20% over the following month. The bakery owner attributes this sales increase directly to the higher quality of the local flour. The owner plans to expand further use of local ingredients across the entire product line.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Local flour is significantly more expensive than the flour the bakery previously used.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A new shopping center opened two blocks away from the bakery at the exact same time the flour switch occurred.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Several competing bakeries in the region have also recently switched to using local ingredients.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The bakery has maintained the same prices for its products since switching to local flour.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Customer surveys indicate that many people believe locally sourced ingredients are better for the environment.

explanations.correct: The owner concludes that local flour caused the sales increase. However, if a new shopping center opened at the same time, increased foot traffic to the area provides an alternative explanation for the sales spike that has nothing to do with the flour quality. This undermines the causal claim.
explanations.A: Accurate but irrelevant — higher cost does not explain why sales increased. Even if flour is expensive, that does not address whether it drove the sales increase.
explanations.B: Correct. This introduces a competing cause for the observed sales increase, weakening the owner's conclusion.
explanations.C: Competitors' choices are not directly relevant to whether this bakery's flour switch caused its own sales increase.
explanations.D: If prices stayed the same, the sales increase is even more likely attributable to product quality — this strengthens rather than weakens the argument.
explanations.E: This supports the idea that local ingredients are appealing to customers, which actually strengthens the owner's conclusion.

lr.difficultyReason: Simple predictive argument with one obvious counterexample. Stimulus predicts patient recovery based on early intervention; correct answer shows early intervention does not guarantee recovery.
lr.stimulus: A hospital administrator reviewed patient records from the cardiac unit and noted that patients who received intervention within one hour of symptom onset recovered significantly faster than those who received intervention after two hours. The administrator concludes that early intervention in cardiac emergencies will always lead to faster recovery.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously undermines the argument's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Patients who receive late intervention sometimes have less severe underlying cardiac conditions than those treated early.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The hospital has upgraded its cardiac equipment several times over the past decade.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Younger patients tend to recover faster from cardiac emergencies regardless of intervention timing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some patients with severe cardiac damage recover fully even without any medical intervention.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Insurance companies reimburse hospitals more generously for early intervention treatments.

explanations.correct: The administrator assumes that early intervention causes faster recovery. However, if patients treated late already had less severe conditions, their underlying condition — not intervention timing — explains the recovery differences. This shows the causal claim is not as strong as the stimulus suggests, weakening the 'always leads to faster recovery' conclusion.
explanations.A: Correct. This provides an alternative explanation (severity of condition rather than timing of intervention) that weakens the causal conclusion.
explanations.B: Irrelevant — equipment upgrades are not connected to whether early intervention itself causes faster recovery.
explanations.C: Age affects recovery independent of intervention timing, but this does not refute that early intervention leads to faster recovery overall.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — patients recovering without intervention does not address whether intervention timing matters.
explanations.E: Insurance incentives are a financial matter unrelated to the actual medical effects of early intervention.

lr.difficultyReason: Analogical argument with simple disanalogy. Stimulus claims two situations are analogous; correct answer identifies a key difference that undermines the analogy.
lr.stimulus: An economist argues that raising the minimum wage for restaurant workers will produce the same result as it did in the nearby county: increased employment. The nearby county raised its minimum wage 18 months ago, and restaurant employment grew by 8% in the year following the increase. Therefore, our county should expect similar employment growth if it raises minimum wage.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most calls into question the economist's reasoning?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The nearby county is geographically closer to a major metropolitan area than our county is.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Employment in other industries in the nearby county remained relatively stable after the minimum wage increase.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The nearby county's minimum wage increase was slightly larger in percentage terms than the increase being proposed for our county.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Several large restaurant chains expanded into the nearby county in the period immediately before the minimum wage increase took effect.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Workers in the nearby county who received higher minimum wages spent more money on dining out.

explanations.correct: The economist's argument rests on the analogy: nearby county raised minimum wage → employment grew, so our county will experience the same. However, if major restaurant chains expanded into the nearby county *before* the wage increase, the employment growth resulted from expansion, not from the minimum wage policy itself. This disanalogy undermines the comparison and weakens the conclusion.
explanations.A: Geographic proximity to a city is noted but does not directly undermine the causal analogy about minimum wage effects.
explanations.B: Stability in other industries is not relevant to whether minimum wage caused restaurant employment growth.
explanations.C: A difference in percentage increases is a minor detail that does not fundamentally challenge the comparison.
explanations.D: Correct. This identifies a key disanalogy: the nearby county had external expansion that our county may lack, so we cannot assume the same outcome.
explanations.E: Increased spending is consistent with the minimum wage raising employment and prosperity — actually supports the economist's position.

lr.difficultyReason: Single causal claim with one obvious alternative explanation. The stimulus argues that the new packaging caused an increase in sales, but the correct answer introduces a simple confounder (change in retail distribution) that could explain the rise just as well.
lr.stimulus: A marketing director at a consumer goods company noticed that sales of the company's laundry detergent increased by 30 percent in the six months following the introduction of a new, more eco-friendly packaging design. The director concludes that the new packaging design was responsible for the increase in sales.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Many consumers report that they prefer the old packaging design to the new one.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The new packaging design cost 15 percent less to produce than the old packaging design.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The company's primary competitor introduced a nearly identical packaging design two years before the company did.

choices.label: D
choices.text: During the same six-month period, the company doubled its shelf space in supermarkets nationwide, making the detergent far more visible to consumers.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Market research shows that consumers increasingly prefer eco-friendly products.

explanations.correct: D provides an alternative explanation for the 30 percent sales increase. If the company doubled its shelf space during the same period, that retail expansion—not the new packaging—could be the primary driver of the sales increase. This undermines the director's causal claim.
explanations.A: Irrelevant. Consumer preference for the old design would undermine the packaging change as a driver, but the stimulus is about a sales increase, not satisfaction. Many sold products can still come from a less-preferred package.
explanations.B: Irrelevant to the causal claim. Production cost has no bearing on whether the packaging design drove consumer purchases.
explanations.C: Out of scope. The competitor's earlier packaging does not explain why this company's sales rose after its own packaging change, nor does it offer an alternative cause.
explanations.E: Supports the director's conclusion. If consumers prefer eco-friendly products, the eco-friendly packaging becomes a more plausible driver of the sales increase, so this strengthens rather than weakens the argument.
explanations.D: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Two-step causal chain in a medical context: drug lowers cholesterol, and lowered cholesterol reduces cardiac events. Weakener exposes a non-obvious alternative cause operating on the second link. Trap (B) strengthens by ruling out a different confound; trap (E) attacks a premise but not the conclusion.
lr.stimulus: A five-year clinical study found that patients who took the cholesterol-lowering drug lovastin experienced 30 percent fewer cardiac events than patients who took a placebo. Lovastin is known to reduce blood cholesterol, and elevated cholesterol is a well-established risk factor for cardiac events. The study's authors concluded that lovastin's cholesterol-lowering action is what prevented the cardiac events among patients taking the drug.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Lovastin also produces a previously undocumented anti-inflammatory effect in blood vessel walls, and vascular inflammation independently contributes to cardiac events.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Patients in the two groups were matched for age, sex, smoking status, and family history of heart disease.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cardiac events occurred in both groups at roughly the rates researchers had projected before the study began.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lovastin is more expensive than several other cholesterol-lowering drugs currently on the market.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some patients in the lovastin group discontinued the drug before the study concluded.

explanations.correct: The authors attribute the drop in cardiac events specifically to cholesterol reduction. (A) introduces a non-obvious alternative cause — an anti-inflammatory effect that independently prevents cardiac events — so the benefit may have flowed from a mechanism other than cholesterol lowering. The second link in the causal chain is undermined.
explanations.A: Correct.
explanations.B: Strengthens, if anything — matching across known confounders makes the correlation more reliable.
explanations.C: Irrelevant — projection accuracy says nothing about which mechanism produced the outcome.
explanations.D: Out of scope — price has no bearing on whether the drug's effect is due to cholesterol reduction.
explanations.E: Attacks a minor feature of the trial's execution without touching the causal claim about the patients who did take the drug.

lr.difficultyReason: Predictive economic argument extrapolating from one quarter's data. Weakener denies a load-bearing background assumption about seasonality. Trap (C) strengthens; trap (D) is out-of-scope comparative.
lr.stimulus: Analyst: In the first quarter after Morven Motors redesigned its flagship sedan, sales of that model rose by 22 percent over the same quarter last year, while sales of the company's other models were flat. Morven's executives have therefore announced that the redesign will produce sustained sales growth for the sedan throughout the coming year.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most undermines the executives' prediction?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Morven has not redesigned any of its other sedan models in the past five years.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Morven historically offers its largest rebates on the flagship sedan during the first quarter, and this year's rebates were unusually generous.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Automotive reviewers gave the redesigned sedan higher marks than they gave the previous version.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A competitor of Morven's reported flat sales of its comparable sedan this quarter.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Morven spent more on its first-quarter advertising campaign than in any previous first quarter.

explanations.correct: The executives infer sustained growth from a single quarter's increase, assuming the jump reflects the redesign. (B) identifies an alternative cause peculiar to the first quarter — unusually large rebates — that will not be in place during later quarters, so the growth is unlikely to persist.
explanations.A: Irrelevant — what happened with other models doesn't speak to whether this sedan's increase will continue.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Strengthens, if anything — favorable reviews support continued demand.
explanations.D: Out of scope — a competitor's flat sales don't tell us whether Morven's jump will endure.
explanations.E: This is a confound for the first-quarter spike but weakens less than (B); heavy advertising that matches past campaigns could easily be sustained. (B) names a factor the executives cannot continue — the rebate was already described as unusually generous.

lr.difficultyReason: Analogical argument from one municipality to another. Weakener denies the background assumption that the baseline conditions in the two cities are comparable. Trap (D) strengthens via a surface-similarity cue; trap (A) attacks a subsidiary claim.
lr.stimulus: After the city of Dunsbridge installed protected bicycle lanes on its six busiest commercial streets, reported collisions involving cyclists fell by 40 percent within two years. The city council of neighboring Harrow has now approved similar protected lanes on its own busiest streets, confident that Harrow will see a comparable decline in cyclist collisions.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most seriously undermines the council's expectation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dunsbridge's reporting of minor cycling collisions has historically been less thorough than Harrow's.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Harrow's commercial streets carry roughly the same volume of motor-vehicle traffic as Dunsbridge's did before the lanes were installed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Protected bicycle lanes are more expensive to install than painted bicycle lanes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dunsbridge and Harrow have comparable proportions of experienced cyclists among their residents.

choices.label: E
choices.text: In Dunsbridge, the vast majority of cycling collisions before the lanes were installed involved cyclists being struck while turning left across oncoming traffic, a maneuver that remains legal and unaltered in Harrow.

explanations.correct: The council assumes the lanes will address the kinds of collisions Harrow faces. (E) reveals that the pre-lane collisions in Dunsbridge were dominated by a left-turn conflict unaffected by protected lanes. If the same maneuver is unaltered in Harrow, the lanes there should not produce a comparable drop — the claimed benefit depended on a cause the lanes don't actually address.
explanations.A: Attacks a subsidiary point — the reliability of the Dunsbridge count — without touching Harrow's expected outcome.
explanations.B: Strengthens, if anything — matched traffic volume supports the analogy.
explanations.C: Out of scope — cost has no bearing on whether collisions will fall.
explanations.D: Strengthens — comparable rider experience supports the analogy.
explanations.E: Correct.

lr.difficultyReason: Environmental causal argument with an appealing mechanism. Weakener reveals reversed causation: the correlation runs the other direction. Trap (A) is an opposite answer; trap (C) attacks a minor premise.
lr.stimulus: A team of ecologists surveyed 200 streams in a large river basin and found that streams with dense populations of freshwater mussels had, on average, markedly clearer water than streams with sparse mussel populations. Because mussels filter particulates from the water as they feed, the ecologists concluded that the mussels are the primary reason the clear-water streams are clear.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the ecologists' conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In laboratory tanks, individual freshwater mussels can filter several liters of water per hour.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Freshwater mussels cannot survive in streams whose water is already murky from suspended particulates, because their gills become clogged.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some of the ecologists' survey measurements were taken during a week of unusually heavy rainfall.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A different invertebrate present in many of the surveyed streams also filters particulates but on a smaller scale.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Freshwater mussel populations throughout the basin have declined over the past two decades.

explanations.correct: The ecologists infer that mussels cause the clarity. (B) reverses the causal direction: mussels can't live in already-murky water, so clear water is a precondition for dense mussel populations rather than a consequence of them. The correlation is explained in the opposite direction from the one the ecologists proposed.
explanations.A: Opposite answer — confirming filtering capacity strengthens the mussel-causes-clarity claim.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Attacks a subsidiary point about measurement conditions without directly challenging the correlation or its causal interpretation.
explanations.D: Too narrow — a smaller-scale additional filterer doesn't explain away the mussels' contribution.
explanations.E: Out of scope — basin-wide decline over two decades doesn't bear on the cross-sectional comparison among today's streams.

lr.difficultyReason: Technology causal argument with a plausible productivity story. Weakener denies a load-bearing assumption about the comparison baseline — the tasks assigned differed. Trap (E) strengthens; trap (D) is out-of-scope.
lr.stimulus: Journalist: A software firm recently gave half of its junior engineers an AI coding assistant and asked the other half to continue working without one. After six months, engineers with the assistant had closed 35 percent more support tickets than engineers without it. The firm's chief technology officer has therefore concluded that the AI assistant makes junior engineers substantially more productive.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most calls the chief technology officer's conclusion into question?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A minority of the engineers assigned an AI assistant reported that they rarely used it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The engineers given the AI assistant were systematically routed the firm's simpler, more self-contained support tickets, while the other engineers handled tickets requiring extended investigation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: At other firms that have deployed similar AI assistants, senior engineers have reported mixed opinions about their utility.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The AI assistant's annual license fee is substantial.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Independent code reviewers judged the work produced by engineers with the assistant to be of comparable quality to the work of those without it.

explanations.correct: Closed-ticket counts are only a meaningful productivity measure if the two groups handled comparable work. (B) shows the assisted group drew simpler tickets, which would inflate their count regardless of the assistant. The higher ticket-closure rate can be explained by a different, non-obvious cause: task assignment.
explanations.A: Attacks a minor execution detail; even so, most engineers in the group presumably did use the tool, and (A) doesn't explain why that group closed more tickets.
explanations.B: Correct.
explanations.C: Out of scope — senior engineers at other firms are a different population with different work.
explanations.D: Irrelevant — cost has no bearing on whether productivity rose.
explanations.E: Strengthens, if anything — equal quality with higher volume supports a productivity gain.

lr.difficultyReason: Linguistic generalization from a sample. Weakener exposes a sampling flaw — the compared corpora are not contemporaneous. Trap (A) strengthens; trap (C) is out-of-scope.
lr.stimulus: Linguist: A recent computational study compared two corpora of English prose: one drawn from personal letters written between 1850 and 1900, the other from email and text messages written between 2010 and 2020. The study found that the average sentence in the modern corpus was 38 percent shorter than the average sentence in the nineteenth-century corpus. The linguist responsible for the study concluded that English speakers today favor dramatically shorter sentences than their nineteenth-century counterparts did.
lr.questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most weakens the linguist's conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The nineteenth-century corpus and the modern corpus were of roughly equal total word count.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Personal letters of the nineteenth century typically used longer, more elaborated sentences than any other kind of writing produced in that period, while email and text messages today typically use shorter sentences than any other modern written form.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some of the nineteenth-century letters were originally composed in languages other than English and translated.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Most of the modern messages in the study were composed on mobile phones.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The linguist measured sentence length by counting words between punctuation marks.

explanations.correct: The conclusion generalizes to English speakers today versus those of the nineteenth century.
